definition: AquaMaps is a collaborative project with the aim of producing computer-generated (and ultimately, expert reviewed) predicted global distribution maps for [marine species](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marine_biology) on a 0.5 × 0.5 degree [grid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grid_(spatial_index)) of the [ocean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ocean)s based on data available through online species databases such as [FishBase](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FishBase) and [SeaLifeBase](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SeaLifeBase) and species occurrence records from [OBIS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OBIS) or [GBIF](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GBIF) and using an environmental envelope model (see [niche modelling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Niche_modelling)) in conjunction with expert input.

Blastulation is the stage in early [animal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Animal) [embryonic development](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Embryonic_development) that produces the blastula.
Blending inheritance is an [obsolete theory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Superseded_scientific_theories) in [biology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biology) from the 19th century.
Bletting is a process of softening that certain fleshy [fruit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fruit)s undergo, beyond [ripening](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ripening).

Blindsight is the ability of people who are [cortically blind](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cortical_blindness) to respond to visual stimuli that they do not consciously see due to [lesion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lesion)s in the [[Visual cortex#Primary visual cortex (V1)|primary visual cortex]], also known as the [striate cortex](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Visual_cortex) or [Brodmann Area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brodmann_area) 17.

definition: blood gill is a [gill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gill)-like structure restricted to organs with spacious lumen and poorly developed/absent [trachea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trachea), found in larvae of [aquatic insect](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aquatic_insect)s.

Blood pressure (BP) is the [pressure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pressure) of [circulating blood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Circulatory_system) against the walls of [blood vessels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blood_vessels).

Blood shift has at least two separate meanings: * In [medicine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medicine), it is synonymous with [left shift](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Left_shift_(medicine)) * In diving [physiology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Physiology), it is part of the [[Diving reflex#Blood shift|diving reflex]] [[Category:Physiology]] 0lpc91br55ph20nk4xpdf7rg9lzbp3w

blood substitute (also called artificial blood or blood surrogate) is a substance used to mimic and fulfill some functions of [biological](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biology) [blood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blood).

blood type (also known as a blood group) is a classification of [blood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blood) based on the presence and absence of [antibodies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antibody) and [inherited](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heredity) [antigen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigen)ic substances on the surface of [red blood cell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_blood_cell)s (RBCs).
Blood vessels are the tubular structures of a [circulatory system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Circulatory_system) transporting [blood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blood) in animal bodies.

Blood volume (volemia) is the [volume](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volume) of [blood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blood) ([blood cell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blood_cell)s and [plasma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blood_plasma)) in the [circulatory system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Circulatory_system) of any individual.

blood–ocular barrier is a barrier created by endothelium of [capillaries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Capillaries) of the [retina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Retina) and [iris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iris_(anatomy)), [ciliary epithelium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ciliary_body) and [retinal pigment epithelium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Retinal_pigment_epithelium).

blood–retinal barrier, or the BRB, is part of the [blood–ocular barrier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blood–ocular_barrier) that consists of cells that are joined tightly together to prevent certain substances from entering the tissue of the retina.

blood–testis barrier is a physical barrier between the [blood vessel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blood_vessel)s and the [seminiferous tubule](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seminiferous_tubule)s of the animal [testes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Testicle).

blot is a method of transferring large biomolecules ([protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein)s, [DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA) or [RNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RNA)) onto a carrier, such as a [membrane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Membrane) composed of [nitrocellulose](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nitrocellulose), [polyvinylidene fluoride](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polyvinylidene_fluoride) or [nylon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nylon).

blotting matrix, in [molecular biology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Molecular_biology) and [genetics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetics), is the substrate onto which [macromolecules](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Macromolecules), such as [proteins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Proteins), are transferred in a [blot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blot_(biology)) method.
Blue Brain Project was a Swiss brain research initiative that aimed to create a [digital reconstruction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artificial_brain) of the mouse brain.

blue dwarf is a hypothetical class of [star](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Star) that develops from a [red dwarf](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_dwarf) after it has exhausted much of its [hydrogen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hydrogen) fuel supply.
blue ice is frozen sewage material that has leaked mid-flight from commercial aircraft lavatory waste systems.
Blue Ridge dusky salamander (Desmognathus orestes) is a species of [salamander](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salamander) in the family [Plethodontidae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plethodontidae).
blue whale penis is the largest in the animal kingdom.

blue–white screen is a [screening technique](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetic_screen) that allows for the rapid and convenient detection of recombinant bacteria in [vector](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vector_DNA)-based [molecular cloning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Molecular_cloning) experiments.

Blumea - Journal of Plant Taxonomy and Plant Geography (Tijdschrift voor de Systematiek en de Geografie der Planten in Dutch) is a [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer_review) [journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academic_journal) of [botany](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Botany) published by the [National Herbarium of the Netherlands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Herbarium_of_the_Netherlands).

Blyttia () is a quarterly [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer_review) [scientific journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_journal) of [botany](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Botany) published by the [Norwegian Botanical Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Norwegian_Botanical_Association) since 1943.

BMC Bioinformatics is a [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer-reviewed) [open access](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Open_access) [scientific journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_journal) covering [bioinformatics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bioinformatics) and [computational biology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computational_biology) published by [BioMed Central](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BioMed_Central).

BMC Ecology and Evolution (since January 2021), previously BMC Evolutionary Biology (2001–2020), is a [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer-reviewed) [open access](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Open_access) [scientific journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_journal) covering all fields of [evolutionary biology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evolutionary_biology), including [phylogenetics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phylogenetics) and [palaeontology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palaeontology).

BMC Genomics is an [open-access](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Open-access) [scientific](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific) journal covering all areas of [genomics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genomics) and [proteomics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Proteomics).

BMC Molecular and Cell Biology is a [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer-reviewed) [open-access](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Open-access) [scientific journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_journal) that covers the fields of molecular and cell biology, focusing on areas such as [signal transduction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Signal_transduction), [gene expression](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene_expression), and [cellular processes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cellular_processes).

BMC Plant Biology is a [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer-reviewed) [open-access](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Open-access) [scientific journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_journal) that covers the field of plant biology, focusing on areas such as [plant genetics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plant_genetics), [plant physiology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plant_physiology), and plant-environment interactions.

BMC Structural Biology was an [open access](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Open_access_(publishing)) [peer-review](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer-review)ed [scientific journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_journal) that covered research in [structural biology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Structural_biology).

BMC Systems Biology was an [open access](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Open_access_(publishing)) [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer_review) [scientific journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_journal) that covered research in [systems biology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Systems_biology).

BMC Zoology is a [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer-reviewed) [open-access](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Open-access) [scientific journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_journal) that covers the field of zoology, focusing on areas such as [animal behavior](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Animal_behavior), [ecology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ecology), and [evolutionary biology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evolutionary_biology).

Bob Lanese (August 2, 1941 – April 9, 2024) was an American [trumpet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trumpet) player who spent most of his career as a professional musician in [Germany](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany).

cell bank is a facility that stores cells of specific [genome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genome) for the purpose of future use in a product or medicinal needs, but can also describe the entity of stored cells itself.

Cell Biochemistry and Biophysics is a [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer-reviewed) [scientific journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_journal) covering all aspects of the [biology of cells](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_biology), especially their [biochemistry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biochemistry) and [biophysics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biophysics).

Cell biology, cellular biology, or cytology, is the branch of [biology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biology) that studies the [structure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anatomy), [function](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Physiology), and behavior of the [cell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_(biology))s.

Cell Biology International is a [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer_review) [scientific journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_journal) published by [Portland Press](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portland_Press) for the [International Federation for Cell Biology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Federation_for_Cell_Biology).

Cell biophysics (or cellular biophysics) is a sub-field of [biophysics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biophysics) that focuses on physical principles underlying [cell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_(biology)) function.

Cell Calcium is a monthly [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer_review) [scientific journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_journal) published by [Elsevier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elsevier) that covers the field of [cell biology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_biology) and focuses mainly on [calcium signalling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcium_signalling) and [metabolism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metabolism) in living organisms.

Cell CANARY (Cellular Analysis and Notification of Antigen Risks and Yields) is a recent technology that uses genetically engineered [B cells](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/B_cells) to identify [pathogen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pathogen)s.

cell cortex, also known as the actin cortex, cortical cytoskeleton or actomyosin cortex, is a specialized thin layer of cross-linked [actomyosin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Actomyosin)s attached to the [cell membrane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_membrane).

Cell counting is any of various methods for the [counting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Counting) or similar [quantification](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantification_(science)) of [cell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_(biology))s in the [life sciences](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Life_sciences), including [medical diagnosis and treatment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medicine).
Cell culture or tissue culture is the process by which [cells](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_(biology)) are grown under controlled conditions, generally outside of their natural environment.

definition: cell culture assay is any method used to assess the [cytotoxicity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cytotoxicity) of a material.

Cell cycle analysis by DNA content measurement is a method that most frequently employs [flow cytometry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flow_cytometry) to distinguish cells in different phases of the [cell cycle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_cycle).
Cell cycle withdrawal refers to the natural stoppage of [cell cycle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_cycle) during [cell division](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_division).

Cell damage (also known as cell injury) is a variety of changes of stress that a [cell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_(biology)) suffers due to external as well as internal environmental changes.

Cell Discovery is a [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer-reviewed) [open-access](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Open-access) scientific journal covering research in [cell biology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_biology) and [molecular biology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Molecular_biology).
Cell division orientation is the direction along which the new daughter [cell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_(biology))s are formed.

Cell engineering is the purposeful process of adding, deleting, or modifying [genetic sequences](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nucleic_acid_sequence) in living [cells](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_(biology)) to achieve [biological engineering](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biological_engineering) goals such as altering cell production, changing cell growth and proliferation requirements, adding or removing [cell functions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_function), and many more.
Fate determination in [developmental biology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Developmental_biology) is the particular development of a specific [cell type](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_type).

Cell fusion is an important [cellular process](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cellular_process) in which several uninucleate [cell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_(biology))s (cells with a single [nucleus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_nucleus)) combine to form a [multinucleate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multinucleate) cell, known as a [syncytium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syncytium).
Cell junctions Cell adhesion is a vital component of the body.
Cell lineage denotes the developmental history of a tissue or organ from the [fertilized egg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zygote).

cell membrane (also known as the plasma membrane or cytoplasmic membrane, and historically referred to as the plasmalemma) is a [semipermeable](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Semipermeable_membrane) [biological membrane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biological_membrane) that separates and protects the [interior](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cytoplasm) of a [cell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_(biology)) from the [outside environment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Extracellular_space) (the extracellular space).

Cell Metabolism is a monthly [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer-reviewed) [scientific journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_journal) covering [physiology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Physiology), with an emphasis on understanding the molecular basis of how the body self-regulates in the face of change, and how disturbances in these balances can lead to disease.
cell nucleus (; : nuclei) is a [membrane-bound organelle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Membrane-bound_organelle) found in [eukaryotic cell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eukaryotic_cell)s.
Cell physiology is the biological study of the activities that take place in a [cell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_(biology)) to keep it alive.
Cell polarity refers to spatial differences in shape, structure, and function within a [cell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_(biology)).

Cell potency is a [cell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_(biology))'s ability to [differentiate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cellular_differentiation) into other [cell types](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_types).

Cell Research is a monthly [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer-reviewed) [scientific journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_journal) covering [cell biology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_biology).

Cell signaling (cell signalling in [British English](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_English)) is the [biological process](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biological_process) by which a [cell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_(biology)) interacts with itself, with other cells, and with the environment.

Cell Stem Cell is a [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer_review) [scientific journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_journal) published by [Cell Press](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_Press), an imprint of [Elsevier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elsevier).
Cell synchronization is a process by which cells in a culture at different stages of the [cell cycle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_cycle) are brought to the same phase.

Cell Systems is a monthly [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer-reviewed) [scientific journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_journal) covering research in [systems biology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Systems_biology).

cell theory is a [scientific theory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_theory) first formulated in the mid-nineteenth century, that living [organism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organism)s are made up of [cell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_(biology))s, that they are the basic structural/organizational unit of all organisms, and that all cells come from pre-existing cells.

cell wall is a structural layer that surrounds some [[Cell (biology)#Types|cell types]], found immediately outside the [cell membrane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_membrane).
Cell-based models are [mathematical model](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mathematical_model)s that represent biological [cells](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_(biology)) as discrete entities.

Cell-free protein synthesis (CFPS), also known as [in vitro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/In_vitro) [protein synthesis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein_biosynthesis) or in vitro transcription/translation (IVTT), is the production of [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) using [biological](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biology) machinery in a [cell-free system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell-free_system), that is, without the use of living [cells](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_(biology)).

Circulating cell-free RNA or cfRNA refers to freely-circulating [ribonucleic acid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RNA) molecules in various biological fluids such as blood (both [plasma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blood_plasma) and [serum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Serum_(blood))), urine, [cerebrospinal fluid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cerebrospinal_fluid) (CSF), [saliva](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saliva), and [pleural fluid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pleural_fluid).

cell-free system is an [in vitro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/In_vitro) tool widely used to study [biological](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biological) [reactions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chemical_reaction) that happen within [cells](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_(biology)) apart from a full cell system, thus reducing the complex interactions typically found when working in a whole cell.

Cellular immunity, also known as cell-mediated immunity, is an [immune response](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Immune_response) that does not rely on the production of [antibodies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antibodies).

media.file: Killer T cells surround a cancer cell.png

definition: Cell-penetrating peptides (CPPs) are short [peptides](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peptides) that facilitate cellular intake and uptake of molecules ranging from [nanosize](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nanotechnology) particles to small [chemical compound](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chemical_compound)s to large fragments of [DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA).

Cellosaurus is an online [knowledge base](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Knowledge_base) on [cell lines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_lines), which attempts to document all cell lines used in [biomedical research](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biomedical_research).

Cells is a monthly [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer-reviewed) [open-access](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Open-access) [scientific journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_journal) that covers all aspects of [cell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cytology) and [molecular biology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Molecular_biology), and [biophysics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biophysics).
cellular adaptation refers to changes made by a [cell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_(biology)) in response to adverse or varying environmental changes.

Cellular agriculture is the production of [agricultural](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Agriculture) products from cell cultures, using a combination of [biotechnology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biotechnology), [tissue engineering](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tissue_engineering), [molecular biology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Molecular_biology), and [synthetic biology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Synthetic_biology) to create and design new methods for producing proteins, fats, and tissues that would otherwise be derived from traditional agriculture.

Cellular and Molecular Life Sciences is a [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer-reviewed) [scientific journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_journal) covering cellular and molecular [life sciences](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Life_sciences).

Cellular and Molecular Neurobiology is a [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer-reviewed) [scientific journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_journal) covering [neuroscience](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neuroscience), especially at the cellular and subcellular levels.

Cellular components are the complex [biomolecule](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biomolecule)s and [structures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Structural_biology) of which [cells](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_(biology)), and thus living [organism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organism)s, are composed.

Cellular deconvolution (also referred to as [cell type](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_type) composition or cell proportion estimation) refers to computational techniques aiming at estimating the proportions of different cell types in samples collected from a [tissue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tissue_(biology)).

Cellular extensions also known as cytoplasmic protrusions and cytoplasmic processes are those structures that project from different [cells](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_(biology)), in the body, or in other organisms.

Cellular memory modules are a form of [epigenetic inheritance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transgenerational_epigenetic_inheritance) that allow cells to maintain their original identity after a series of [cell divisions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_division) and developmental processes.

Cellular microbiology is a discipline that bridges [microbiology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microbiology) and [cell biology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_biology) to investigate interactions between microorganisms and host cells at the molecular level.

cellular model or virtual cell is a [computational model](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computational_model) of aspects of a [biological cell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biological_cell), for the purposes of [in silico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/In_silico) research.
Cellular neuroscience is a branch of [neuroscience](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neuroscience) concerned with the study of [neuron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neuron)s at a cellular level.
Cellular noise is random variability in quantities arising in [cellular biology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cellular_biology).

Cellular respiration is the process of [oxidizing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oxidation_state) biological fuels using an [inorganic electron acceptor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electron_acceptor), such as [oxygen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oxygen), to drive production of [adenosine triphosphate (ATP)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adenosine_triphosphate), which stores chemical energy in a biologically accessible form.

Cellular Signalling is a [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer_review) [scientific journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_journal) focusing on various aspects of [cell signalling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_signaling).

Cellular waste products are formed as a by-product of [cellular respiration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cellular_respiration), a series of processes and reactions that generate energy for the cell, in the form of [ATP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adenosine_triphosphate).

Cellulite () or gynoid lipodystrophy (GLD) is the [herniation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Herniation) of [subcutaneous fat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Subcutaneous_fat) within fibrous [connective tissue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Connective_tissue) that manifests as skin dimpling and [nodularity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nodule_(medicine)), often on the [pelvic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pelvic) region (specifically the [buttocks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buttocks)), lower limbs, and [abdomen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abdomen).
Cell–cell fusogens are [glycoproteins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glycoproteins) that facilitate the [fusion of cell to cell membranes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_fusion).

Cell–cell interaction refers to the direct interactions between [cell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_(biology)) surfaces that play a crucial role in the [development](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Developmental_biology) and function of [multicellular](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multicellular) organisms.
Cement glands are small organs found in [Acanthocephala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Acanthocephala) that are used to temporarily close the posterior end of the female after copulation.
Cementochronology is a method for assessing age at death and determining season at death.

cementoenamel junction (CEJ) is the location where the [enamel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tooth_enamel), which covers the anatomical [crown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crown_(tooth)) of a [tooth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tooth), and the [cementum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cementum), which covers the anatomical root of a tooth, meet.
cenchrus (plural cenchri) is a specialized anatomical structure in the [insect](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Insect) group known as [sawflies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sawfly).

Census of Antarctic Marine Life (CAML) is a field project of the [Census of Marine Life](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Census_of_Marine_Life) that researches the marine biodiversity of Antarctica, how it is affected by [climate change](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Climate_change), and how this change is altering the ecosystem of the Southern Ocean.

Census of Coral Reefs (CReefs) is a field project of the [Census of Marine Life](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Census_of_Marine_Life) that surveys the [biodiversity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biodiversity) of [coral reef](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coral_reef) ecosystems internationally.

page: Census of Diversity of Abyssal Marine Life
definition: Census of Diversity of Abyssal Marine Life (CeDAMar) is a field project of the [Census of Marine Life](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Census_of_Marine_Life) that studies the species diversity of one of the largest and most inaccessible environments on the planet, the [abyssal plain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abyssal_plain).

Census of Marine Life was a scientific initiative involving a global network of researchers in more than 80 nations, engaged to assess and explain the [diversity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biodiversity), distribution, and abundance of [life in the oceans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marine_life).

Census of Marine Zooplankton is a field project of the [Census of Marine Life](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Census_of_Marine_Life) that has aimed to produce a global assessment of the species diversity, [biomass](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biomass), biogeographic distribution, and genetic diversity of more than 7,000 described species of [zooplankton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zooplankton) that drift the ocean currents throughout their lives.

Centre of Excellence in Molecular Biology (CEMB) is a biological research institute located on the West Bank of the Canal Road [Lahore, Punjab](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lahore,_Punjab), Pakistan.

definition: centimorgan (abbreviated cM) or map unit (m.u.) is a unit for measuring [genetic linkage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetic_linkage).
centisome is a unit of length defined as one percent of the length of a particular [chromosome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chromosome).

Central chemoreceptors are [chemoreceptors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chemoreceptor) beneath the ventral surface of the [medulla oblongata](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medulla_oblongata) which are highly sensitive to [pH](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PH) changes of nearby [cerebrospinal fluid (CSF)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cerebrospinal_fluid).
central [governor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Governor_(device)) is a proposed process in the brain that regulates exercise in regard to a neurally calculated safe exertion by the body.

Central nervous system fatigue, or central fatigue, is a form of [fatigue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fatigue_(medical)) that is associated with changes in the [synaptic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chemical_synapse) concentration of [neurotransmitter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neurotransmitter)s within the [central nervous system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_nervous_system) (CNS; including the [brain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_brain) and [spinal cord](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spinal_cord)) which affects exercise performance and muscle function and cannot be explained by peripheral factors that affect muscle function.

Central place foraging (CPF) theory is an [evolutionary ecology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evolutionary_ecology) model for analyzing how an organism can maximize [foraging](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foraging) rates while traveling through a patch (a discrete resource concentration), but maintains the key distinction of a forager traveling from a home base to a distant foraging location rather than simply passing through an area or travelling at random.

central spindle is a microtubule based structure, which forms in between segregating [chromosomes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chromosomes) during [anaphase](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anaphase) where the two sets of [microtubules](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microtubules), emanating from opposite halves of the [cell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_(biology)), overlap, and become arranged into antiparallel bundles by various microtubule associated proteins (MAPs) and [motor proteins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Motor_proteins).

central tendon of the [diaphragm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thoracic_diaphragm) is a thin but strong [aponeurosis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aponeurosis) situated slightly anterior to [the vault formed by the muscle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Posterior_abdominal_wall), resulting in longer posterior muscle fibers.

definition: Central venous pressure (CVP) is the [blood pressure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blood_pressure) in the [venae cavae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Venae_cavae), near the [right atrium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Right_atrium) of the [heart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heart).

Centrolecithal (Greek kentron = center of a circle, lekithos = yolk) describes the placement of the [yolk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yolk) in the centre of the [cytoplasm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cytoplasm) of [ova](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ovum).

cephalic index or cranial index is a number obtained by taking the maximum width ([biparietal diameter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biparietal_diameter) or BPD, side to side) of the head of an [organism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organism), multiplying it by 100 and then dividing it by their maximum length (occipitofrontal diameter or OFD, front to back).

definition: Cephalization is an evolutionary trend in [bilateria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bilateria)n animals in which, over a sufficient number of generations, [special sense](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Special_sense) organs and nerve [ganglia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ganglion) concentrate towards the front of the body, often producing an enlarged head.

cephalocentric hypothesis, also called cephalocentrism, encephalocentrism or cerebrocentrism, is the doctrine that the [brain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brain) is the seat of the [mind](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mind), [consciousness](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Consciousness), sensation and cognition.

Cephalodiscidae mitochondrial code (translation table 33) is a [genetic code](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetic_code) used by the [mitochondria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mitochondria)l genome of [Cephalodiscidae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cephalodiscidae) ([Pterobranchia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pterobranchia)).
cephalon is the [head](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Head) section of an [arthropod](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthropod).

cephalothorax is the region including cephalon and thorax, marked in yellow.|upright=1.2]] The cephalothorax, also called prosoma in some groups, is a [tagma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tagma_(biology)) of various [arthropod](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthropod)s, comprising the head and the [thorax](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thorax_(arthropod_anatomy)) fused together, as distinct from the [[Abdomen#Arthropoda|abdomen]] behind.

Cerata, singular ceras, are anatomical structures found externally in [nudibranch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nudibranch) [sea slug](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sea_slug)s, especially in aeolid nudibranchs, [marine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marine_animal) [opisthobranch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Opisthobranch) [gastropod](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gastropod) [mollusk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mollusk)s in the [clade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clade) [Aeolidida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aeolidida).

Cerci (: cercus) are paired [appendage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Appendage)s usually on the rear-most segments of many [arthropod](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthropod)s, including [insect](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Insect)s and [symphyla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Symphyla)ns.

Cerebellar abiotrophy (CA), also called cerebellar cortical abiotrophy (CCA), is a [genetic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetics) [neurological](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neurology) disease in animals, best known to affect certain breeds of [horse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horse)s, [dog](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dog)s and [cat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cat)s.
Cerebral autoregulation is a process in mammals that aims to maintain adequate and stable [cerebral blood flow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cerebral_blood_flow).

Cerebral Cortex is a [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer-reviewed) [scientific journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_journal) in the [neuroscience](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neuroscience) area, focusing on the development, organization, plasticity, and function of the [cerebral cortex](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cerebral_cortex), including the [hippocampus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hippocampus).

Cerebral hyperperfusion syndrome, also known as reperfusion syndrome, is a dysregulated state of cerebral blood flow following the restoration of arterial blood flow to the brain, usually following treatment of [carotid artery stenosis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carotid_artery_stenosis).
cerebral organoid describes an artificially grown, [in vitro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/In_vitro), tissue resembling parts of the human [brain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brain).

Cerebral perfusion pressure (CPP) is the net [pressure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pressure) gradient causing [cerebral blood flow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cerebral_blood_flow) to the brain (brain [perfusion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Perfusion)).

Cerebral diplopia or polyopia describes seeing two or more images arranged in ordered rows, columns, or diagonals after [fixation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fixation_(visual)) on a [stimulus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stimulus_(psychology)).

CERNO (Coincident Extreme Ranks in Numerical Observations) is a non-parametric, rank-based statistical test that evaluates the distribution of ranks for a subset of samples that have been labeled (the labels defining the subset).

Chemically induced dimerization (CID) is a biological mechanism in which two proteins bind only in the presence of a certain small molecule, enzyme or other dimerizing agent.

Chemiosmosis is the movement of [ion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ion)s across a [semipermeable membrane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Semipermeable_membrane) through an [integral membrane protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Integral_membrane_protein), down their [electrochemical gradient](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electrochemical_gradient).

chemocline is a type of [cline](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cline_(hydrology)), a layer of fluid with different properties, characterized by a strong, vertical [chemistry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chemistry) gradient within a body of [water](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Water).
Chemogenetics is the process by which [macromolecule](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Macromolecule)s can be engineered to interact with previously unrecognized small molecules.

chemoreceptor, also known as chemosensor, is a specialized [sensory receptor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sensory_neuron) which [transduces](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transduction_(physiology)) a [chemical substance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chemical_substance) ([endogenous](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Endogeny_(biology)) or induced) to generate a biological signal.

Chemosensory [[speciation#Methods of selection|speciation]] ([chemosensory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chemosensory) isolation) is the evolution of a population to become distinct [species](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Species) that is driven by chemical stimuli (i.e., chemical signals, recognition).

chemosynthesis is the biological conversion of one or more carbon-containing molecules (usually [carbon dioxide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carbon_dioxide) or [methane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Methane)) and nutrients into organic matter using the [oxidation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oxidation) of inorganic compounds (e.g., [hydrogen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hydrogen) gas, [hydrogen sulfide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hydrogen_sulfide)) or [ferrous](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferrous) ions as a source of energy, rather than sunlight, as in [photosynthesis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Photosynthesis).

Chemotactic drug-targeting is the science of engineering drug carriers which mimic natural chemotactic behavior and reduces systemic effects in specific environments or specific cells in the human body.

Chemotaxis (from [chemo-](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chemical_substance) + [taxis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taxis)) is the movement of an organism or entity in response to a chemical stimulus.

Chemotaxis assays are experimental tools for the evaluation of the [chemotactic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chemotactic) ability of [prokaryotic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prokaryotic) or [eukaryotic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eukaryotic) cells.

chemotroph is an organism that obtains [energy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Energy) by the [oxidation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Redox) of [electron donor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electron_donor)s in their environments.

Chondroblasts, or [perichondrial](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Perichondrial) cells, is the name given to [mesenchymal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mesenchymal) [progenitor cells](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Progenitor_cells) in situ which, from [endochondral ossification](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Endochondral_ossification), will form [chondrocytes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chondrocytes) in the growing [cartilage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cartilage) [matrix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matrix_(biology)).

chordae tendineae (: chorda tendinea) or tendinous cords, colloquially known as the heart strings, are inelastic cords of [fibrous connective tissue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fibrous_connective_tissue) that connect the [papillary muscle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papillary_muscle)s to the [tricuspid valve](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tricuspid_valve) and the [mitral valve](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bicuspid_valve) in the [heart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heart).
Chordin (from Greek χορδή, string, catgut) is a protein with a prominent role in dorsal–ventral patterning during early embryonic development.

Chordotonal organs are [stretch receptor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stretch_receptor) organs found only in [insect](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Insect)s and [crustacean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crustacean)s.

chorioallantoic membrane (CAM), also known as the chorioallantois, is a highly vascularized [membrane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Membrane) found in the [egg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Egg)s of certain [amniote](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amniote)s like [bird](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bird)s and [reptile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reptile)s.

choriogenesis is the formation of the [chorion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chorion), an outer membrane of the placenta that eventually forms [chorionic villi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chorionic_villi) that allow the transfer of blood and nutrients from mother to fetus.
choriovitelline placenta is a [placenta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Placenta) formed by the [yolk sac](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yolk_sac) and [chorion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chorion).

choroid, also known as the choroidea or choroid coat, is a part of the [uvea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uvea), the [vascular](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blood_vessel) layer of the [eye](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eye).

Clinical physiology is an [academic discipline](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academic_disciplines) within the medical sciences and a clinical [medical specialty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medical_specialty) for [physicians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Physicians) in the health care systems of [Sweden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sweden), Disciplines within clinical physiology field include [audiologists](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Audiology), cardiac physiologists, critical care scientists, gastro-intestinal physiologists, [neurophysiologists](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neurophysiology), [respiratory physiologist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Respiratory_physiologist)s, and sleep physiologists.

clitellum is a thickened [gland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gland)ular and non-segmented section of the body wall near the head in [earthworm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Earthworm)s and [leeches](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leeches) that secretes a [viscid sac](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Viscid_sac) in which eggs are stored.

cloaca ( ), : cloacae ( or ), or vent, is the rear [orifice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Body_orifice) that serves as the only opening for the [digestive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gut_(anatomy)) ([rectum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rectum)), [reproductive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reproductive_system), and [urinary tract](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urination)s (if present) of many [vertebrate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vertebrate) animals.

definition: Clonal interference is a phenomenon in evolutionary biology, related to the [population genetics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Population_genetics) of organisms with significant [linkage disequilibrium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Linkage_disequilibrium), especially [asexually reproducing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asexual_reproduction) organisms.
clone is a group of identical cells that share a common ancestry, meaning they are derived from the same cell.

definition: Cloning is the process of producing individual [organism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organism)s with identical [genome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genome)s, by either natural or artificial means.

cloning vector is a small piece of [DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA) that can be stably maintained in an organism, and into which a foreign DNA fragment can be inserted for [cloning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Molecular_cloning) purposes.
Clonogens are [cells](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_(biology)) that can self-renew and form [colonies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colony_(biology)).

Closed ecological systems or contained ecological systems (CES) are [ecosystems](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ecosystems) that do not rely on matter exchange with any part outside the system in order to help maintain life.
closing capacity (CC) is the volume in the [lung](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lung)s at which its smallest airways, the respiratory bronchioles, collapse.
cloven hoof, cleft hoof, divided hoof, or split hoof is a [hoof](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hoof) split into two toes.
cloven paw is a congenital anomaly (birth defect) that affects some animals such as dogs.
Clovis Vincent (26 September 1879 – 14 November 1947) was a French [neurologist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neurologist) and neurosurgeon.

Clozapine N-oxide (CNO) is a synthetic [drug](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drug) used mainly in [biomedical research](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medical_research) as a [ligand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ligand) to activate [Designer Receptors Exclusively Activated by Designer Drugs (DREADDs)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Receptor_activated_solely_by_a_synthetic_ligand), == References == [[Category:Neuroscience]] [[Category:Pharmacology]] on0f3vit50czj6lyplju2olgjrps0p8
Cluster roots, also known as proteoid roots, are [plant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plant) [root](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Root)s that form clusters of closely spaced short lateral rootlets.
clypeus is one of the [sclerite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sclerite)s that make up the face of an [arthropod](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthropod).
Covariance matrix adaptation evolution strategy (CMA-ES) is a particular kind of strategy for [numerical optimization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Numerical_optimization).

cnemial crest is a crestlike prominence located at the front side of the head of the [tibiotarsus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tibiotarsus) or [tibia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tibia) in the [leg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leg)s of many [mammal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mammal)s and [reptile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reptile)s (including [bird](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bird)s and other [dinosaur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dinosaur)s).

cnidariologist is a [zoologist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zoologist) specializing in [Cnidaria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cnidaria), a group of freshwater and marine aquatic [invertebrates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Invertebrates) that include the [sea anemones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sea_anemones), [corals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corals), [hydroids](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hydroids), and [jellyfish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jellyfish).

cnidocyte (also known as a cnidoblast) is a type of [cell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_(biology)) containing a large secretory [organelle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organelle) called a cnidocyst, that can deliver a sting to other organisms as a way to subdue prey and defend against predators.

cnidosac is an [anatomical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anatomical) feature that is found in the group of [sea slug](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sea_slug)s known as aeolid [nudibranch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nudibranch)s, a clade of [marine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marine_(ocean)) [opisthobranch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Opisthobranch) [gastropod](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gastropod) [mollusc](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mollusk)s.

co-adaptation is the process by which two or more species, genes or [phenotypic trait](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phenotypic_trait)s undergo [adaptation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adaptation) as a pair or group.

coactivator is a type of [transcriptional coregulator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transcription_coregulator) that binds to an [activator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Activator_(genetics)) (a [transcription factor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transcription_factor)) to increase the rate of [transcription](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transcription_(biology)) of a [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene) or set of genes.

Coalescent theory is a [model](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_modelling) of how [allele](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Allele)s sampled from a [population](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Population_(biology)) may have originated from a [common ancestor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Most_recent_common_ancestor).
Coalition for Genetic Fairness (CGF) is a public interest group concerned about genetic discrimination.

Coarse woody debris (CWD) or coarse woody habitat (CWH) refers to fallen dead [tree](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tree)s and the remains of large [branch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Branch)es on the ground in [forest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forest)s .

Coastal Science Campus of the [University of California, Santa Cruz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_California,_Santa_Cruz) consists of five main institutions: UC Santa Cruz's Long Marine Laboratory, UC Santa Cruz's Coastal Biology Building, the [NOAA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Oceanic_and_Atmospheric_Administration) Southwest Fisheries Science Center, the Seymour Marine Discovery Center, and the California Marine Wildlife Veterinary Care and Research Center.

coefficient of coincidence (c.o.c.) is a measure of interference in the formation of [chromosomal crossover](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chromosomal_crossover)s during [meiosis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meiosis).
coefficient of inbreeding (COI) is a number measuring how [inbred](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inbreeding) an individual is.
coefficient of relationship is a measure of the degree of [consanguinity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Consanguinity) (or biological relationship) between two individuals.

coenogamete is a multi-nucleate [gamete](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gamete) (a gamete with more than one [nucleus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nucleus_(cell))).
coenosarc is the living tissue overlying the stony skeletal material of the coral.

coenosteum is the stony skeletal material secreted by the [coenosarc](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coenosarc), the layer of living material lying between the [corallite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corallite)s (the stony cups in which the [polyp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polyp_(zoology))s sit).

Coexistence theory is a framework to understand how competitor traits can maintain [species diversity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Species_diversity) and stave-off [competitive exclusion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Competitive_exclusion) even among [similar species](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guild_(ecology)) living in ecologically similar environments.

definition: Cohorts for Heart and Aging Research in Genomic Epidemiology, abbreviated CHARGE, is a [consortium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Consortium) formed to facilitate meta-analyses of [genome-wide association studies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genome-wide_association_studies) of [aging](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aging) and [cardiovascular](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardiovascular) traits, and the replication of [genotype](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genotype)–[phenotype](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phenotype) associations identified in such studies.

Colavita visual dominance effect refers to the phenomenon in which study participants respond more often to the [visual](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Visual) component of an [audiovisual](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Audiovisual) stimulus, when presented with [bimodal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bimodal) [stimuli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stimulus_(psychology)).

definition: Cold and heat adaptations in humans are a part of the broad adaptability of [Homo sapiens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Homo_sapiens).
Cold hardening is the [physiological](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Physiological) and [biochemical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biochemical) process by which an organism prepares for cold weather.

cold seep (sometimes called a cold vent) is an area of the [ocean floor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ocean_floor) where seepage of fluids rich in [hydrogen sulfide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hydrogen_sulfide), [methane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Methane), and other [hydrocarbon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hydrocarbon)s occurs, often in the form of a [brine pool](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brine_pool).
Cold shock response is a series of [neurogenic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neurogenic) cardio-respiratory responses caused by sudden [[Drowning#Cold-water immersion|immersion in cold water]].

COLD-PCR (co-amplification at lower denaturation temperature PCR) is a modified [polymerase chain reaction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polymerase_chain_reaction) (PCR) protocol that enriches variant [alleles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alleles) from a mixture of wildtype and [mutation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mutation)-containing [DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA).

Cold-stunning, also known as hypothermic stunning, is a [hypothermic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hypothermic) reaction experienced by [marine reptile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marine_reptile)s, especially [sea turtle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sea_turtle)s, after prolonged exposure to cold water.

Collapsin response mediator protein family or CRMP family consists of five intracellular [phosphoproteins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phosphoproteins) ([CRMP-1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CRMP1), [CRMP-2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DPYSL2), [CRMP-3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DPYSL4), [CRMP-4](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DPYSL3), [CRMP-5](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DPYSL5)) of similar molecular size (60–66 kDa) and high (50–70%) [amino acid sequence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amino_acid_sequence) identity.

Collateral ventilation is a back-up system of [alveolar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pulmonary_alveolus) ventilation that can bypass the normal route of airflow when airways are restricted or obstructed.

collecting duct system of the [kidney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kidney) consists of a series of tubules and ducts that physically connect [nephron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nephron)s to a [minor calyx](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minor_calyx) or directly to the [renal pelvis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Renal_pelvis).

collophore is a tube-like structure on the ventral side of the first [abdominal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abdominal) segment of the body of [springtail](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Springtail)s (collembolans).

Colocalization Benchmark Source (CBS) is a free collection of downloadable images for testing and validating the degree of [colocalization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colocalization) of markers in any [fluorescence microscopy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fluorescence_microscopy) study.

Combined Annotation Dependent Depletion (CADD) is a tool that evaluates the deleteriousness of [single nucleotide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Single-nucleotide_polymorphism), [insertion and deletion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indel) variants in the human [genome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genome).

Combined Bisulfite Restriction Analysis (or COBRA) is a [molecular biology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Molecular_biology) technique that allows for the sensitive quantification of [DNA methylation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA_methylation) levels at a specific genomic locus on a [DNA sequence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA_sequence) in a small sample of genomic DNA.

Combined DNA Index System (CODIS) is the [United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States) [national DNA database](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_DNA_database) created and maintained by the [Federal Bureau of Investigation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_Bureau_of_Investigation).

Comboios Biological Reserve () is a [biological reserve](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biological_reserve_(Brazil)) in the state of [Espírito Santo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Espírito_Santo), Brazil.

COMBREX is a multifaceted project that includes a database of gene annotations, [functional predictions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Functional_genomics) and recommendations based on [Active Learning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Active_learning_(machine_learning)) principles associated with millions of genes in [prokaryotic genomes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prokaryote).

single cell gel electrophoresis assay (SCGE, also known as comet assay) is an uncomplicated and sensitive technique for the detection of [DNA damage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA_damage) at the level of the individual [eukaryotic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eukaryotic) [cell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_(biology)).

Commensalism is a long-term [biological interaction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biological_interaction) ([symbiosis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Symbiosis)) in which members of one [species](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Species) gain benefits while those of the other species neither benefit nor are harmed.
commissure () is the location at which two objects [[wikt:abut#Verb|abut]] or are joined.
Committee on Mathematical Biology was a research and PhD-training unit at the [University of Chicago](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Chicago), active from 1947 to 1965.

commodification of nature is an area of research within critical environmental studies that is concerned with the ways in which natural entities and processes are made exchangeable through the [market](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Market_economy), and the implications thereof.
Common coding theory is a [cognitive psychology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cognitive_psychology) theory describing how perceptual representations (e.g.
Common descent is a concept in [evolutionary biology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evolutionary_biology) applicable when one species is the ancestor of two or more species later in time.

Common envelope jets supernova (CEJSN) is a type of [supernova](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supernova), where the explosion is caused by the merger of a [giant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giant_star) or [supergiant star](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supergiant) with a compact star such as a [neutron star](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neutron_star) or a [black hole](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_hole).

common extensor tendon is a [tendon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tendon) that attaches to the [lateral epicondyle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lateral_epicondyle_of_the_humerus) of the [humerus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Humerus).
common iliac veins are formed by the [external iliac vein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/External_iliac_vein)s and [internal iliac vein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Internal_iliac_vein)s.
northern raven, is a large, all-black [passerine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Passerine) bird.
Common species and uncommon species are designations used in [ecology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ecology) to describe the population status of a species.

common symbiosis signaling pathway (CSSP) is a highly conserved ==See also== * [Receptor tyrosine kinase](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Receptor_tyrosine_kinase) * [Serine threonine kinase](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Serine/threonine-specific_protein_kinase) * [Pattern recognition receptor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pattern_recognition_receptor)s * [Monoglyceride](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monoglyceride) * [Strigolactone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Strigolactone) * [Plant intelligence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plant_cognition) * [Cell signalling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_signaling) * [Signal transduction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Signal_transduction) * [[Pathogen-associated molec

Communal roosting is an animal behavior where a group of individuals, typically of the same [species](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Species), congregate in an area for a few hours based on an external signal and will return to the same site with the reappearance of the signal.

Communications Biology is a [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer-reviewed) [open access](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Open_access) [scientific journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_journal) covering research in [biology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biology).

community is a group or [association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Association_(ecology)) of [population](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Population_ecology)s of multiple [species](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Species) occupying the same geographical area at the same time, also known as a [biocoenosis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biocoenosis), biotic community, biological community, ecological community, or life assemblage.

term: Community Cyberinfrastructure for Advanced Microbial Ecology Research and Analysis
page: Community Cyberinfrastructure for Advanced Microbial Ecology Research and Analysis
definition: CAMERA, or the Community Cyberinfrastructure for Advanced Microbial Ecology Research and Analysis, is an online [cloud computing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cloud_computing) service that provides [hosted software tools](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Software_as_a_service) and a [high-performance computing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/High-performance_computing) infrastructure for the analysis of [metagenomic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metagenomic) data.

Community fingerprinting is a set of [molecular biology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Molecular_biology) techniques that can be used to quickly profile the [diversity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biodiversity) of a [microbial](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microorganism) community.

Community genetics is a recently emerged field in biology that fuses elements of [community ecology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Community_ecology), [evolutionary biology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evolutionary_biology), and [molecular](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Molecular_genetics) and [quantitative genetics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantitative_genetics).

media.file: Solidago and Narrowleaf cottonwood, taken by Jamie Lamit, Uploaded Oct7, 2013.jpg

definition: Community Greens, sometimes referred to as backyard commons, urban [common](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Common_lands)s, or [pocket neighborhood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pocket_neighborhood)s, are shared open green spaces on the inside of city blocks, created either when residents merge backyard space or reclaim underutilized urban land such as vacant lots and [alley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alley)ways.

community matrix is the [linearization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Linearization) of a [generalized Lotka–Volterra equation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generalized_Lotka–Volterra_equation) at an [equilibrium point](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Equilibrium_point).

Community respiration (CR) refers to the total amount of [carbon-dioxide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CO2) that is produced by individuals [organisms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organisms) in a given [community](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Community), originating from the [cellular respiration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cellular_respiration) of [organic material](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organic_material).

Comparative Biochemistry and Physiology is a series of three journals published by [Elsevier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elsevier) with coverage of three aspects of [biochemistry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biochemistry) and [physiology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Physiology).

Comparative Biochemistry and Physiology Part A: Molecular Integrative Physiology is a [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer_review) [scientific journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_journal) that covers research in [biochemistry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biochemistry) and [physiology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Physiology).

Comparative Biochemistry and Physiology Part B: Biochemistry Molecular Biology is a [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer_review) [scientific journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_journal) that covers research in [biochemistry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biochemistry), [physiology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Physiology), and [molecular biology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Molecular_biology).

Comparative Biochemistry and Physiology Part C: Toxicology Pharmacology is a [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer_review) [scientific journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_journal) that covers research in [biochemistry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biochemistry) and [physiology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Physiology).

Comparative Biochemistry and Physiology Part D: Genomics and Proteomics is a [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer_review) [scientific journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_journal) that covers research in [biochemistry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biochemistry) and [physiology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Physiology).

Comparative biology is the study of patterns and natural [variation in life](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biodiversity) at all levels, from genes to [communities](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Community_(ecology)).

media.file: Heads of Scelidopetalon biwenxuani and Amblyopus vittatus - ZooKeys-317-081-g001.jpeg

definition: Comparative cognition is the comparative study of the mechanisms and origins of [cognition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cognition) in various [species](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Species), and is sometimes seen as more general than, or similar to, [comparative psychology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comparative_psychology).

Comparative Cytogenetics is a [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer-reviewed) [open access](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Open_access) [scientific journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_journal) covering plant and animal [cytogenetics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cytogenetics), [karyosystematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karyotype), and [molecular systematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Molecular_systematics).

Comparative embryology is the branch of [embryology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Embryology) that compares and contrasts [embryo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Embryo)s of different species, showing how organisms are interrelated and share [common ancestry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Common_ancestry).

media.file: Comparative view of the human and elephant frame, Benjamin Waterhouse Hawkins, 1860.jpg

definition: Comparative genomic hybridization (CGH) is a molecular [cytogenetic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cytogenetic) method for analysing [copy number variations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copy_number_variations) (CNVs) relative to [ploidy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ploidy) level in the [DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA) of a test sample compared to a reference sample, without the need for culturing cells.

media.file: A genome alignment of eight Yersinia isolates.png

definition: Comparative medicine is a distinct discipline of [experimental medicine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Experimental_medicine) that uses [animal models](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Model_organism) of human and animal disease in [translational](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Translational_research) and [biomedical research](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biomedical_research).
Comparative neuropsychology refers to an approach used for understanding human [brain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brain) functions.

Comparative physiology is a [subdiscipline](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_academic_disciplines) of [physiology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Physiology) that studies and exploits the diversity of functional characteristics of various kinds of [organisms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organisms).

Comparative psychology is the [scientific](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific) study of the [behavior](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Behavior) and [mental process](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mental_process)es of non-[human](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human) [animal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Animal)s, especially as these relate to the [phylogenetic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phylogenetic) history, [adaptive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adaptation) significance, and development of behavior.
compartment is a part of a [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) that serves a specific function.

Compartmentalization of decay in trees (CODIT) is a model developed by plant pathologist [Alex Shigo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alex_Shigo) after studying [wood-decay fungus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wood-decay_fungus) patterns.

Compartmentalized ciliogenesis is the most common type of [ciliogenesis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ciliogenesis) where the [cilium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cilium) [axoneme](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Axoneme) is formed separated from the cytoplasm by the ciliary membrane and a ciliary gate known as the transition zone.
Compensatory growth is a type of regenerative growth that can take place in a number of human organs after the organs are either damaged, removed, or cease to function.

Compensatory growth, known as catch-up growth and compensatory gain, is an accelerated growth of an organism following a period of slowed development, particularly as a result of [nutrient](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nutrient) deprivation.
Competence stimulating peptides (CSP) are chemical messengers that assist the initiation of [quorum sensing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quorum_sensing), and exist in many bacterial genera.

Competition is an [interaction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biological_interaction) between [organism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organism)s or [species](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Species) in which both require one or more [resources](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Resource_(biological)) that are in [limited](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Limiting_factor) supply (such as [food](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Food), [water](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Water), or [territory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Territory_(animal))).
Competition-ChIP is variant of the [Chip-Sequencing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chip-Sequencing) protocol, used to measure relative binding dynamics of a transcription factor (TF) on DNA.
Competitive altruism is a possible mechanism for the persistence of [cooperative behaviours](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cooperation), specifically those that are performed unconditionally.
competitive Lotka–Volterra equations are a simple model of the [population dynamics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Population_dynamics) of species competing for some common resource.

compilospecies is a genetically aggressive species which acquires the heredities of a closely related [sympatric](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sympatry) species by means of [hybridisation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybridisation_(biology)) and comprehensive [introgression](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Introgression).

Complex Enrichment Analysis Tool is an online [bioinformatics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bioinformatics) tool used to analyze high-throughput datasets (or small-scale datasets) using protein complex enrichment analysis.

C5a is a protein fragment released from cleavage of [complement component C5](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Complement_component_5) by protease [C5-convertase](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C5-convertase) into C5a and C5b fragments.
complementarity describes a relationship between two structures each following the lock-and-key principle.

Complementary cells are a mass of [cell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_(biology))s in plants, formed from the [cork cambium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cork_cambium) at the position of the [lenticel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lenticel)s.
Complementation refers to the capacity of a segment of genetic material (eg DNA) to rescue the phenotype of a mutation.
complete mixing refers to a modeling assumption where each individual in a population has an equal probability of interacting with any other individual.

oil bodies of [liverwort](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liverwort)s, occasionally dubbed complex oil bodies for distinction, are unique [organelle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organelle)s exclusive to the [Marchantiophyta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marchantiophyta).

Complex segregation analysis (CSA) is a technique within [genetic epidemiology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetic_epidemiology) to determine whether there is evidence that a major [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene) underlies the distribution of a given [phenotypic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phenotypic) trait.

Complex traits, also known as [polygenic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polygenic_traits) or [multigenic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multigenic_trait) traits, are [phenotypes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phenotypes) determined by the [interaction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene–environment_interaction) of multiple genetic and environmental factors.
Complex vertebral malformation or CVM is a lethal hereditary syndrome found in [Holstein cattle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Holstein_cattle).

Compliance is the ability of a hollow organ (vessel) to distend and increase volume with increasing transmural pressure or the tendency of a hollow organ to resist recoil toward its original dimensions on application of a distending or compressing force.

composite cross population (CCP) is created by crossing a number of plants from different lines, and subsequently bulking [seed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seed)s from the resulting [offspring](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Offspring).
