definition: compositional domain in [genetics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetics) is a region of [DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA) with a distinct [guanine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guanine) (G) and [cytosine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cytosine) (C) G-C and C-G content (collectively [GC content](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GC_content)).

compound eye is a [visual organ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eye) found in [arthropod](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthropod)s such as [insect](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Insect)s and [crustacean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crustacean)s.

Comprehensive Antibiotic Resistance Database (CARD) is a [biological database](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biological_database) that collects and organizes reference information on [antimicrobial resistance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antimicrobial_resistance) genes, proteins and phenotypes.
Computational anatomy is an interdisciplinary field of [biology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biology) focused on quantitative investigation and modelling of anatomical shapes variability.

Computational and Structural Biotechnology Journal is a [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer-reviewed) [open-access](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Open-access) [scientific journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_journal), published as part of the Science Partner Journal (SPJ) program of the [American Association for the Advancement of Science](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Association_for_the_Advancement_of_Science).

Computational and Systems Neuroscience (COSYNE ) is an annual [scientific conference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_conference) for the exchange of experimental and theoretical/computational approaches to problems in [systems neuroscience](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Systems_neuroscience).

Computational biology refers to the use of techniques in [computer science](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computer_science), [data analysis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Data_analysis), [mathematical modeling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mathematical_modeling) and [computational simulations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computer_simulation) to understand [biological system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biological_system)s and relationships.

Computational neuroscience (also known as theoretical neuroscience or mathematical neuroscience) is a branch of x=y Frontiers in Neuroinformatics] ===Conferences=== * [Computational and Systems Neuroscience](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computational_and_Systems_Neuroscience) (COSYNE) – a computational neuroscience meeting with a systems neuroscience focus.

page: Computer Atlas of Surface Topography of Proteins

definition: Computers in Biology and Medicine is a monthly [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer-reviewed) [scientific journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_journal) established in 1970.

Comstock–Needham system is a naming system for insect [wing vein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wing_vein)s, devised by [John Comstock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Henry_Comstock) and [George Needham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_George_Needham) in 1898.
Conceptacles are specialized cavities of marine and freshwater [algae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Algae) that contain the reproductive organs.

Concerted evolution is the phenomenon where [paralogous](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paralogous) genes within one [species](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Species) are more closely related to one another than to members of the same [gene family](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene_family) in closely related species.

definition: concordance is the [probability](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Probability) that a pair of individuals will both have a certain characteristic ([phenotypic trait](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phenotypic_trait)) given that one of the pair has the characteristic.

condition index in fish is a way to measure the overall health of a [fish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fish) by comparing its weight with the typical weight of other fish of the same kind and of the same length.

conditioned avoidance response (CAR) test, also known as the active avoidance test, is an [animal test](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Animal_model) used to identify [drug](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drug)s with [antipsychotic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antipsychotic)-like effects by checking if they limit the animals' will.
condyle of humerus is the distal end of the [humerus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Humerus).

Condylostoma nuclear code (translation table 28) is a [genetic code](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetic_code) used by the [nuclear genome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nuclear_genome) of the [heterotrich](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heterotrich) [ciliate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ciliate) [Condylostoma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Condylostoma) magnum.

Cone cells or cones are [photoreceptor cells](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Photoreceptor_cells) in the [retina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Retina) of the vertebrate [eye](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eye).

term: Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems
page: Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems
definition: Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (abbreviated as NeurIPS and formerly NIPS) is a [machine learning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Machine_learning) and [computational neuroscience](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computational_neuroscience) [conference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academic_conference) held annually in December.

media.file: Logo for Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems.svg

definition: conformational dynamics data bank (CDDB) is a [database](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Database) about [conformational dynamics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conformational_change) of [heavy proteins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Immunoglobulin_heavy_chain) and [protein assemblies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein_complex).

definition: Conformational proofreading or conformational selection is a general mechanism of [molecular recognition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Molecular_recognition) systems, suggested by Yonatan Savir and Tsvi Tlusty, in which introducing an [energetic barrier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Activation_energy) - such as a structural mismatch between a molecular recognizer and its target - enhances the recognition specificity and quality.

Conidial anastomosis tubes (CATs) are cells formed from the [conidia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conidia) (a type of fungal asexual spores) of many filamentous [fungi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fungi).
Conidiomata (singular: Conidioma) are blister-like fruiting structures produced by a specific type of fungus called a [coelomycete](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coelomycete).

media.file: Chain of conidia of an Alternaria sp. fungus PHIL 3963 lores.jpg

definition: Conjugate eye movement refers to motor coordination of the eyes that allows for bilateral fixation on a single object.

conjunctiva (: conjunctivae) is a thin [mucous membrane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mucous_membrane) that lines the inside of the [eyelid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eyelid)s and covers the [sclera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sclera) (the white of the eye).

Connation in [plant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plant)s is the developmental fusion of organs of the same type, for example, [petal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Petal)s to one another to form a tubular [corolla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corolla_(flower)).

Connectionism is an approach to the study of human mental processes and cognition that utilizes mathematical models known as connectionist networks or [artificial neural network](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artificial_neural_network)s.

connective tissue neoplasm or connective tissue tumor is a [neoplasm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neoplasm) arising from the tissues of the [connective tissue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Connective_tissue).

definition: Connectomics is the production and study of [connectomes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Connectomes), which are comprehensive maps of [connections](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biological_neural_network) within an [organism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organism)'s [nervous system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nervous_system).

connexon, also known as a connexin hemichannel, is an assembly of six proteins called [connexin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Connexin)s that form the pore for a [gap junction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gap_junction) between the [cytoplasm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cytoplasm) of two adjacent [cells](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_(biology)).

term: Conquest of the Khanate of Sibir
page: Conquest of the Khanate of Sibir

definition: Conquiliologistas do Brasil ([Portuguese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portuguese_language): [Conchologists](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conchology) of [Brazil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brazil)) is an association created on September 19, 1989, in [São Paulo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/São_Paulo), [Brazil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brazil), with the main goal of spreading and increasing [conchology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conchology), the study of [mollusc shell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mollusc_shell)s.
Consanguine marriage is marriage between individuals who are closely related.

conscious evolution refers to the theoretical ability of human beings to become conscious participants in the evolution of their [culture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_culture)s, or even of the entirety of [human society](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_society), based on a relatively recent combination of factors, including increasing awareness of cultural and [social pattern](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Social_pattern_(disambiguation))s, reaction against perceived problems with existing patterns, injustices, inequities, and other factors.
Consciousness is being aware of something internal to one's self, or of states or objects in one's external environment.
consensus site is a term in molecular biology that refers to a site on a [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) that is often modified in a particular way.

Conservación Patagónica was a conservation group with a mission *Ecosystem Restoration: [Patagonia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patagonia) has suffered its share of ecological abuse: intensive sheep ranching on sandy, arid soils has resulted in widespread [desertification](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Desertification).

Conservation biology is the study of the conservation of nature and of [Earth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Earth)'s [biodiversity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biodiversity) with the aim of protecting [species](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Species), their [habitat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Habitat)s, and [ecosystem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ecosystem)s from excessive rates of [extinction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Extinction) and the erosion of biotic interactions.

definition: Conservation Biology is a bimonthly [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer_review) [scientific journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_journal) of the [Society for Conservation Biology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Society_for_Conservation_Biology), published by [Wiley-Blackwell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wiley-Blackwell) and established in May 1987.

Conservation genetics is an [interdisciplinary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interdisciplinary) subfield of [population genetics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Population_genetics) that aims to understand the dynamics of [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene)s in a population for the purpose of [natural resource management](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Natural_resource_management), conservation of [genetic diversity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetic_diversity), and the prevention of species [extinction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Extinction).

Conservation Genetics is a bimonthly [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer-reviewed) [scientific](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific) journal covering all areas of [conservation genetics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conservation_genetics).

Conservation Genetics Resources is a quarterly [peer-reviewed scientific journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer-reviewed_scientific_journal) covering methodological improvements, computer programs, and the development of [genomic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genomic) resources related to [conservation genetics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conservation_genetics).
Conservation Genomics is the use of [genomic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genomics) study to aide in the preservation and viability of different and diverse organisms and populations.

Conservation Letters is a bimonthly [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer-reviewed) [open access](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Open_access) [scientific journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_journal) of the [Society for Conservation Biology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Society_for_Conservation_Biology) published by [Wiley-Blackwell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wiley-Blackwell).

Conservation paleobiology is a field of [paleontology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paleontology) that applies the knowledge of the geological and paleoecological record to the [conservation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conservation_biology) and restoration of [biodiversity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biodiversity) and [ecosystem services](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ecosystem_services).

Conservation Physiology is an online only, fully open access journal published by [Oxford University Press](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oxford_University_Press) on behalf of the [Society for Experimental Biology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Society_for_Experimental_Biology).

Conservation psychology is the scientific study of the reciprocal relationships between [human](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human)s and the rest of [nature](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nature), with a particular focus on how to encourage [conservation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conservation_movement) of the [natural world](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Natural_environment).

conservation status of a [group of organisms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taxon) (for example, a [species](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Species)) indicates whether the group still exists and how likely it is to become [extinct](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Extinction) in [the near future](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Extinction_debt).
Conservation-induced extinction is where efforts to save [endangered species](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Endangered_species) lead to the extinction of other species.

Conservation-reliant species are animal or plant [species](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Species) that require continuing species-specific [wildlife management](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wildlife_management) intervention such as [[Hunting#Wildlife management|predator control]], [habitat management](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Habitat_conservation) and [parasite control](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pest_control) to survive, even when a self-sustainable recovery in population is achieved.

Constitutional delay of growth and puberty (CDGP) is a term describing a temporary delay in the skeletal growth and thus height of a child with no physical abnormalities causing the delay.
Constitutive ablation refers to [gene expression](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene_expression) which results in [cell death](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_death).

Construction costs is a concept in biology that conveys how much [glucose](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glucose) is required to construct a unit of plant biomass, given the biosynthetic pathways and starting from glucose and mineral constituents.

constructive development refers to the hypothesis that organisms shape their own developmental trajectory by constantly responding to, and causing, changes in both their internal state and their external environment.

consumer in a [food chain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Food_chain) is a living creature that eats organisms from a different population.

contest competition refers to a situation where available resources, such as food and mates, are utilized only by one or a few individuals, thus preventing development or reproduction of other individuals.

contig (from contiguous) is a set of overlapping [DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA) segments that together represent a [consensus region of DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Consensus_sequence).

continental divide is a [drainage divide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drainage_divide) on a [continent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Continent) such that the [drainage basin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drainage_basin) on one side of the divide feeds into one [ocean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ocean) or [sea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sea), and the basin on the other side either feeds into a different ocean or sea, or else is [endorheic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Endorheic_basin), not connected to the open sea.
continental shelf is a portion of a [continent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Continent) that is submerged under an area of relatively shallow water, known as a shelf sea.

contingency describes how the outcome of evolution may be affected by the history of a particular lineage.

Cross-resistance is when something develops resistance to several substances that have a similar [mechanism of action](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mechanism_of_action).

crossover value is the linked frequency of [chromosomal crossover](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chromosomal_crossover) between two [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene) loci ([markers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetic_marker)).

cursorial organism is one that is adapted specifically to [run](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Running).

cushion plant is a compact, low-growing, mat-forming [plant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plant) that is found in [alpine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alpine_climate), [subalpine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Subalpine), [arctic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arctic_climate), or [subarctic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Subarctic_climate) environments around the world.
cut of meat is part of an animal carcass sold for [meat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meat).

cuticle (), or cuticula, is any of a variety of tough but flexible, non-mineral outer coverings of an organism, or parts of an organism, that provide protection.

DNA base flipping, or nucleotide flipping, is a mechanism in which a single [nucleotide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nucleotide) base, or [nucleobase](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nucleobase), is rotated outside the nucleic acid double helix.

DNA computing is an emerging branch of [unconventional computing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unconventional_computing) which uses [DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA), [biochemistry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biochemistry), and [molecular biology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Molecular_biology) hardware, instead of the traditional [electronic computing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic_computing).

DNA condensation refers to the process of compacting [DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA) molecules [in vitro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/In_vitro) or [in vivo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/In_vivo).

Natural DNA damage is an alteration in the chemical structure of [DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA), such as a break in a strand of DNA, a [nucleobase](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nucleobase) missing from the backbone of DNA, or a chemically changed base such as [8-OHdG](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/8-Oxo-2'-deoxyguanosine).

DNA damage theory of aging proposes that [aging](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aging) is a consequence of unrepaired accumulation of [naturally occurring DNA damage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA_damage_(naturally_occurring)).

DNA database or DNA databank is a [database](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Database) of [DNA profile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA_profiling)s which can be used in the analysis of [genetic disease](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetic_disease)s, [genetic fingerprinting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetic_fingerprinting) for [criminology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Criminology), or [genetic genealogy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetic_genealogy).

DNA encryption is the process of hiding or perplexing genetic information by a [computation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computation)al method in order to improve [genetic privacy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetic_privacy) in [DNA sequencing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA_sequencing) processes.
DNA fragmentation is the separation or breaking of [DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA) strands into pieces.

DNA laddering is a feature that can be observed when DNA fragments resulting from [apoptotic DNA fragmentation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apoptotic_DNA_fragmentation) are visualized after separation by gel electrophoresis, first described in 1980 by [Andrew Wyllie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_Wyllie_(pathologist)) at the [University of Edinburgh Medical School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Edinburgh_Medical_School).

DNA ligase is a type of enzyme that facilitates the joining of [DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA) strands together by catalyzing the formation of a [phosphodiester bond](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phosphodiester_bond).
DNA machine is a [molecular machine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Molecular_machine) constructed from [DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA).

DNA microarray (also commonly known as a DNA chip or [biochip](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biochip)) is a collection of microscopic [DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA) spots attached to a solid surface.

DNA paternity testing uses [DNA profiles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA_profiling) to determine whether an individual is the [biological](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biology) parent of another individual.

DNA phenotyping is the process of predicting an organism's [phenotype](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phenotype) using only genetic information collected from [genotyping](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genotyping) or [DNA sequencing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA_sequencing).

DNA profiling (also called DNA fingerprinting and genetic fingerprinting) is the process of determining an individual's deoxyribonucleic acid ([DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA)) characteristics.

re-replication (or simply rereplication) is an undesirable and possibly fatal occurrence in [eukaryotic cells](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eukaryote) in which the genome is replicated more than once per [cell cycle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_cycle).

definition: DNA repair is a collection of processes by which a [cell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_(biology)) identifies and corrects damage to the [DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA) molecules that encode its [genome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genome).

DNA replication is the [process](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biological_process) by which a [cell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_(biology)) makes exact copies of its [DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA).
DNA replication stress refers to the state of a cell whose [genome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genome) is exposed to various stresses.

definition: DNA separation by silica adsorption is a method of DNA separation that is based on DNA molecules binding to [silica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Silica) surfaces in the presence of certain salts and under certain [pH](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PH) conditions.
DNA sequencer is a [scientific instrument](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_instrument) used to automate the [DNA sequencing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA_sequencing) process.

DNA sequencing is the process of determining the [nucleic acid sequence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nucleic_acid_sequence) – the order of [nucleotides](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nucleotides) in [DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA).

DNA sequencing theory is the broad body of work that attempts to lay analytical foundations for determining the order of specific [nucleotide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nucleotide)s in a sequence of [DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA), otherwise known as [DNA sequencing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA_sequencing).

DNA Specimen Provenance Assignment (DSPA) also known as DNA Specimen Provenance Assay, is a molecular diagnostic test used to definitively assign [biopsy specimen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biopsy) identity and establish specimen purity during the diagnostic testing cycle for [cancer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cancer) and other [histopathological](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Histopathology) conditions.
DNA supercoiling refers to the amount of twist in a particular [DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA) strand, which determines the amount of strain on it.

DNA-binding domain (DBD) is an independently folded [protein domain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein_domain) that contains at least one [structural motif](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Structural_motif) that recognizes double- or single-stranded [DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA).

DNA-directed RNA interference (ddRNAi) is a [gene-silencing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene_silencing) technique that utilizes [DNA construct](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA_construct)s to activate a cell's [endogenous](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Endogeny_(biology)) [RNA interference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RNA_interference) (RNAi) pathways.

DNA-encoded chemical libraries (DECL) is a technology for the [synthesis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chemical_synthesis) and [screening](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/High-throughput_screening) on an unprecedented scale of collections of [small molecule](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Small_molecule) compounds.

DNA‐templated organic synthesis (DTS) is a way to control the [reactivity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reactivity_(chemistry)) of synthetic molecules by using nature's [molarity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Molarity)‐based approach.

Transcription factor: Using the [ChIP-Seq](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ChIP-sequencing) technique, the binding sites to DNA in certain transcription factor groups are determined, and the DHS profiles are compared.

DNase-seq ([DNase I hypersensitive site](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNase_I_hypersensitive_site)s sequencing) is a method in [molecular biology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Molecular_biology) used to identify the location of regulatory regions, based on the genome-wide sequencing of regions sensitive to cleavage by [DNase I](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNase_I).

DNA–DNA hybridization is a [molecular biology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Molecular_biology) technique that measures the degree of [genetic similarity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetic_similarity) between [DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA) sequences.

Do-it-yourself biology (DIY biology, DIY bio) is a [biotechnological](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biotechnology) [social movement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Social_movement) in which individuals, communities, and small organizations study biology and [life science](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_life_sciences) using the same methods as traditional research institutions.

definition: Evolutionary developmental psychology (EDP) is a research paradigm that applies the basic principles of [evolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evolution) by [natural selection](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Natural_selection), to understand the development of human behavior and cognition.

Evolutionary dynamics is a branch of mathematical evolutionary biology that developed from research using [differential equations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Differential_equations) to model both [genetic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetics) and [phenotypic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phenotype) change.
Evolutionary ecology is a science at the intersection of [ecology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ecology) and [evolutionary biology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evolutionary_biology).
Evolutionary economics is a school of [economic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Economics) thought that is inspired by [evolutionary biology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evolutionary_biology).

Evolutionary epistemology refers to three distinct topics: (1) the biological evolution of [cognitive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cognition) mechanisms in animals and humans, (2) a theory that knowledge itself evolves by [natural selection](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Natural_selection), and (3) the study of the historical discovery of new abstract entities such as abstract number or abstract value that necessarily precede the individual acquisition and usage of such abstractions.

Evolutionary ethics is a field of inquiry that explores how [evolutionary theory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evolutionary_theory) might bear on our understanding of [ethics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethics) or [morality](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morality).

evolutionary faunas of marine animals from the [Cambrian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cambrian) to the present (that is, the entire [Phanerozoic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phanerozoic)) was introduced by [Jack Sepkoski](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jack_Sepkoski) in 1981 using [factor analysis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Factor_analysis) of the fossil record.

grade is a [taxon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taxon) united by a level of [morphological](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morphology_(biology)) or [physiological](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Physiological) complexity.

Evolutionary graph theory is an area of research lying at the intersection of [graph theory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Graph_theory), [probability theory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Probability_theory), and [mathematical biology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mathematical_biology).

Evolutionary linguistics or Darwinian linguistics is a [sociobiological](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sociobiology) approach to the study of [language](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Language).

Evolutionary medicine or Darwinian medicine is the application of modern [evolutionary theory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evolution) to understanding health and [disease](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disease).

definition: Evolutionary neuroscience is the scientific study of the [evolution of nervous systems](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evolution_of_nervous_systems).

definition: Evolutionary pressure, selective pressure or selection pressure is exerted by factors that reduce or increase [reproductive success](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reproductive_success) in a portion of a population, driving [natural selection](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Natural_selection).

Evolutionary psychology is a theoretical approach in [psychology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Psychology) that examines cognition and behavior from a modern [evolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evolution)ary perspective.

evolutionary radiation is an increase in [taxonomic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taxonomy_(biology)) diversity that is caused by elevated rates of [speciation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Speciation), ==See also== * [Evolutionary fauna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evolutionary_fauna) * [Adaptive radiation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adaptive_radiation) * [Nonadaptive radiation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nonadaptive_radiation) ==References== [[Category:Evolutionary biology terminology]] p60esqkznb9qgddvfr62dkjjobd81gj
Evolutionary rescue is a process by which a population—that would have gone extinct in the absence of evolution—persists due to natural selection acting on heritable variation.

Evolutionary suicide is an evolutionary phenomenon in which the process of [adaptation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adaptation) causes the population to become [extinct](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Extinct).

Evolutionary taxonomy, evolutionary systematics or Darwinian classification is a branch of [biological classification](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biological_classification) that seeks to classify [organism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organism)s using a combination of [phylogenetic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phylogenetics) relationship (shared descent), progenitor-descendant relationship (serial descent), and degree of [evolutionary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evolutionary) change.

Evolutionary theodicies are responses to the question of [animal suffering](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wild_animal_suffering) as an aspect of the [problem of evil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Problem_of_evil).

Evolutionary theory was a [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer-reviewed) [scientific journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_journal) covering all aspects of [evolutionary biology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evolutionary_biology).

Evolutionary therapy is a subfield of [evolutionary medicine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evolutionary_medicine) that utilizes concepts from [evolutionary biology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evolutionary_biology) in management of diseases caused by evolving entities such as [cancer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cancer) and microbial infections.
Evolutionary tinkering is an explanation of how [evolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evolution) happens in nature.
Evolutionary toxicology is an emerging field of science focusing on shifts in population genetics caused by the introduction of contaminants to the environment.

evolutionary tradeoff is a situation in which [evolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evolution) cannot advance one part of a [biological system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biological_system) without distressing another part of it.
Evolutionary transition in individuality is the process through which descendants of independent organism become lower level units within a super-organism on a higher hierarchical level.
Evolutionism is a term used (often derogatorily) to denote the [theory of evolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Theory_of_evolution).
Evolvability is defined as the capacity of a system for [adaptive evolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adaptation).

Pairwise coevolution When [Darwin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_Darwin) received an [orchid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angraecum_sesquipedale) from [Madagascar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madagascar) whose [nectary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nectary) was one and a half feet long, he surmised that there must be a [pollinator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pollinator) [moth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moth) with a [proboscis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Proboscis) long enough to reach the nectar.
Ewa Paluch is a French-Polish biophysicist and cell biologist.

Exapion fuscirostre (formerly Apion fuscirostre) is a species of [straight-snouted weevil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brentidae) known by the general common name Scotch broom seed weevil.
Exapion ulicis (formerly Apion ulicis) is a species of [straight-snouted weevil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brentidae) known by the general common name Gorse Seed Weevil.
Exaptation or co-option is a shift in the [function](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Function_(biology)) of a trait during [evolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evolution).
exceptional forest ecosystems of Quebec (; EFE) are stands of trees of outstanding interest for biodiversity that are intended to be preserved for future generations.

definition: Excess post-exercise oxygen consumption (EPOC, informally called afterburn) is a measurably increased rate of [oxygen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oxygen) intake following strenuous [activity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Exercise).
Excretion is elimination of [metabolic waste](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metabolic_waste), which is an essential process in all [organism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organism)s.

excretory system is a passive biological system that removes excess, unnecessary materials from the [body fluid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Body_fluid)s of an [organism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organism), so as to help maintain internal chemical [homeostasis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Homeostasis) and prevent damage to the body.

definition: Exercise intolerance is a condition of inability or decreased ability to perform [physical exercise](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Physical_exercise) at the normally expected level or duration for people of that age, size, sex, and muscle mass.
Exercise-associated muscle cramps (EAMC) are defined as [cramp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cramp)ing (painful muscle spasms) during or immediately following exercise.

Exercise-induced collapse (EIC) is a [genetic disorder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetic_disorder) that causes [dogs of certain breeds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dog_breed) to collapse after a period of intense exercise.
Exercise-induced laryngeal obstruction (EILO) is a transient, reversible narrowing of the [larynx](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Larynx) during high-intensity exercise.

exerkine is a [signaling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_signaling) molecule released in response to [exercise](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Exercise) that helps mediate systemic adaptations to exercise.
Exertion is the [physical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Action_(physics)) or perceived use of [energy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Energy).

exfoliation describes the natural process of [bark](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bark_(botany)) peeling or otherwise separating from a [tree trunk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tree_trunk), typically in large strips or plates that remain partially attached to the trunk until such time as they are completely detached by the elements or the eventual and subsequent exfoliation of additional layers of bark.
Exhalation (or expiration) is the flow of the [breath](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Breathing) out of an organism.

ExoCarta is a manually curated database of [exosomal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Exosome_(vesicle)) proteins, [RNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RNA) and [lipids](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lipids).
exodermis is a physiological barrier that has a role in root function and protection.
Exogamy is the [social norm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Social_norm) of mating or marrying outside one's [social group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Social_group).

exome is composed of all of the [exons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Exon) within the [genome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genome), the sequences which, when transcribed, remain within the mature [RNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RNA) after [introns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Introns) are removed by [RNA splicing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RNA_splicing).

Exome sequencing, also known as whole exome sequencing (WES), is a [genomic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genomic) technique for [sequencing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sequencing) all of the protein-coding regions of [genes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genes) in a [genome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genome) (known as the [exome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Exome)).

exonic splicing enhancer (ESE) is a DNA [sequence motif](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sequence_motif) consisting of 6 bases within an [exon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Exon) that directs, or enhances, accurate [splicing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Splicing_(genetics)) of heterogeneous nuclear RNA ([hnRNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HnRNA)) or [pre-mRNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pre-mRNA) into messenger RNA ([mRNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MRNA)).

Exonucleases are [enzymes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enzymes) that work by cleaving [nucleotides](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nucleotides) one at a time from the end (exo) of a polynucleotide chain.
Exophers are a type of membrane-bound [extracellular vesicle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Extracellular_vesicle) (EV) that are released by budding out of cells into the extracellular space.

Exoribonuclease-resistant RNAs (xrRNAs) are structured viral [RNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RNA) elements that block 5′→3′ degradation by host [exoribonuclease](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Exoribonuclease)s such as [Xrn1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/XRN1_(gene)).

expanded genetic code is an artificially modified [genetic code](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetic_code) in which one or more specific [codon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Codon)s have been re-allocated to encode an [amino acid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amino_acid) that is not among the 22 common naturally-encoded [proteinogenic amino acid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Proteinogenic_amino_acid)s.
Expected progeny differences (EPD) are an evaluation of an [animal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Animal)’s genetic worth as a parent.

Experimental Biology and Medicine is a [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer-reviewed) [scientific journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_journal) that covers experimental [biological](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biology) and [medical research](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medical_research).
related: Society for Experimental Biology and Medicine

definition: Experimental Brain Research is a [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer_review) [scientific journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_journal) covering research in [neuroscience](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neuroscience).

Experimental Cell Research is a [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer_review) [scientific journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_journal) covering [cell biology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_biology).

Experimental ecology is the scientific study of ecological relationships and processes using controlled experiments, mostly which focus on understanding how living organisms interact with their natural environment.

definition: Experimental Neurology is a monthly [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer_review) [medical journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medical_journal) that focuses on research in [neuroscience](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neuroscience) concerning mechanisms underlying [neurological disorders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neurological_disorders).

Experimental Physiology is a monthly [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer-reviewed) [scientific journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_journal) published by [Wiley-Blackwell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wiley-Blackwell) on behalf of [The Physiological Society](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Physiological_Society).
exponential integrate-and-fire models are compact and computationally efficient nonlinear [spiking neuron model](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spiking_neuron_model)s with one or two variables.

EXPOSE is a multi-user facility mounted outside the [International Space Station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Space_Station) (ISS) dedicated to [astrobiology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Astrobiology).

Expression cloning is a technique in [DNA cloning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA_cloning) that uses [expression vector](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Expression_vector)s to generate a library of clones, with each clone expressing one [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein).

expression quantitative trait locus (eQTL) is a type of [quantitative trait locus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantitative_trait_locus) (QTL), a genomic [locus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Locus_(genetics)) (region of DNA) that is associated with [phenotypic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phenotype) variation for a specific, quantifiable [trait](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phenotypic_trait).

expression vector, otherwise known as an expression construct, is usually a [plasmid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plasmid) or virus designed for [gene expression](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene_expression) in cells.
expressivity is the degree to which a [phenotype](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phenotype) is expressed by individuals having a particular [genotype](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genotype).

Extended Evolutionary Synthesis (EES) consists of a set of theoretical concepts argued to be more comprehensive than the earlier [modern synthesis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_synthesis_(20th_century)) of [evolutionary biology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evolutionary_biology) that took place between 1918 and 1942.
Extended female sexuality is where the female of a species [mates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mating) despite being infertile.

Extended order is an [economics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Economics) and [sociology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sociology) concept introduced by [Friedrich Hayek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Friedrich_Hayek) in his book [The Fatal Conceit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Fatal_Conceit).

Extended producer responsibility (EPR) is a strategy to add all of the estimated [environmental costs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Environmental_costs) associated with a product throughout the [product life cycle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Product_life_cycle) to the [market price](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Market_price) of that product, contemporarily mainly applied in the field of [waste management](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waste_management).
extension Poly(A) Test (ePAT) describes a method to determine the poly(A) tail lengths of [mRNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MRNA) [molecule](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Molecule)s.

extensor retinaculum (dorsal carpal ligament, or posterior annular ligament) is but a thickening of the [antebrachial fascia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antebrachial_fascia) (deep fascia of forearm) that holds the [tendon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tendon)s of the [extensor muscles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_extensors_of_the_human_body) in place.

External gills are the [gill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gill)s of an animal, most typically an amphibian, that are exposed to the environment, rather than set inside the [pharynx](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pharynx) and covered by [gill slit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gill_slit)s, as they are in most [fishes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fishes).
External lamina is a structure similar to [basal lamina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basal_lamina) that surrounds the [sarcolemma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarcolemma) of muscle cells.
external limiting membrane (or outer limiting membrane) is one of the ten distinct layers of the [retina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Retina) of the [eye](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_eye).
Extinction is the termination of a [species](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Species) via the [death](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Death) of its [last member](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Endling).

definition: extinction debt is the future [extinction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Extinction) of [species](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Species) due to events in the past.

extinction probability is the chance of an [inherited trait](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inherited_trait) becoming [extinct](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Extinction) as a [function](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Function_(mathematics)) of [time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time) ∞ this may be the complement of the [chance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Probability) of becoming a universal [trait](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phenotypic_trait).

Extinction threshold is a term used in [conservation biology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conservation_biology) to explain the point at which a [species](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Species), [population](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Population_(biology)) or [metapopulation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metapopulation), experiences an abrupt change in density or number because of an important parameter, such as habitat loss.
Extra-pair copulation (EPC) is a [mating](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mating) behaviour in [monogamous](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monogamy_in_animals) species.

extracellular fluid (ECF) denotes all [body fluid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Body_fluid) outside the [cells](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_(biology)) of any [multicellular organism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multicellular_organism).

Extracellular space refers to the part of a [multicellular organism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multicellular_organism) outside the [cells](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_(biology)), usually taken to be outside the [plasma membrane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plasma_membrane)s, and occupied by fluid.

Extracellular vesicles (EVs) are [lipid bilayer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lipid_bilayer)-delimited particles that are naturally released from almost all types of [cells](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_(biology)).
extrachromosomal array is a method for [mosaic analysis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mosaic_analysis) in [genetics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetics).

extramachrochaetae (emc) is a [Drosophila melanogaster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drosophila_melanogaster) gene that codes for the Emc [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein), which has a wide variety of developmental roles.
Extranuclear inheritance or cytoplasmic inheritance is the transmission of genes that occur outside the [nucleus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_nucleus).

Extraterrestrial intelligence (ETI) refers to hypothetical beings – [extraterrestrial life](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Extraterrestrial_life) or more artificial beings 30 May 2021) [[Category:Extraterrestrial life]] [[Category:Intelligence]] [[Category:Biological hypotheses]] 9u98gv5kdpg630ji7fpx21icy16fjas

extremophile () is an [organism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organism) that is able to live or even thrive in [extreme environments](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Extreme_environments), such as extreme [temperature](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Temperature) (hot or cold), [pressure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pressure), [radiation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radiation), [salinity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salinity), or [pH level](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PH_level).

definition: Eyeblink conditioning (EBC) is a form of [classical conditioning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Classical_conditioning) that has been used extensively to study neural structures and mechanisms that underlie [learning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Learning) and [memory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Memory).
eyelid ( ) is a thin fold of skin that covers and protects the [eye](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eye).
eyespot (sometimes ocellus) is an [eye](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eye)-like marking.

eyespot apparatus (or stigma) is a photoreceptive [organelle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organelle) found in the flagellate or (motile) cells of [green algae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Green_algae) and other [unicellular](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microorganism) [photosynthetic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Photosynthesis) organisms such as [euglenid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euglenid)s.

EzTaxon database is a web-based tool for the identification of [prokaryotes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prokaryotes) based on [16S ribosomal RNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/16S_ribosomal_RNA) gene sequences.

frequency-current curve (fI or F-I curve) is the function that relates the net [synaptic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Synapse) current (I) flowing into a [neuron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neuron) to its firing rate (F) }} [[Category:Neuroscience]] a1dryekyh69hzx3cs5sx766340t9lhp

f-ratio is the fraction of total [primary production](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primary_production) fuelled by [nitrate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nitrate) (as opposed to that fuelled by other [nitrogen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nitrogen) [compounds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chemical_compound) such as [ammonium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ammonium)).
F1 hybrid (also known as filial 1 hybrid) is the first filial [generation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generation_(Non-human_organism)) of offspring of distinctly different parental types.
Fatty acid binding protein 7, brain (FABP7; also brain lipid binding protein, BLBP), is a human [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).

definition: Facts on the ground is a diplomatic and [geopolitical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geopolitical) term that means the situation in reality as opposed to in the abstract.
Facultative means (antonym [obligate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Obligate)), and is used mainly in biology.

facultative parasite is an [organism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organism) that may resort to [parasitic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parasite) activity, but does not absolutely rely on any [host](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Host_(biology)) for completion of its [life cycle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biological_life_cycle).

Focal adhesions (FAs) also cell–matrix adhesions are large [multiprotein complexes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multiprotein_complexes) through which mechanical force and regulatory signals are transmitted between the [extracellular matrix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Extracellular_matrix) (ECM) and an interacting [cell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_(biology)).
Foetal cerebral redistribution or 'brain-sparing' is a diagnosis in [foetal medicine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foetal_medicine).

fold of the left vena cava, ligament of the left vena cava, or vestigial fold of Marshall, is a triangular fold of the serous [pericardium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pericardium) that lies between the left [pulmonary artery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pulmonary_artery) and subjacent [pulmonary vein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pulmonary_vein).

Foliicolous refers to the growth habit of certain [lichen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lichen)s, [algae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Algae), [fungi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fungi), [liverwort](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liverwort)s, and other [bryophyte](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryophyte)s that prefer to grow on the leaves of [vascular plants](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vascular_plants).
follicle is a small, spherical or vase-like group of cells enclosing a cavity in which some other structure grows or other material is contained.
Follicular drug delivery is a mechanism that enables the transport of therapeutic agents through the hair follicles present on the skin.

follower neuron is a nerve cell that arises in the developmental stage of the [brain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brain) and whose growth and orientation is intrinsically related to [pioneer neuron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pioneer_neuron)s.

definition: fontanelle (or fontanel) (colloquially, soft spot) is an [anatomical feature](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_body) of the infant [human skull](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_skull) comprising soft [membranous](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Membrane) gaps ([sutures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Suture_(joint))) between the cranial bones that make up the [calvaria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calvaria_(skull)) of a [fetus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fetus) or an [infant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Infant).

Fontes do Ipiranga Biological Reserve () is a [biological reserve](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biological_reserve_(Brazil)) in the Fontes do Ipiranga State Park in [São Paulo State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/São_Paulo_(state)), Brazil.
Food and biological process engineering is a discipline concerned with applying principles of engineering to the fields of food production and distribution and biology.
Food drunkenness is the physiological state of a person after consuming large amounts of food.

Food energy is [chemical energy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chemical_energy) that animals derive from [food](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Food) to sustain their [metabolism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metabolism) and [muscular](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muscle) activity.
food plot is a planted area set aside to act as a supplementary food source for [wildlife](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wildlife).
Food self-provisioning (FSP) is the growing of one's own food, especially fruits and vegetables.

Foot-and-mouth disease (FMD) or hoof-and-mouth disease (HMD) is an [infectious](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Infectious_disease) and sometimes fatal [viral](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virus_(biology)) [disease](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disease) that primarily affects [even-toed ungulates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Even-toed_ungulates), including domestic and wild [bovid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bovidae)s.
Foramen cecum, in [dental anthropology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dental_anthropology), is a minor expression of the [protostylid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protostylid) of the tooth.

Forcipules are the modified, pincer-like [front legs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maxilliped) of [centipede](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Centipede)s that are used to inject [venom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Venom) into prey.

forearm is the region of the [upper limb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Upper_limb) between the [elbow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elbow-joint) and the [wrist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wrist).
forebrain or prosencephalon is the [[Anatomical terms of location#Directional terms|rostral]] (forward-most) portion of the [brain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brain).

forelimb or front limb is one of the [paired](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bilateral_symmetry) [articulated](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joint) [appendage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Appendage)s ([limb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Limb_(anatomy))s) attached on the [cranial](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cranial) ([anterior](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anterior_(anatomy))) end of a [terrestrial](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Terrestrial_animal) [tetrapod](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tetrapod) [vertebrate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vertebrate)'s [torso](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Torso).

Forensic anthropology is the application of the anatomical science of [anthropology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthropology) and its various subfields, including forensic [archaeology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Archaeology) and forensic [taphonomy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taphonomy), }} ==External links== * [https://www.bournemouth.ac.uk/search/forensic%20Anthropology University of Bournemouth] * [https://web.archive.org/web/20110928145314/http://www.shc.ed.ac.uk/archaeology/postgraduate/msc_foren
Forensic biology is the application of [biological](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biological) principles and techniques in the investigation of criminal and civil cases.
Forensic DNA analysis is the determination of a [DNA profile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA_profile) for legal and investigative purposes.
Forensic entomological decomposition is how insects decompose and what that means for timing and information in criminal investigations.

Forensic limnology is a sub-field of [freshwater ecology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Limnology), which focuses especially on the presence of [diatoms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diatoms) in crime scene samples and victims.
Forest degradation is a process in which the biological wealth of a forest area is permanently diminished by some factor or by a combination of factors.
Forest dynamics are the underlying physical and biological forces that shape and change a [forest ecosystem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forest_ecosystem).

Forest ecology is the scientific study of the interrelated patterns, processes, [flora](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flora), [fauna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fauna), [funga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Funga), and [ecosystem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ecosystem)s in [forests](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forests).

Forest Ecosystems is a bimonthly [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer-reviewed) [open access](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Open_access) [scientific journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_journal) covering research related to the structure and dynamics of * * * ==See also== *[Agricultural and Forest Meteorology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Agricultural_and_Forest_Meteorology) *[Urban Forestry and Urban Greening](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urban_Forestry_and_Urban_Greening) *[Forest Ecology and Management](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forest_Ecology_and_Management) ==References== ==External links== * [[Category:Ecology journals]] [[Category:Open-access journ

forest floor, also called [detritus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Detritus) or [[wikt:duff#Noun 2|duff]], is the part of a [forest ecosystem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forest_ecosystem) that mediates between the living, aboveground portion of the [forest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forest) and the mineral [soil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soil), principally composed of dead and decaying plant matter such as rotting [wood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wood) and shed [leaves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leaf).

Forest floor interception is the part of the (net) [precipitation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Precipitation) or [throughfall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Throughfall) that is temporarily stored in the top layer of the [forest floor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forest_floor) and successively evaporated within a few hours or days during and after the [rainfall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rain) event.

Forest genetic resources or forest tree genetic resources are [genetic resources](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetic_resources) (i.e., [genetic material](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetic_material) of actual or future value) of forest shrub and tree species.
Forest migration is the movement of large [seed plant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spermatophyte) dominated communities in geographical space over time.

fork cell, also known as a fork neuron, is a type of [neuron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neuron) found in the human brain, located in the [anterior cingulate cortex](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anterior_cingulate_cortex) (ACC) and [frontoinsular cortex](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Insular_cortex) (FI).

Form classification is the classification of organisms based on their [morphology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morphology_(biology)), which does not necessarily reflect their biological relationships.
Form perception is the recognition of visual elements of objects, specifically those to do with shapes, patterns and previously identified important characteristics.
[Formate dehydrogenase](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Formate_dehydrogenase)s are enzymes that catalyse the oxidation of formate to carbon dioxide.

fossorial animal () is one that is adapted to digging and which lives primarily (but not solely) underground.

Foster's rule, also known as the island rule or the island effect, is an [ecogeographical rule](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ecogeographical_rule) in [evolutionary biology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evolutionary_biology) stating that members of a [species](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Species) get smaller or bigger depending on the resources available in the environment.

foveal avascular zone (FAZ) is a region within the [fovea centralis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fovea_centralis) at the centre of the [retina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Retina) of the human eye that is devoid of retinal blood vessels.

gametophyte () is one of the two [alternating](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alternation_of_generations) [multicellular phases](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multicellular_organism) in the life cycles of [plant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plant)s.

gastric mucosa is the [mucous membrane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mucous_membrane) layer that lines the entire [stomach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stomach).

gastrointestinal wall of the [gastrointestinal tract](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_gastrointestinal_tract) is made up of four layers of specialised tissue.

gastrovascular cavity is the primary organ of [digestion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digestion) and [[Circulatory system#Absence of circulatory system|circulation]] in two major animal phyla: the [Coelenterates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cnidaria) or cnidarians (including [jellyfish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jellyfish) and [corals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corals)) and [Platyhelminthes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Platyhelminthes) (flatworms).

GemIdent is an interactive [image recognition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Image_recognition) program that identifies [regions of interest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Region_of_interest) in images and photographs.

gemma (English plural gemmas, Latin plural gemmae) is a single [cell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_(biology)), or a mass of cells, or a modified bud of tissue, that detaches from the parent and develops into a new individual.

Gemmules are internal [buds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Budding) found in [sponge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sea_sponge)s and are involved in [asexual reproduction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asexual_reproduction).

Genotype to Phenotype Databases: a Holistic Approach (GEN2PHEN) is a European project aiming to develop a knowledge [web portal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Web_portal) integrating information from the [genotype](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genotype) (G) to the [phenotype](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phenotype) (P) in a unifying portal: The Knowledge Centre.

Gender typing is the process by which a child becomes aware of their [gender](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gender) and thus behaves accordingly by adopting values and attributes of members of the sex that they identify as their own.

Gene is a [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer-reviewed) [scientific journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_journal) in [genetics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetics) and [molecular biology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Molecular_biology), focusing on the [cloning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cloning), [structure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene_structure), [function](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phenotype), as well as the biomedical and biotechnological importance of [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene)s.

Gene amplification refers to a number of natural and artificial processes by which the number of copies of a [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene) is increased * [Transcription-mediated amplification](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transcription-mediated_amplification), an isothermal, single-tube [nucleic acid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nucleic_acid) amplification system utilizing two enzymes, [RNA polymerase](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RNA_polymerase) and [reverse transcriptase](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reverse_transcriptase), to rapidly amplify the target RNA/DNA, enabling the simultaneous detection of multiple pathogenic organisms in a single tube.
Gene by Gene is a commercial [genetic testing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetic_testing) company based in [Houston, Texas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Houston).

gene cassette is a type of [mobile genetic element](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mobile_genetic_element) that contains a gene and a [recombination](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Site-specific_recombination) site.

gene co-expression network (GCN) is an [[Graph (discrete mathematics)#Undirected graph|undirected graph]], where each node corresponds to a [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene), and a pair of nodes is connected with an edge if there is a significant [co-expression](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene_expression) relationship between them.

definition: Gene conversion is the process by which one [DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA) sequence replaces a [homologous sequence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Homologous_sequence) such that the sequences become identical after the conversion.

Gene delivery is the process of introducing foreign genetic material, such as [DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA) or [RNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RNA), into host [cells](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_(biology)).
Gene Designer is a computer [software](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Software) package for [bioinformatics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bioinformatics).

Gene Disease Database is a systematized collection of data, typically structured to model aspects of reality, in a way to comprehend the underlying mechanisms of complex diseases, by understanding multiple composite interactions between [phenotype](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phenotype)-[genotype](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genotype) relationships and gene-disease mechanisms.

Gene doping is the hypothetical non-therapeutic use of [gene therapy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene_therapy) by athletes in order to improve their performance in those [sporting events](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sports_competition) which prohibit such applications of genetic modification technology, == Health risks == ==See also== * [Doping in sport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doping_in_sport) * [Human genetic enhancement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_genetic_enhancement) * [Stem cell doping](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stem_cell_doping) ==References== attribution contains text

Gene duplication (or chromosomal duplication or gene amplification) is a mechanism through which new genetic material is generated during [molecular evolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Molecular_evolution).

Gene expression is the process by which the information contained within a [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene) is used to produce a functional gene product, such as a [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) or a functional [RNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RNA) molecule.

gene expression profiling is the measurement of the activity (the [expression](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene_expression)) of thousands of genes at once, to create a global picture of cellular function.
gene family is a set of several similar genes, formed by duplication of a single original [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene), and generally with similar biochemical functions.

gene flow (also known as migration and allele flow) is the transfer of [genetic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetic_variation) material from one [population](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Population_(biology)) to another.

gene gun or biolistic particle delivery system is a device used to deliver exogenous [DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA) ([transgene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transgene)s), [RNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RNA), or [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) to cells.

gene knock-in (abbreviation: KI) refers to a [genetic engineering](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetic_engineering) method that involves the one-for-one substitution of DNA sequence information in a [genetic locus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Locus_(genetics)) or the [insertion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Insertion_(genetics)) of sequence information not found within the locus.

Gene knockdown is an experimental technique by which the [expression](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene_expression) of one or more of an [organism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organism)'s [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene)s is reduced.

Gene nomenclature is the scientific [naming](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nomenclature) of [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene)s, the units of [heredity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heredity) in living organisms.

Gene Ontology (GO) is a major [bioinformatics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bioinformatics) initiative to unify the representation of [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene) and [gene product](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene_product) attributes across all [species](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Species).
Gene order is the permutation of [genome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genome) arrangement.

gene pool is the set of all [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene)s, or [genetic information](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetic_information), in any [population](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Population_(biology)), usually of a particular [species](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Species).
gene prediction or gene finding refers to the process of identifying the regions of genomic DNA that encode [genes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genes).

Genetic regulatory circuits (also referred to as transcriptional regulatory circuits) is a concept that evolved from the [Operon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operon) Model discovered by [François Jacob](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/François_Jacob) and [Jacques Monod](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacques_Monod).

media.file: Representation of a Genetic Regulatory Circuit.png

definition: gene (or genetic) regulatory network (GRN) is a collection of molecular regulators that interact with each other and with other substances in the cell to govern the [gene expression](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene_expression) levels of [mRNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MRNA) and proteins which, in turn, determine the function of the cell.

Gene Relationships Across Implicated Loci (GRAIL) is a free web application developed by [Soumya Raychaudhuri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soumya_Raychaudhuri) at the [Broad Institute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Broad_Institute) with the goal of determining the relationships among [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene)s in different disease associated [loci](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Locus_(genetics)) through [statistical analysis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statistics).

gene signature or gene expression signature is a single or combined group of genes in a cell with a uniquely characteristic pattern of gene expression [[Category:Genetics]] 5mg7o8iv2to2hxktk6blu3f4y4xxnuv

Gene targeting is a [biotechnological](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biotechnology) tool used to change the [DNA sequence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA_sequencing) of an organism (hence it is a form of [genome editing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genome_editing)).

gene theft or DNA theft is the act of acquiring the [genetic material](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetic_material) of another individual, usually from [public places](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Public_space), without their permission.

Gene therapy is [medical technology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Health_technology) that aims to produce a [therapeutic effect](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Therapeutic_effect) through the manipulation of [gene expression](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene_expression) or through altering the biological properties of living cells.

definition: A) with typical GTA (gene transfer agent) production and transduction (B).|alt=|330x330px]] Gene transfer agents (GTAs) are DNA-containing [virus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virus)-like particles that are produced by some [bacteria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bacteria) and [archaea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Archaea) and mediate [horizontal gene transfer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horizontal_gene_transfer).

Gene trapping is a [high-throughput](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/High-throughput_screening) approach that is used to introduce insertional [mutations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mutations) across an organism's genome.

Gene-environment interplay describes how [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene)s and [environments](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biophysical_environment) work together to produce a [phenotype](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phenotype), or observable trait.

genealogical DNA test is a [DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA)-based [genetic test](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetic_testing) used in [genetic genealogy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetic_genealogy) that looks at specific locations of a person's [genome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genome) in order to find or verify ancestral [genealogical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genealogical) relationships, or (with lower reliability) to estimate the [ethnic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethnicity) mixture of an individual.

Genecology is a branch of [ecology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ecology) which studies [genetic variation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetic_variation) of [species](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Species) and [communities](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Community) compared to their [population distribution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Population_distribution) in a particular [environment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Environment_(biophysical)).

GeneNetwork is a combined database and [open-source](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Open-source_software) [bioinformatics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bioinformatics) data analysis software resource for [systems genetics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Systems_genetics).

general mixed Yule–coalescent model (GMYC), also called the generalized mixed Yule–coalescent model, is a method in [molecular phylogenetics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Molecular_phylogenetics) and [systematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Systematics) for inferring putative [species](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Species) boundaries from [DNA sequence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA_sequence) data.

general selection model (GSM) is a model of [population genetics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Population_genetics) that describes how a population's [allele frequencies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Allele_frequencies) will change when acted upon by [natural selection](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Natural_selection).

general senses are the [sense](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sense)s which are perceived due to receptors scattered throughout the body such as touch, temperature, and hunger, rather than tied to a specific structure, as the [special senses](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Special_senses) [vision](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Visual_perception) or [hearing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hearing) are.

generalist species is able to thrive in a wide variety of environmental conditions and can make use of a variety of different [resources](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Natural_resource) (for example, a [heterotroph](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heterotroph) with a varied [diet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diet_(nutrition))).
