Generalized exchange is a type of [social exchange](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Social_exchange) in which a desired outcome that is sought by an individual is not dependent on the resources provided by that individual.
generalized Lotka–Volterra equations are a set of equations which are more general than either the competitive or predator–prey examples of Lotka–Volterra types.
Generalized periodic epileptiform discharges (GPEDs) are very rare abnormal patterns found in [EEG](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/EEG).

categories: Population genetics in the United Kingdom

definition: generation time is the average time between two consecutive generations in the lineages of a [population](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Population_(biology)), being linked to [biological life cycle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biological_life_cycle)s.
Generative anthropology is a field of study based on the [hypothesis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hypothesis) that the origin of human language happened in a singular event.

Generative Tissue (gTissue) is a living tissue created in a patient (human or non-human) by a [surgeon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Surgeon), consisting of an [extracellular matrix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Extracellular_matrix), [cells](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_(biology)), and supporting vascular supply with generative properties.

GeneRec is a generalization of the [recirculation algorithm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Recirculation_algorithm), and approximates [Almeida-Pineda recurrent backpropagation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Almeida-Pineda_recurrent_backpropagation).
GeneRIF or Gene Reference Into Function is a short (255 characters or fewer) statement about the function of a gene.

Genes is a quarterly [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer-reviewed) [open access](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Open_access) [scientific journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_journal) that is published by [MDPI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MDPI).

Genes to Cells is a [peer-review](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer-review)ed [scientific journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_journal) that publishes original research on the molecular mechanisms of biological events.

Genes, Brain and Behavior (also known as G2B) is a bimonthly [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer-reviewed) [open access](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Open_access) [scientific journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_journal) covering research in the fields of [behavioral](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Behavioural_genetics), [neural](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neurogenetics), and [psychiatric genetics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Psychiatric_genetics).
related: International Behavioural and Neural Genetics Society

definition: Genesis: The Journal of Genetics and Development (often styled genesis) is a [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer_review) [scientific journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_journal) of [genetics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetics) and [developmental biology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Developmental_biology).
Genesys is an online, global portal about plant [genetic resources](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetic_resources) for food and agriculture.

GeneTalk is a web-based platform, tool, and database for filtering, reduction and prioritization of human [sequence variants](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetic_variation) from [[Next_generation_sequencing#Next-generation_methods|next-generation sequencing]] (NGS) data.
Genetic ablation occurs when a gene is deemed “null” through the homologous [genetic recombination](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetic_recombination) of a gene.
genetic algebra is a (possibly [non-associative](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-associative_algebra)) algebra used to model inheritance in genetics.
Genetic Alliance is a nonprofit organization, founded in 1986 by Joan O.

Genetic architecture is the underlying genetic basis of a [phenotypic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phenotype) [trait](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trait_(biological)) and its variational properties.
Genetic assimilation is a process described by [[C.

Genetic association is when one or more [genotype](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genotype)s within a population co-occur with a [phenotypic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phenotype) trait [more often than would be expected by chance occurrence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Association_(statistics)).

Genetic code is a set of rules used by living [cells](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_(biology)) to [translate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Translation_(biology)) information encoded within genetic material ([DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA) or [RNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RNA) sequences of nucleotide triplets or [codon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Codon)s) into [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein)s.

Genetic codes is a simple [ASN.1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ASN.1) database hosted by the [National Center for Biotechnology Information](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Center_for_Biotechnology_Information) and listing all the known [Genetic code](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetic_code)s.

Genetic counseling is the process of investigating individuals and families affected by or at risk of genetic disorders to help them understand and adapt to the medical, psychological and familial implications of genetic contributions to disease.

genetic demixing refers to a phenomenon in which an initial mixture of individuals with two or more distinct [genotypes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genotypes) rearranges in the course of time, giving birth to a spatial organization where some or all genotypes are concentrated in distinct patches.

definition: Genetic divergence is the process in which two or more populations of an ancestral species accumulate independent genetic changes ([mutations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mutations)) through time, often leading to reproductive isolation and continued mutation even after the populations have become [reproductively isolated](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reproductive_isolation) for some period of time, as there is not any genetic exchange anymore.
Genetic diversity is the total number of [genetic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetics) characteristics in the genetic makeup of a species.
Genetic ecology is the study of the stability and expression of varying genetic material within abiotic mediums.

Genetic epidemiology is the study of the role of [genetic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetics) factors in determining health and disease in families and in populations, and the interplay of such genetic factors with environmental factors.

Genetic equilibrium is the condition of an [allele](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Allele) or [genotype](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genotype) in a gene pool (such as a population) where the frequency does not change from generation to generation.

Genetic exceptionalism is the belief that [genetic information](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetic_information) is special and so must be treated differently from other types of medical data or other [personally identifiable information](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Personal_data).

Genetic genealogy is the use of [genealogical DNA test](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genealogical_DNA_test)s, i.e., [DNA profiling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA_profiling) and [DNA testing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetic_testing), in combination with traditional [genealogical methods](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genealogy), to infer [genetic relationship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetic_distance)s between individuals.

Genetic heterogeneity refers to different genetic causes for the same disease and can be classified into three types: allelic heterogeneity, [locus heterogeneity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Locus_heterogeneity), and phenotypic heterogeneity.

definition: [Genetic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetics) imbalance is to describe situation when the [genome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genome) of a cell or organism has more copies of some genes than other genes due to [chromosomal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chromosomal) [rearrangements](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rearrangement_reaction) or [aneuploidy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aneuploidy).
Genetic Information Research Institute (GIRI) is a non-profit institution that was founded in 1994 by [Jerzy Jurka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerzy_Jurka).

Genetic linkage is the tendency of [DNA sequences](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nucleic_acid_sequence) that are close together on a [chromosome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chromosome) to be inherited together during the [meiosis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meiosis) phase of [sexual reproduction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sexual_reproduction).

Genetic load is the difference between the [fitness](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fitness_(biology)) of an average [genotype](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genotype) in a [population](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Population_(biology)) and the fitness of some reference genotype, which may be either the best present in a population, or may be the theoretically [optimal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maxima_and_minima) genotype.

mapping functions are used to model the relationship between [map](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene_mapping) distances (measured in map units or [centimorgan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Centimorgan)s) and [recombination](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetic_recombination) frequencies, particularly as these measurements relate to regions encompassed between [genetic marker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetic_marker)s.

genetic marker is a [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene) or [DNA sequence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA_sequence) with a known location on a [chromosome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chromosome) that can be used to identify individuals or [species](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Species).
Genetic matchmaking is the idea of matching couples for romantic relationships based on their biological compatibility.

Genetic monitoring is the use of [molecular markers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetic_marker) to (i) identify individuals, species or populations, or (ii) to quantify changes in [population genetic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Population_genetic) metrics (such as [effective population size](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Effective_population_size), [genetic diversity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetic_diversity) and population size) over time.

Genetic predisposition refers to a [genetic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetics) characteristic which influences the possible [phenotypic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phenotypic) development of an individual organism within a species or population under the influence of [environmental](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Natural_environment) conditions.
Genetic purging is the increased pressure of natural selection against deleterious [alleles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alleles) prompted by [inbreeding](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inbreeding).

monogenesis and polygenesis are two different [hypotheses](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hypothesis) about the [phylogenetic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phylogenetics) origin of human languages.

Linkage disequilibrium, often abbreviated to LD, is a term in [population genetics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Population_genetics) referring to the association of genes, usually linked genes, in a population.

Linnaeus's flower clock was a garden plan hypothesized by [Carl Linnaeus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carl_Linnaeus) that would take advantage of several plants that open or close their flowers at particular times of the day to accurately indicate the time.

Linnean Tercentenary Medal was commissioned in 2007 by the [Linnean Society](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Linnean_Society) to commemorate the tercentenary of the birth of [Carl Linnaeus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carl_Linnaeus).

Linwood Springs Research Station (LSRS) is a [raptor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bird_of_prey) [research station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Research_station) located in [Stevens Point, Wisconsin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stevens_Point,_Wisconsin).

definition: Lipid bilayer characterization is the use of various optical, chemical and physical probing methods to study the properties of lipid bilayers.

fusion is the process by which two initially distinct [lipid bilayer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lipid_bilayer)s merge their [hydrophobic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hydrophobic) cores, resulting in one interconnected structure.

Lipid bilayer mechanics is the study of the physical material properties of [lipid bilayers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lipid_bilayers), classifying bilayer behavior with [stress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stress_(mechanics)) and [strain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Strain_(materials_science)) rather than biochemical interactions.
LIPID MAPS (Lipid Metabolites and Pathways Strategy) is a web portal designed to be a gateway to [Lipidomics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lipidomics) resources.

Lipid-anchored proteins (also known as lipid-linked proteins) are [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein)s that are [covalently](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Covalent_bond) attached to [lipid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lipid)s embedded into [biological membranes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biological_membranes).
Lipidology is the scientific study of [lipid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lipid)s.

[liposome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liposome) extruder is a device that prepares cell membranes, [exosomes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Exosome_(vesicle)) and also generates nanoscale liposome formulations.
liquid ordered phase is a [liquid crystal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liquid_crystal)line phase of a lipid bilayer, and is of significant biological importance.

Liquid plant manures are [fermented](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fermentation) extracts of plant material that are used primarily as [fertilizer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fertilizer)s, but also for [pest control](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biological_pest_control), [plant strengthening](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plant_strengthening) and other phytosanitary purposes.

Mogi-Guaçu Biological Reserve () is a [biological reserve](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biological_reserve_(Brazil)) located in the state of [São Paulo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/São_Paulo_(state)), [Brazil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brazil).
Moiety conservation is the conservation of a subgroup in a [chemical species](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chemical_species), which is cyclically transferred from one molecule to another.
Moisture stress is a form of [abiotic stress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abiotic_stress) that occurs when the moisture of plant tissues is reduced to suboptimal levels.

Moisés Expósito-Alonso (born 1990, [Alicante](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alicante)) is a Spanish scientist and [assistant professor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Assistant_professor) of global change biology at the [University of California, Berkeley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_California,_Berkeley), member of the Innovative Genomics Institute, and inaugural Freeman Hrabowski Scholar from the [Howard Hughes Medical Institute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Howard_Hughes_Medical_Institute).
categories: Stanford University Department of Biology faculty

definition: Mol* (, also known as Molstar) is a web-based, [open-source](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Open-source_software), software toolkit for analysis and visualization of [macromolecular](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Macromolecule) structures.

page: Mold, protozoan, and coelenterate mitochondrial code and the mycoplasma/spiroplasma code
definition: mold, protozoan, and coelenterate mitochondrial code and the mycoplasma/spiroplasma code (translation table 4) is the [genetic code](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetic_code) used by various organisms, in some cases with slight variations, notably the use of UGA as a [tryptophan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tryptophan) codon rather than a [stop codon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stop_codon).

Molecular anatomy is the subspecialty of [microscopic anatomy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Histology) concerned with the identification and description of [molecular](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Molecule) [structures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Molecular_biology) of [cell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_(biology))s, [tissue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tissue_(biology))s, and [organs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organ_(anatomy)) in an organism.

Molecular and Cellular Neuroscience is a bimonthly [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer-reviewed) [scientific journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_journal) covering all aspects of [neurosciences](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neurosciences).

Molecular anthropology, also known as genetic anthropology, is the study of how [molecular biology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Molecular_biology) has contributed to the understanding of human evolution.

Molecular beacons, or molecular beacon probes, are [oligonucleotide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oligonucleotide) [hybridization probe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybridization_probe)s that can report the presence of specific [nucleic acid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nucleic_acid)s in homogenous solutions.

Molecular biology is a branch of [biology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biology) that seeks to understand the [molecular](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Molecule) structures and chemical processes that are the basis of biological activity within and between [cells](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_(biology)).

Molecular Biology () is a [scientific journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_journal) which covers a wide scope of problems related to [molecular](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Molecular_biology), [cell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_biology), and [computational biology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computational_biology) including [genomics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genomics), [proteomics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Proteomics), [bioinformatics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bioinformatics), [molecular virology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Molecular_virology) and [immunology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Immunology), molecular development biology, and [molecular evolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Molecular_evolution).

Molecular Biology of the Cell is a biweekly [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer-reviewed) [scientific journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_journal) published by the [American Society for Cell Biology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Society_for_Cell_Biology).

Molecular Brain is a [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer_review) [open access](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Open_access) [scientific journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_journal) covering research on all aspects of the [nervous system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nervous_system) at the molecular, cellular and systems levels.

Molecular Brain Research was a [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer_review) [scientific journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_journal) of [molecular neuroscience](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Molecular_neuroscience).

Molecular breeding is the application of [molecular biology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Molecular_biology) tools, often in [plant breeding](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plant_breeding) == References == == Further reading == * [[Category:Molecular biology]] [[Category:Breeding]] 3stp48ulbxqxoy1hqrq1vmf0far84kf

Molecular Cell is a [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer-reviewed) [scientific journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_journal) that covers research on [cell biology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_biology) at the [molecular level](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Molecular_biology), with an emphasis on new mechanistic insights.

Molecular cellular cognition (MCC) is a branch of [neuroscience](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neuroscience) that involves the study of cognitive processes with approaches that integrate molecular, cellular and behavioral mechanisms.

molecular clock is a figurative term for a technique that uses the [mutation rate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mutation_rate) of [biomolecule](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biomolecule)s to [deduce the time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chronological_dating) in [prehistory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prehistory) when two or more [life form](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Life_form)s [diverged](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetic_divergence).

Molecular cloning is a set of experimental methods in [molecular biology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Molecular_biology) that are used to assemble [recombinant DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Recombinant_DNA) molecules and to direct their [replication](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA_replication) within [host organisms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Host_(biology)).

molecular demon or biological molecular machine is a biological [macromolecule](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Macromolecule) that resembles and seems to have the same properties as [Maxwell's demon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maxwell's_demon).
TRAM is a genetic system that has features of [non-mendelian inheritance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-mendelian_inheritance) Turnover, copy number and functional Redundancy And Modulatory.

Molecular ecology is a [subdiscipline](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Subdiscipline) of [ecology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ecology) that is concerned with applying [molecular genetic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Molecular_genetics) techniques to ecological questions (e.g., population structure, phylogeography, conservation, speciation, hybridization, biodiversity).

Molecular Ecology is a twice monthly [scientific journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_journal) covering investigations that use molecular techniques to address questions in [ecology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ecology), [evolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evolution), [behavior](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Behavior), and [conservation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conservation_biology).

Molecular Ecology Resources is a monthly [scientific](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific) journal covering development of tools and techniques to address questions in [ecology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ecology), [evolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evolution), [behavior](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Behavior), and [conservation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conservation_biology).
Molecular Endocrinology is a peer-reviewed journal that publishes research on the molecular processes of [hormone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hormone)s.

Molecular epidemiology is a branch of [epidemiology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Epidemiology) and [medical science](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medical_science) that focuses on the contribution of potential genetic and environmental risk factors, identified at the molecular level, to the [etiology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Etiology), distribution and prevention of disease within families and across populations.

Molecular evolution describes how [inherited](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heredity) [DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA) and/or [RNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RNA) change over [evolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evolution)ary time, and the consequences of this for [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein)s and other components of [cells](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_(biology)) and [organism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organism)s.
molecular fragmentation methods have been built to break apart molecules, some of which are listed below.

Molecular genetics is a branch of [biology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biology) that addresses how differences in the structures or expression of [DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA) molecules manifests as variation among organisms.

Molecular Genetics and Metabolism is a [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer-reviewed) [academic journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academic_journal) published by [Academic Press](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academic_Press).

The Laboratory for Molecular Infection Medicine Sweden (MIMS) at [Umeå University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umeå_University) was established in 2007 as a joint venture between the European Molecular Biology Laboratory (EMBL) and the Nordic EMBL Partnership for Molecular Medicine, [Heidelberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heidelberg).

molecular lesion or point lesion is damage to the structure of a [biological molecule](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biomolecule) such as [DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA), [RNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RNA), or [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein).

Molecular Medicine Partnership Unit is an alliance between the [European Molecular Biology Laboratory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Molecular_Biology_Laboratory) and the [Medical Faculties of the University of Heidelberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heidelberg_University_Faculty_of_Medicine).

Molecular models of DNA structures are representations of the [molecular geometry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Molecular_geometry) and [topology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA_topology) of deoxyribonucleic acid ([DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA)) molecules using one of several means, with the aim of simplifying and presenting the essential, physical and chemical, properties of DNA molecular structures either in vivo or in vitro.

Molecular Neurobiology is a bimonthly [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer-reviewed) [scientific journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_journal) covering all aspects of [molecular neuroscience](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Molecular_neuroscience).

Molecular Neurodegeneration is a [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer-reviewed) [scientific journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_journal) covering research on the molecular mechanisms underlying [neurodegeneration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neurodegeneration), especially as pertaining to [neurodegenerative disease](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neurodegenerative_disease)s.

Molecular neuroscience is a branch of [neuroscience](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neuroscience) that observes concepts in [molecular biology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Molecular_biology) applied to the [nervous systems](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nervous_systems) of animals.

Molecular Pain is a [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer-reviewed) [open access](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Open_access) [medical journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medical_journal) covering all aspects of research on [pain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pain).

Molecular phenotyping describes the technique of quantifying pathway reporter genes, i.e. pre-selected genes that are modulated specifically by metabolic and [signaling pathways](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Signaling_pathways), in order to infer activity of these pathways.

Molecular phylogenetics () is the branch of [phylogeny](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phylogeny) that analyzes genetic, hereditary molecular differences, predominantly in DNA sequences, to gain information on an organism's evolutionary relationships.

Molecular Phylogenetics and Evolution is a [peer-review](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer-review)ed [scientific journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_journal) of [evolutionary biology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evolutionary_biology) and [phylogenetics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phylogenetics).

Molecular Plant is a monthly [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer-reviewed) [scientific journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_journal) which publishes both original research and review articles in the field of [plant biology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plant_biology), with a particular emphasis on plant cell biology, physiology, biochemistry, molecular biology, genetics, development, plant-microbe interaction, genomics, bioinformatics, and [molecular evolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Molecular_evolution).

Molecular Plant Pathology is a monthly [open access](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Open_access) [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer_review) [scientific journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_journal) published by [Wiley-Blackwell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wiley-Blackwell) on behalf of the [British Society for Plant Pathology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Society_for_Plant_Pathology).

molecular probe is a group of [atoms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atoms) or [molecules](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Molecules) used in [molecular biology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Molecular_biology) or [chemistry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chemistry) to study the properties of other molecules or structures.

Molecular Reproduction and Development is a [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer_review) [scientific journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_journal) that publishes research articles on [developmental](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Developmental_biology) and [reproductive biology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reproductive_biology).

Molecular risk assessment is a procedure in which [biomarker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biomarker)s (for example, biological [molecules](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Molecules) or changes in [tumor cell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tumor_cell) [DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA)) are used to estimate a person's risk for developing [cancer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cancer).

definition: molecular-weight size marker, also referred to as a [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) ladder, [DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA) ladder, or [RNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RNA) ladder, is a set of [standards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Standard_(metrology)) that are used to identify the [approximate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Approximation) size of a [molecule](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biological_molecule) run on a [gel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gel_electrophoresis) during [electrophoresis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gel_electrophoresis), using the [principle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Principle) that [molecular weight](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Molecular_weight) is inversely proportional to migration rate through a gel matrix.

Molecules and Cells is a [peer-review](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer-review)ed [open access](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Open_access) [scientific journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_journal) of [molecular](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Molecular_biology) and [cellular biology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cellular_biology).

definition: monocentric chromosome is a chromosome that has only one [centromere](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Centromere) in a [chromosome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chromosome) and forms a narrow constriction.

Monochorionic twins are [monozygotic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monozygotic) (identical) [twins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twins) that share the same [placenta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Placenta).
monoclonality refers to the state of a line of [cells](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_(biology)) that have been derived from a single clonal origin.
Monocytes are a type of leukocyte or [white blood cell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_blood_cell).
monodomain model is a reduction of the [bidomain model](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bidomain_model) of the electrical propagation in myocardial tissue.

Monodominance is an [ecological condition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ecology) in which more than 60% of the [tree canopy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tree_canopy) comprises a single species of tree.
Monogenism or sometimes monogenesis is the theory of human origins which posits a [common descent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Common_descent) for all humans.

definition: Monographs in Systematic Botany also known as Monographs in Systematic Botany from the Missouri Botanical Garden is a series of [[Monograph#Taxonomy (systematic biology)|monographs]] relating to the study of [systematic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Systematics) [botany](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Botany).
monohybrid cross is a cross between two organisms with different variations at one genetic locus of interest.

Monolysocardiolipin (MLCL) is a [phospholipid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phospholipid) with three [fatty acid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fatty_acid) chains located in the [inner membrane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inner_mitochondrial_membrane) of [mitochondria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mitochondria).

Monopolin is a [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) complex that in budding yeast is composed of the four proteins [CSM1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CSM1), [HRR25](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HRR25), [LRS4](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LRS4), and [MAM1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MAM1).
monotypic taxon is a taxonomic group ([taxon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taxon)) that contains only one immediately subordinate taxon.
Montane ecosystems are found on the slopes of [mountain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mountain)s.

definition: Montane grasslands and shrublands are a [biome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biome) defined by the [World Wide Fund for Nature](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Wide_Fund_for_Nature).

Montezumia is a primarily [neotropical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neotropical) genus of eumenine wasps whose 48 species (Willink 1982) range from [Argentina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Argentina) to the southwestern [United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States) (Arizona).

Moran's theorem (or the Moran effect) states that the time [correlation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Correlation) of two separate populations of the same species is equal to the correlation between the environmental variabilities where they live.

morbid map is a chart or diagram of [disease](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disease)s and the [chromosomal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chromosome) location of [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene)s the diseases are associated with.

Morisita's overlap index, named after [Masaaki Morisita](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Masaaki_Morisita), is a [statistical measure of dispersion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dispersion_(statistics)) of individuals in a population.

Morphallaxis is the regeneration of specific [tissue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biological_tissue) in a variety of [organisms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organisms) due to loss or death of the existing tissue.

MorphoBank is a [web application](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Web_application) for collaborative evolutionary research, specifically [phylogenetic systematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phylogenetic_systematics) or [cladistics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cladistics), on the [phenotype](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phenotype).
morphogenetic field is a research hypothesis and a discrete region of cells in an [embryo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Embryo).

Morpholino, also known as a phosphorodiamidate Morpholino oligomer (PMO), is a [nucleic acid analog](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nucleic_acid_analogue) whose backbone consists of methylene[morpholine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morpholine) rings linked through [phosphorodiamidate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phosphoramidate) groups, in contrast to the sugars linked through [phosphates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phosphates) found in natural nucleic acids.
morphology is the study of the form and structure of [organism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organism)s and their specific structural features.

Morphome is one of the omes in [biology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biology) to map and classify all the [morphological](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morphology_(biology)) features of [species](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Species).

Morris water navigation task, also known as the Morris water maze (not to be confused with [water maze](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Water_maze_(neuroscience))), is a behavioral procedure used with rats or mice.

Morris–Lecar model is a [biological neuron model](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biological_neuron_model) developed by professors Catherine Morris and Harold Lecar to reproduce the variety of [oscillatory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neural_oscillation) behavior in relation to [Ca | header = Possible Bifurcations | header_align = center | header_background = | footer = [[Electrophysiology#Current clamp|Current clamp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcium_in_biology) simulations of the Morris–Lecar model.

Mosaic coevolution is a theory in which [geographic location](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geographic_location) and [community ecology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Community_ecology) shape differing [coevolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coevolution) between strongly interacting species in multiple populations.

Mosaic evolution (or modular evolution) is the concept, mainly from [palaeontology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palaeontology), that [evolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evolution)ary change takes place in some body parts or systems without simultaneous changes in other parts.

neck frill is the relatively extensive margin seen on the back of the heads of [reptile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reptile)s with either a [bony](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bone) support such as those present on the [skull](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skull)s of [dinosaur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dinosaur)s of the suborder [Marginocephalia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marginocephalia) or a [cartilaginous](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cartilage) one as in the [frill-necked lizard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frill-necked_lizard).

Necromeny is a [symbiotic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Symbiosis) relationship where an animal (typically a juvenile stage [nematode](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nematode)) infects a host and waits inside its body until its death, at which point it develops and completes its life-cycle on the cadaver, feeding on the decaying matter and the subsequent bacterial growth.

Necrotaxis embodies a special type of [chemotaxis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chemotaxis) when the [chemoattractant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chemoattractant) molecules are released from [necrotic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Necrotic) or [apoptotic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apoptotic) cells.

Nectar is a [viscous](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Viscous), [sugar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sugar)-rich [liquid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liquid) produced by [plant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plant)s in glands called nectaries, either within the [flower](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flower)s with which it attracts [pollinating](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pollination) animals, or by extrafloral nectaries, which provide a nutrient source to animal [mutualists](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mutualism_(biology)), which in turn provide [[plant defense against herbivory#Indirect defenses|herbivore protection]].

Nectar robbing is a [foraging behavior](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foraging_behavior) used by some organisms that feed on floral [nectar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nectar), carried out by feeding from holes bitten in flowers, rather than by entering through the flowers' natural openings.
nectar source is a flowering plant that produces [nectar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nectar_(plant)) as part of its reproductive strategy.

Negligible senescence is a term coined by [biogerontologist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biogerontology) [Caleb Finch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caleb_Finch) to denote organisms that do not exhibit evidence of biological aging ([senescence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Senescence)), such as measurable reductions in their reproductive capability, measurable functional decline, or rising death rates with age.

Nematode chemoreceptors are [chemoreceptor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chemoreceptor)s of [nematode](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nematode)s.

Nematode infection in dogs - the [infection](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Infection) (also [infestation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Infestation)) of [dog](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dog)s with [parasitic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parasitism) [nemamotodes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pinworm_infection) - are, along with tapeworm infections and infections with protozoa ([giardiasis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giardiasis), [neosporosis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neospora_caninum)), frequent [parasitoses](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parasitic_disease) in veterinary practice.
Nematology is the scientific discipline concerned with the study of [nematode](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nematode)s, or roundworms.

Nematosomes are multicellular motile bodies found in the [gastrovascular cavity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gastrovascular_cavity) of the model sea anemone Nematostella vectensis [starlet sea anemone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Starlet_sea_anemone).

definition: Neoblasts () are [adult stem cells](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adult_stem_cells) found in [planarian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Planarian) flatworms.

Neocatastrophism is the [hypothesis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hypothesis) that life-exterminating events such as [gamma-ray burst](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gamma-ray_burst)s have acted as a galactic regulation mechanism in the [Milky Way](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milky_Way) upon the emergence of complex [life](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Life) in its [habitable zone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Galactic_habitable_zone).

mottled water hyacinth weevil, Neochetina eichhorniae, is a [beetle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beetle) that has been introduced as a [biological pest control](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biological_pest_control) herbivore agent to [waterway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waterway)s and [lake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake)s in countries worldwide to control the spread of the invasive [noxious weed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Noxious_weed) species [Eichhornia crassipes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eichhornia_crassipes), the water hyacinth, an [aquatic plant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aquatic_plant) native to the [Amazon basin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amazon_basin).
Neoepitopes are a class of [major histocompatibility complex](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_histocompatibility_complex) (MHC) bound [peptide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peptide)s.

neomammalian brain is one of three aspects of [[Paul D.

Natal teeth are [teeth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tooth) that are present above the gumline (have already [erupted](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tooth_eruption)) at [birth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Birth), and neonatal teeth are teeth that emerge through the [gingiva](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gingiva) during the first month of life (the [neonatal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Infant) period).

Neosomy is the formation of new external structure in an active stage of an [invertebrate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Invertebrate), in a taxon that normally only changes during [moulting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moulting).

definition: Neotoma Paleoecology Database (Neotoma) is an open international data resource that stores and shares multiple kinds of [fossil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fossil), [paleoecological](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paleoecological), and [paleoenvironmental](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paleoenvironmental) data.

nephridiopore is a pore at the end of the [nephridium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nephridium), an [excretory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Excretion) [organ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organ_(anatomy)) found in [invertebrates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Invertebrates), such as [flatworm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flatworm)s and [annelid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annelid)s.
nephron is the minute or microscopic structural and functional unit of the [kidney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kidney).
nephrostome is the funnel-like component of a [metanephridium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metanephridium).

neritic zone (or sublittoral zone) is the relatively shallow part of the [ocean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ocean) above the drop-off of the [continental shelf](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Continental_shelf), approximately in depth.

definition: Nerve glide, also known as [nerve](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nerve) flossing or nerve stretching, is an exercise that stretches nerves.

nerve guidance conduit (also referred to as an artificial nerve conduit or artificial nerve graft, as opposed to an [autograft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Autograft)) is an artificial means of guiding axonal regrowth to facilitate [nerve regeneration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nerve_regeneration) and is one of several clinical treatments for [nerve injuries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nerve_injury).

nerve net consists of interconnected [neuron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neuron)s lacking a [brain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brain) or any form of [cephalization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cephalization).
Nervous tissue, also called neural tissue, is the main [tissue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tissue_(biology)) component of the [nervous system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nervous_system).

NEST is a [simulation software](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simulation_software) for [spiking neural network](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spiking_neural_network) models, including large-scale neuronal networks.

nest protection hypothesis (NPH) is one of multiple hypotheses that seek to explain the behaviour of birds repeatedly introducing green, often aromatic, plant material into the nest after its completion and throughout the incubation and nestling periods.
Nest usurpation is when the queen of one species of [eusocial](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eusocial) insects takes over the colony of another species.

Nested association mapping (NAM) is a technique designed by the labs of [Edward Buckler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Buckler), [https://www.ars.usda.gov/people-locations/person/?person-id=2555 James Holland], and [https://www.ars.usda.gov/people-locations/person/?person-id=3766/ Michael McMullen] for identifying and dissecting the genetic architecture of [complex traits](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Complex_traits) in corn ([Zea mays](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maize)).

nested gene is a [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene) whose entire coding sequence lies within the bounds (between the [start codon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Start_codon) and the [stop codon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stop_codon)) of a larger external gene.

Nestedness is a measure of structure in an [ecological system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ecosystem), usually applied to species-sites systems (describing the distribution of species across locations), or species-species interaction networks (describing the interactions between species, usually as bipartite networks such as hosts-parasites, plants-pollinators, etc.).

Nesting behavior is an [instinct](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Instinct) in [animals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Animal) during [reproduction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sexual_reproduction) where they prepare a place with optimal conditions to nurture their [offspring](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Offspring).
Nestocoelius is a monotypic [Australasia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australasia)n genus of [potter wasp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Potter_wasp)s.
net acid excretion (NAE) is the net amount of acid [excreted](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Excretion) in the [urine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urine) per unit time.

Net ecosystem production (NEP) in [ecology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ecology), [limnology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Limnology), and [oceanography](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oceanography), is the difference between [gross primary production](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primary_production) (GPP) and [net ecosystem respiration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ecosystem_respiration).

Netherlands Institute for Neuroscience (NIN) (Dutch: Nederlands Herseninstituut) is a research institute of the [Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Netherlands_Academy_of_Arts_and_Sciences) (KNAW) that carries out [neuroscience](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neuroscience) research with special emphasis on the [brain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brain) and [visual system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Visual_system).
categories: Neuroscience research centers in the Netherlands

definition: Network neuroscience is an approach to understanding the structure and function of the [human brain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_brain) through an approach of [network science](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Network_science), through the [paradigm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paradigm) of [graph theory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Graph_theory).

Neural accommodation or neuronal accommodation occurs when a [neuron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neuron) or [muscle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muscle) cell is depolarised by slowly rising current ([ramp depolarisation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ramp_function)) in vitro.

Neural adaptation or sensory adaptation is a gradual decrease over time in the responsiveness of the [sensory system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sensory_system) to a constant [stimulus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stimulus_(physiology)).

Neural backpropagation is the phenomenon in which, after the [action potential](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Action_potential) of a [neuron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neuron) creates a voltage spike down the [axon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Axon) (normal propagation), another impulse is generated from the [soma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soma_(biology)) and propagates towards the [apical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apical_dendrite) portions of the dendritic arbor or [dendrites](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dendrites) (from which much of the original input current originated).

Neural coding (or neural representation) refers to the relationship between a [stimulus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stimulus_(physiology)) and its respective neuronal responses, and the [signalling relationships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electrophysiology) among networks of neurons in an [ensemble](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neuronal_ensemble).
Neural computation is the [information processing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Information_processing_(psychology)) performed by networks of [neuron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neuron)s.

Neural Computation is a monthly [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer-reviewed) [scientific journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_journal) covering all aspects of [neural computation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neural_computation), including modeling the brain and the design and construction of neurally-inspired information processing systems.

neural crest is a ridge-like structure that is formed transiently between the [epidermal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Epidermal) [ectoderm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ectoderm) and [neural plate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neural_plate) during [vertebrate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vertebrate) development.

Neural decoding is a [neuroscience](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neuroscience) field concerned with the hypothetical reconstruction of sensory and other stimuli from information that has already been encoded and represented in the [brain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brain) by [networks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biological_neural_network) of [neurons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neurons).

Neural facilitation, also known as paired-pulse facilitation (PPF), is a phenomenon in [neuroscience](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neuroscience) in which postsynaptic potentials (PSPs) ([EPPs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/End-plate_potential), [EPSPs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Excitatory_postsynaptic_potential) or [IPSPs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inhibitory_postsynaptic_potential)) evoked by an impulse are increased when that impulse closely follows a prior impulse.

neural network (NN) or neural net, is a [computational model](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computational_model) inspired by the structure and functions of [biological neural networks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biological_neural_networks).

neural network, also called a neuronal network, is an interconnected population of [neuron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neuron)s (typically containing multiple [neural circuit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neural_circuit)s).

Neural Plasticity is a [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer_review) [scientific journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_journal) covering all aspects of [neuroplasticity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neuroplasticity), especially when concerning its functional involvement in the regulation of behavior and in [psychopathology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Psychopathology).

term: Neural processing for individual categories of objects
page: Neural processing for individual categories of objects

definition: Neural Regeneration Research is a [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer_review) [scientific journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_journal) covering research on [neuroregeneration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neuroregeneration) and [stem cell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stem_cell)s.
neural spine sail is a large, flattish protrusion from the back of an animal formed of a sequence of extended [[Vertebra#Processes|vertebral spinous processes]] and associated tissues.

neural substrate is a term used in [neuroscience](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neuroscience) to indicate the part of the [central nervous system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_nervous_system) (i.e., [brain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brain) and [spinal cord](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spinal_cord)) that underlies a specific [behavior](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Behavior), [cognitive process](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cognitive_process), or [psychological state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Psychological_state).
Neural synchrony is the correlation of [brain activity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brain_activity) across two or more people over time.
Neural tissue engineering is a specific sub-field of [tissue engineering](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tissue_engineering).
neurite or neuronal process refers to any projection from the [cell body](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_body) of a [neuron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neuron).

Neuro biomechanics is a field dedicated to the general study of human movement from various basic perspectives: musculo-skeletal functional anatomy, CNS and neuro-muscular physiology, physics, control theory with cybernetics and computer science.

Neuro-ophthalmology is an academically-oriented [subspecialty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Subspecialty) that merges the fields of [neurology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neurology) and [ophthalmology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ophthalmology), often dealing with complex systemic diseases that have manifestations in the [visual system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Visual_system).
Neuroangiogenesis is the coordinated growth of nerves and blood vessels.
Neuroanthropology is the study of the relationship between culture and the brain.{{efn | Daniel Lende and Greg Downey recount the origins of a definition of .

Neuroarchaeology is a sub-discipline of [archaeology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Archaeology) that uses neuroscientific data to infer things about [brain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brain) form and function in human cognitive evolution.

Neurobiology of Aging is a [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer_review) monthly [scientific journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_journal) published by [Elsevier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elsevier).

Neurobiology of Disease is a monthly [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer_review) [scientific journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_journal) covering research on disease mechanisms underlying disorders of the [nervous system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nervous_system) and [behavior](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Psychopathology).

Neurobiology of Stress is a [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer-reviewed) [open-access](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Open-access) [scientific journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_journal) covering research on the [neurobiology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neurobiology) of [stress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stress_(biology)).

Neurocardiology is the study of the [neurophysiological](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neurophysiological), [neurological](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neurology) and [neuroanatomical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neuroanatomy) aspects of [cardiology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardiology), including the neurological origins of cardiac disorders.

Neurochemical Research is a monthly [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer_review) [scientific journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_journal) covering [neurochemistry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neurochemistry).

Neurocinema or neurocinematics is the science of how watching movies, or particular scenes from movies affect human [brain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brain)s, and the response the human brain gives to any given movie or scene.

Neurocognitive functions are [cognitive function](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cognitive_function)s closely linked to the integrity of specific [brain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brain) systems—particular [cortical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cerebral_cortex) and subcortical regions, [neural pathway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neural_pathway)s, and large-scale networks—such that disruption of those neural substrates produces characteristic patterns of cognitive impairment.

Neurocomputational speech processing is computer-simulation of [speech production](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Speech_production) and [speech perception](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Speech_perception) by referring to the natural neuronal processes of [speech production](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Speech_production) and [speech perception](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Speech_perception), as they occur in the human [nervous system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nervous_system) ([central nervous system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_nervous_system) and [peripheral nervous system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peripheral_nervous_system)).

Neurocomputing is a [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer-reviewed) [scientific journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_journal) covering research on [artificial intelligence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artificial_intelligence), [machine learning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Machine_learning), and [neural computation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neural_computation).

Neuroconstructivism is a theory that states that phylogenetic developmental processes such as [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene)–gene interaction, [gene–environment interaction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene–environment_interaction) New York |publisher=[Oxford University Press](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oxford_University_Press) |isbn=9780199214822 |oclc=71807817 |doi=10.1093/acprof:oso/9780198529910.001.0001 |pmid=17181703 }} [[Category:Constructivism (psychological school)]] [[Category:Animal developmental biology]]

Neurocriminology is an emerging sub-discipline of [biocriminology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biocriminology) and [criminology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Criminology) that applies [brain imaging](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brain_imaging) techniques and principles from [neuroscience](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neuroscience) to understand, predict, and prevent crime.

Neurocristopathy is a diverse class of pathologies that may arise from defects in the development of tissues containing cells commonly derived from the embryonic [neural crest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neural_crest) cell lineage.
Neurodevelopmental framework for learning, like all frameworks, is an organizing structure through which learners and learning can be understood.

Neuroenhancement or cognitive enhancement is the experimental use of [pharmacological](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pharmacological) or non-pharmacological methods intended to [improve](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_enhancement) [cognitive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cognition) and [affective](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Affect_(psychology)) abilities in healthy people who don't have any [mental illness](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mental_disorder).

Neuroepidemiology is a science of [incidence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Incidence_(epidemiology)), [prevalence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prevalence), [risk factor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Risk_factor)s, [natural history](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Natural_history_of_disease) and [prognosis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prognosis) of neurological disorders, as well as of experimental neuroepidemiology, which is research based on [clinical trial](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clinical_trial)s of effectiveness or efficacy of various interventions in neurological disorders.

Neuroepigenetics is the study of how [epigenetic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Epigenetic) changes to [genes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genes) affect the [nervous system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nervous_system).
Neuroergonomics is the application of [neuroscience](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neuroscience) to [ergonomics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ergonomics).

Neuroethics Research Unit was created in 2006, at the [[:fr:Institut de recherches cliniques de Montréal|Institut de recherches cliniques de Montréal]] (IRCM), which is affiliated to the [Université de Montréal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Université_de_Montréal).

Neurogastronomy is the study of [flavor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flavor_(taste)) [perception](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Perception) and the ways it affects [cognition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cognition) and [memory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Memory).

Neurogenesis is the process by which [nervous system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nervous_system) cells, the [neuron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neuron)s, are produced by [neural stem cell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neural_stem_cell)s (NSCs).

nuclear localization sequence, or signal (NLS) is an [amino acid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amino_acid) [sequence motif](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sequence_motif) that 'tags' a protein for import into the [cell nucleus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_nucleus) by [nuclear transport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nuclear_transport).

nuclear matrix is the network of [fibres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fibres) found throughout the inside of a [cell nucleus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_nucleus) after a specific method of chemical extraction.
nuclear pore complex (NPC) is a large [protein complex](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein_complex) giving rise to the nuclear pore.

Nuclear Receptor Signaling Atlas (NURSA) was a United States [National Institutes of Health](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Institutes_of_Health)-funded research consortium focused on [nuclear receptors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nuclear_receptors) and [nuclear receptor coregulators](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transcription_coregulator).

nuclear run-on assay is conducted to identify the [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene)s that are being [transcribed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transcription_(genetics)) at a certain time point.
Nuclear sexing is a technique for genetic [sex determination](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sexing) in those species where XX chromosome pair is present.

Nuclear transport refers to the mechanisms by which [molecule](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Molecule)s move across the [nuclear membrane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nuclear_membrane) of a [cell's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_(biology)) [nucleus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_nucleus).

Nuclease protection assay is a laboratory technique used in [biochemistry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biochemistry) and [genetics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetics) to identify individual [RNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RNA) molecules in a heterogeneous RNA sample extracted from [cells](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_(biology)).

Nucleic acid analogues are compounds which are [structurally analogous](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Structural_analog) to naturally occurring [RNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RNA) and [DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA), through substitutions of any of its sugar, phosphate, and nucleobase components.

hybridization (or hybridisation) is a phenomenon in which single-stranded deoxyribonucleic acid ([DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA)) or ribonucleic acid ([RNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RNA)) molecules [[Nucleic acid thermodynamics#Annealing|anneal]] to [complementary DNA or RNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Complementarity_(molecular_biology)).

Nucleic acid methods are the techniques used to study [nucleic acid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nucleic_acid)s: [DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA) and [RNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RNA).

Nucleic acid secondary structure is the [basepair](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basepair)ing interactions within a single [nucleic acid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nucleic_acid) polymer or between two polymers.

Nucleic acid structure refers to the [structure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biomolecular_structure) of [nucleic acid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nucleic_acid)s such as [DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA) and [RNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RNA).
Nucleic acid tertiary structure is the [[Biomolecular structure#Tertiary structure|three-dimensional shape]] of a [nucleic acid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nucleic_acid) polymer.

nucleic acid test (NAT) is a technique used to directly detect a specific [nucleic acid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nucleic_acid) sequence, usually to detect and identify a particular species or subspecies of organism, often a [virus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virus) or [bacterium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bacterium) that acts as a [pathogen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pathogen) in [blood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blood), [tissue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tissue_(biology)), [urine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urine), etc.

Nucleic acid thermodynamics is the study of how [temperature](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Temperature) affects the [nucleic acid structure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nucleic_acid_structure) of double-stranded [DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA) (dsDNA).

Nucleofection is an [electroporation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electroporation)-based [transfection](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transfection) method which enables transfer of [nucleic acids](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nucleic_acids) such as [DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA) and [RNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RNA) into [cells](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_(biology)) by applying a specific voltage and reagents.

nucleoid (meaning [nucleus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_nucleus)-like) is an irregularly shaped region within the [prokaryotic cell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prokaryote) that contains all or most of the [genetic material](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genome).

Nucleolus organizer regions ([American English](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_English)) or nucleolus organiser regions ([British English](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_English)) (NORs) are [chromosomal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chromosome) regions crucial for the formation of the [nucleolus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nucleolus).
Nucleomodulins are a family of bacterial proteins that enter the nucleus of [eukaryotic cells](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eukaryotic_Cells).

Nucleomorphs are small, vestigial eukaryotic [nuclei](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_nucleus) found between the inner and outer pairs of membranes in certain [plastid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plastid)s.

nucleoside-modified messenger RNA (modRNA) is a synthetic [messenger RNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Messenger_RNA) (mRNA) in which some [nucleoside](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nucleoside)s are replaced by other naturally modified nucleosides or by synthetic [nucleoside analogue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nucleoside_analogue)s.
nucleosome is the basic structural unit of [DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA) packaging in [eukaryotes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eukaryotes).

Nucleosome Remodeling Factor (NURF) is an ATP-dependent chromatin remodeling complex first discovered in [Drosophila melanogaster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drosophila_melanogaster) (fruit fly) that catalyzes [nucleosome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nucleosome) sliding in order to regulate gene [transcription](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transcription_(biology)).
Nucleosome repeat length (NRL) is the average distance between the centers of neighboring [nucleosomes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nucleosomes).

Nuffield Council on Bioethics is a UK-based independent [charitable body](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charitable_organization), which examines and reports on [bioethical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bioethical) issues raised by new advances in biological and [medical research](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medical_research).

Paleoanthropology or paleo-anthropology is a branch of [paleontology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paleontology) and [anthropology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biological_anthropology) which seeks to understand the early development of [anatomically modern human](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anatomically_modern_human)s, a process known as [[wikt:hominization|hominization]], through the reconstruction of evolutionary [kinship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kinship) lines within the family [Hominidae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hominidae), working from biological evidence (such as [petrified](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Petrified) skeletal remains, [bone fragments](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fossil), footprints) and cultural evidence (such as [stone tool](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stone_tool)s, artifacts, and settlement localities).

Paleobiology (or palaeobiology) is an [interdisciplinary field](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interdisciplinary_field) that combines the methods and findings found in both the [earth sciences](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Earth_sciences) and the [life sciences](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Life_sciences).

Paleobotany or palaeobotany, also known as paleophytology, is the branch of [botany](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Botany) dealing with the recovery and identification of [plant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plant) [fossil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fossil)s from [geological](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geology) contexts, and their use for the biological reconstruction of past environments ([paleogeography](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palaeogeography)), and the [evolutionary history of plants](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evolutionary_history_of_plants), with a bearing upon the [evolution of life](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evolution_of_life) in general.

Paleoecology or palaeoecology is the study of interactions between organisms and/or interactions between organisms and their environments across [geologic timescale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geologic_timescale)s.
Paleoethnobotany (also spelled palaeoethnobotany), or archaeobotany, is the study of past human-plant interactions through the recovery and analysis of ancient plant remains.

Paleoneurobiology is the study of [brain evolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brain_evolution) by analysis of brain [endocast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Endocast)s to determine [endocranial](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Endocranium) traits and volumes.
Paleontological Society, formerly the Paleontological Society of America, is an international organisation devoted to the promotion of [paleontology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paleontology).
Paleontology or palaeontology is the scientific study of the life of the past, mainly but not exclusively through the study of [fossils](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fossils).

Paleopathology, also spelled palaeopathology, is the study of ancient [diseases](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diseases) and [injuries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Injuries) in [organism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organism)s through the examination of [fossil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fossil)s, [mummified tissue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mummy), [skeletal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skeletal) remains, and analysis of [coprolite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coprolite)s.

Paleophycology (also once known as paleoalgology) is the subdiscipline of [paleobotany](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paleobotany) that deals with the study and identification of [fossil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fossil) [algae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Algae) and their evolutionary relationships and ecology.
Paleopolyploidy is the result of [genome duplications](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genome_duplications) which occurred at least several million years ago (MYA).
Paleosalinity (or palaeosalinity) is the salinity of the global ocean or of an [ocean basin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ocean_basin) at a point in geological history.
