Pharmacogene Variation Consortium (abbreviated as PhamVar) is an international group of experts that maintains a systematic nomenclature system for [allelic variation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Allele)s of genes that affect the [metabolism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drug_metabolism) of drugs.

Pharmacometabolomics, also known as pharmacometabonomics, is a field which stems from [metabolomics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metabolomics), the quantification and analysis of [metabolites](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metabolites) produced by the body.

Pharming, a [portmanteau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portmanteau) of farming and [pharmaceutical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pharmaceutical), refers to the use of [genetic engineering](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetic_engineering) to insert [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene)s that code for useful pharmaceuticals into host animals or plants that would otherwise not express those genes, thus creating a [genetically modified organism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetically_modified_organism) (GMO).

pharyngeal arches, also known as visceral arches, are transient structures seen in the [embryonic development](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Animal_embryonic_development) of [human](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human)s and other [vertebrate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vertebrate)s, that are recognisable precursors for many structures.
pharyngeal artery is a branch of the [ascending pharyngeal artery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ascending_pharyngeal_artery).
Pharyngeal jaws are a is depicted with a pharyngeal jaw.
Pharyngeal slits are [filter-feeding](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filter_feeder) organs found among [deuterostome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deuterostome)s.

Pharyngeal teeth are [teeth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Teeth) in the [pharyngeal arch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pharyngeal_arch) of the throat of [cyprinid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cyprinid)s, [sucker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catostomidae)s, and a number of other [fish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fish) species otherwise lacking openly visible teeth.
pharyngula is a stage in the [embryo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Embryo)nic development of vertebrates.

pharynx (: pharynges) is the part of the [throat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Throat) behind the [mouth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_mouth) and [nasal cavity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nasal_cavity), and above the [esophagus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Esophagus) and [trachea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trachea) (the tubes going down to the [stomach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stomach) and the [lung](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lung)s respectively).

Phase resetting in neurons is a behavior observed in different [biological oscillators](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oscillators) and plays a role in creating neural synchronization as well as different processes within the body.
Phasgonophora sulcata is a species of chalcidid wasp in the family [Chalcididae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chalcididae).
Phasmids are [sensilla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sensilla) in the lateral tail region of certain species of [nematode](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nematode)s.

phememe (from Ancient Greek [[wikt:φημί]] ‘I speak, say’) is a hypothesized [speech sound](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Speech_sound) with an abstract [gestural](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gesture) meaning, proposed by the linguist [Mary LeCron Foster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mary_LeCron_Foster).

phene is an individual genetically determined characteristic or [trait](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trait_(biology)) which can be possessed by an [organism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organism), such as eye colour, height, behavior, tooth shape or any other observable characteristic.

phenetics (; ), also known as taximetrics, is an attempt to classify organisms based on overall similarity, usually with respect to [morphology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morphology_(biology)) or other observable traits, regardless of their [phylogeny](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phylogeny) or evolutionary relation.
Phenice method is a technique of determining the sex of a [human skeleton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_skeleton) from the innominate [pelvis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pelvis).

phenocopy is a variation in [phenotype](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phenotype) (generally referring to a single [trait](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trait_(biological))) which is caused by environmental conditions (often, but not necessarily, during the organism's [development](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Developmental_biology)), such that the organism's phenotype matches a phenotype which is determined by [genetic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetics) factors.
Phenol extraction is a laboratory technique that purifies [nucleic acid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nucleic_acid) samples using a [phenol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phenol) solution.

Phenology is the study of periodic events in [biological life cycle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biological_life_cycle)s and how these are influenced by [seasonal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seasonality) and interannual variations in [climate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Climate), as well as [habitat factors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Environmental_factor) (such as [elevation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elevation)).

Phenoloxidase system is a major defense system in many [invertebrates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Invertebrate) which ultimately leads to [melanization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Melanization) of pathogens and damaged tissues.

Phenol–chloroform extraction is a [liquid-liquid extraction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liquid-liquid_extraction) technique in [molecular biology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Molecular_biology) used to separate [nucleic acid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nucleic_acid)s from [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein)s and [lipids](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lipids).
PhenomicDB is a free [phenotype](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phenotype) oriented [database](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Database).

Phenoscape is a project to develop a [database](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Database) of phenotype data for species across the [Ostariophysi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ostariophysi), a large group of [teleost fish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Teleost_fish).
phenotype () is the set of observable characteristics or [traits](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phenotypic_trait) of an [organism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organism).
phenotype microarray approach is a technology for [high-throughput phenotyping](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phenomics) of cells.
Phenotype modification is the process of experimentally altering an organism's [phenotype](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phenotype) to investigate the impact of phenotype on the fitness.

Phenotypic heterogeneity describes different mutations in the same [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene) that can sometimes give rise to strikingly different [phenotype](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phenotype)s.
Phenotypic integration is a metric for measuring the correlation of multiple functionally-related traits to each other.
Phenotypic plasticity refers to some of the changes in an [organism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organism)'s behavior, morphology and physiology in response to a unique environment.

Phenotypic response surfaces (PRS) is an [artificial intelligence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artificial_intelligence)-guided [personalized medicine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Personalized_medicine) platform that relies on [combinatorial optimization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Combinatorial_optimization) principles to quantify [drug interaction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drug_interaction)s and [efficacies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Efficacy_(pharmacology)) to develop optimized [combination therapies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Combination_therapy) to treat a broad spectrum of illnesses.

Physical Biology is a [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer_review) [scientific journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_journal) published by [IOP Publishing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IOP_Publishing) covering a range of fields that bridge the biological and physical sciences, including [biophysics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biophysics), [systems biology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Systems_biology), [population dynamics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Population_dynamics), etc.
Physical literacy is the ability to move with competence and confidence in a wide variety of physical activities in multiple environments that benefit the healthy development of the whole person.

Physical map is a technique used in [molecular biology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Molecular_biology) to find the order and physical distance between [DNA base pairs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Base_pair) by [DNA markers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetic_marker).
Physics of life is a branch of [physics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Physics) that studies the fundamental principles governing living systems.

Physiologia Plantarum is a [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer_review) [scientific journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_journal) published by [Wiley-Blackwell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wiley-Blackwell) on behalf of the [Scandinavian Plant Physiology Society](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scandinavian_Plant_Physiology_Society).

Physiological condition is a term used in [biology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biology), [biochemistry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biochemistry), and [medicine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medicine).

Physiological density, also known as real population density, is defined as the [number of people](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Population_(human_biology)) per unit area of [arable land](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arable_land).
Physiological functional capacity (PFC) is the ability to perform the physical tasks of [daily life](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daily_life) and the ease with which these tasks can be performed.

physiological prematurity (also described as [altriciality](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Altriciality)) refers to the fact that compared to most animals, humans are born in a premature biological state.

Physiological psychology is a subdivision of [behavioral neuroscience](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Behavioral_neuroscience) (biological psychology) that studies the neural mechanisms of [perception](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Perception) and behavior through direct manipulation of the brains of nonhuman animal subjects in [controlled experiments](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_control).

Physiological Reports is a [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer-reviewed) [open access](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Open_access) [online](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Online_and_offline)-only [scientific journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_journal) covering original research in all areas of [physiology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Physiology).
Physiological Reviews is a journal published quarterly by the [American Physiological Society](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Physiological_Society) which has been published since 1921.

term: Physiological Society Annual Review Prize Lecture
page: Physiological Society Annual Review Prize Lecture
definition: Physiology Society Annual Review Prize Lecture is an award conferred by [The Physiological Society](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Physiological_Society).

media.file: Claude Bernard and his pupils. Oil painting after Léon-Augus Wellcome V0017769.jpg

definition: Physiology is a [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer_review) [scientific journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_journal) on [physiology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Physiology) published by the [American Physiological Society](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Physiological_Society) and the [International Union of Physiological Societies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Union_of_Physiological_Societies).
physiology of decompression is the aspect of physiology which is affected by exposure to large changes in [ambient pressure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ambient_pressure).

media.file: Leszek Czarnecki wyprawa na Atol Bikini 2006.JPG

definition: physiology of marathons is typically associated with high demands on a [marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marathon) [runner's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Running) [cardiovascular system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardiovascular_system) and their [locomotor system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_musculoskeletal_system).

physiology of underwater diving is the physiological adaptations to diving of air-breathing [vertebrates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vertebrate) that have returned to the ocean from terrestrial lineages.
physiome of an individual's or [species](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Species)' [physiological](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Physiology) state is the description of its functional behavior.
related: List of omics topics in biology

definition: physiotope is the total [abiotic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abiotic) matrix of [habitat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Habitat) present within any certain [ecotope](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ecotope).
Physogastrism or physogastry is a characteristic of certain arthropods (mostly insects and mites), where the abdomen is greatly enlarged and membranous.
Physostomes are fishes that have a pneumatic duct connecting the [gas bladder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gas_bladder) to the [alimentary canal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alimentary_canal).

media.file: Biofilm épais bactéries filamenteuses cyanophycées Authie 7 aout 2017a.jpg

definition: phytobiome consists of a [plant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plant) (phyto) situated in its specific ecological area ([biome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biome)), including its environment and the associated [communities](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Community_(ecology)) of [organism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organism)s which inhabit it.
Phytochemistry is the study of [phytochemical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phytochemical)s, which are chemicals derived from [plant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plant)s.

Phytochemistry is a [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer_review) [scientific journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_journal) covering pure and applied plant chemistry, plant biochemistry and molecular biology.
Phytochory is animal transportation and dispersal where plants as a whole, or parts of their body play an important direct role in animal transportation and dispersal.
phytodetritus is the organic particulate matter resulting from [phytoplankton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phytoplankton) and other organic material in surface waters falling to the seabed.
Phytoecdysteroids are plant-derived [ecdysteroid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ecdysteroid)s.

PhytoKeys is a [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer-reviewed) [open-access](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Open-access) [scientific journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_journal) covering [systematic botany](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Systematic_botany).

Phytologia is an [open-access journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Open-access_journal) to expedite [plant systematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plant_systematics), [phytogeographical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phytogeography) and [ecological](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ecology) publication, focused on North America.
Phytomers are functional units of a plant, continually produced by root and shoot [meristem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meristem)s throughout a plant's vegetative life-cycle.

Phytophthora infestans is an [oomycete](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oomycete) or water mold, a [fungus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fungus)-like [microorganism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microorganism) ([oomycete](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oomycete)) that causes the serious [potato](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Potato) and [tomato](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tomato) [disease](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disease) known as late blight or potato blight.

Phytoplankton () are the [autotroph](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Autotroph)ic (self-feeding) components of the [plankton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plankton) community and a key part of ocean and freshwater [ecosystems](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aquatic_ecosystem).
Phytosemiotics is a branch of [biosemiotics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biosemiotics) that studies the [sign processing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Semiosis) capabilities present in plants.
Phytosociology, also known as phytocoenology or simply plant sociology, is the study of groups of species of plant that are usually found together.

Phytotaxa is a [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer_review) [scientific journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_journal) for rapid publication on any aspect of [systematic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Systematics) [botany](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Botany).
Phytotelma (plural phytotelmata) is a small water-filled cavity in a terrestrial plant.
Phytotope refers to the total habitat available for colonization by plants within a specific biotope, such as a forest, meadow, wetland, or urban green space.

Phytozome is an online [bioinformatics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bioinformatics) [database](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Database) and comparative genomics platform that provides access to sequenced plant and green algal genomes.

PI (or photosynthesis-irradiance) curve is a graphical representation of the [empirical relationship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Empirical_relationship) between [solar irradiance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Solar_irradiance) and [photosynthesis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Photosynthesis).

Piaget's theory of cognitive development, or his [genetic epistemology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetic_epistemology), is a comprehensive theory about the nature and development of human [intelligence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intelligence).

Picocyanobacteria are [cyanobacteria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cyanobacteria) that are part of the [picoplankton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Picoplankton), which is the fraction of [plankton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plankton) composed by [cells](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_(biology)) between 0.2 and 2 μm.

Picoeukaryotes are [picoplankton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Picoplankton)ic [eukaryotic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eukaryote) organisms 3.0 == See also == * [Bacterioplankton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bacterioplankton) * [List of eukaryotic picoplankton species](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_eukaryotic_picoplankton_species) * [Phytoplankton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phytoplankton) * [Picocyanobacteria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Picocyanobacteria) * [Picozoa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Picozoa) == Notes == ==External links== *[http://microbewiki.kenyon.edu/index.php/Nano-_and_Picoeukaryotes MicrobeWiki] A site on a biology Wiki run by Kenyon College [[Category:Mic

Picoplankton is the fraction of [plankton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plankton) composed by [cells](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_(biology)) between 0.2 and 2 μm that can be either prokaryotic and eukaryotic phototrophs and heterotrophs: * [photosynthetic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Photosynthetic) * [heterotrophic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heterotrophic) They are prevalent amongst microbial plankton communities of both freshwater and marine ecosystems.

term: Picower Institute for Learning and Memory
page: Picower Institute for Learning and Memory
definition: Picower Institute for Learning and Memory is one of the three [neuroscience](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neuroscience) groups at [MIT](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MIT) along with the [McGovern Institute for Brain Research](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McGovern_Institute_for_Brain_Research) and the Department of Brain and [Cognitive Science](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cognitive_Science)s.
categories: Neuroscience research centers in the United States

definition: piebald or pied animal is one that has a pattern of unpigmented spots (white) on a pigmented background of hair, feathers or scales.

categories: Fellows of the International Society for Computational Biology
Members of the European Molecular Biology Organization

definition: Pig-a gene mutation assay is a [flow cytometry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flow_cytometry)-based method for detecting mammalian cells that have inactivating [mutation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mutation)s in the endogenous X-linked reporter gene called [phosphatidyl inositolglycan class A gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PIGA) (PIG-A in humans and non-human primates, Pig-a in other mammalian species).
Pigeon toe, also known as in-toeing, is a condition which causes the toes to point inward when walking.
pigment spot ocellus is an [ocellus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ocellus) that contains only part of its cells pigmented.
Pignet Index or Body Build Index is an index used for evaluation of body build.

pileipellis is the uppermost layer of [hyphae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hyphae) in the [pileus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pileus_(mycology)) of a [fungal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fungal) [fruit body](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basidiocarp).
Pileup format is a text-based [format](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File_format) for summarizing the base calls of aligned reads to a reference sequence.

pileus (: pilei) is the cap or cap-like part of a [basidiocarp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basidiocarp) or ascocarp ([fungal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fungal) [fruiting body](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fruiting_body)) that supports a spore-bearing surface, the hymenium.

pilot Polder Andijk, or Test Polder Andijk, Proefpolder Andijk in Dutch, is a [polder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polder) established in 1926 - 1927 in the Zuiderzee near the village of [Andijk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andijk).
pin feather is a developing [feather](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Feather) on a [bird](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bird).

media.file: A nestling of rock dove with pin feathers.jpg

definition: Pinacocytes are flat [cells](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_(biology)) found on the outside of [sponges](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sponge), as well as the internal canals of a sponge.

pinacoderm is the outermost layer of body cells ([pinacocytes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pinacocytes)) of organisms of the phylum [Porifera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Porifera) (sponges), equivalent to the [epidermis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Epidermis_(skin)) in other animals.

categories: Fellows of the American Institute for Medical and Biological Engineering

definition: Pindorama Biological Reserve () is a [biological reserve](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biological_reserve_(Brazil)) in the state of [São Paulo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/São_Paulo_(state)), Brazil.

pineal gland (also called the pineal body) is a small [endocrine gland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Endocrine_gland) in the [brain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brain) of most [vertebrate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vertebrate)s.
Pink algae is a growth of pink, slimey [bacteria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bacteria)l matter which can sometimes occur in pools and laboratory equipment.
Pioneer axon is the classification given to [axons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Axons) that are the first to grow in a particular region.

pioneer neuron is a cell that is a derivative of the [[Corticogenesis#Cortical plates and zones |preplate]] in the early stages of [corticogenesis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corticogenesis) of the brain.

pioneer organism, also called a disaster taxon, is an [organism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organism) that [colonize](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colonisation_(biology))s a previously empty area first, or one that repopulates vacant [niche](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ecological_niche)s after a [natural disaster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Natural_disaster), [mass extinction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mass_extinction) or any other catastrophic event that wipes out most life of the prior [biome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biome).

Pioneer species are resilient [species](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Species) that are the first to [colonize](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colonisation_(biology)) barren [environments](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Natural_environment), or to repopulate disrupted [biodiverse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biodiversity) [steady-state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steady-state) [ecosystem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ecosystem)s as part of [ecological succession](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ecological_succession).

media.file: Plants Colonizing a Lava Flow on Hawaii.jpg

definition: pipeflow is a type of [[wiktionary:subterranean|subterranean]] water flow where water travels along cracks in the soil or old root systems found in above ground [vegetation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vegetation).

Pirbright Institute (formerly the Institute for Animal Health) is a [research institute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Research_institute) in [Surrey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Surrey), England, dedicated to the study of [infectious disease](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Infectious_disease)s of [farm animals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Livestock).
related: Biotechnology and Biological Sciences Research Council

definition: Pit and mounds are small, persistent microtopographical features that present themselves after a disturbance event occurs and uproots trees via [windthrow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Windthrow).

Pith, or medulla, is a [tissue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tissue_(biology)) in the [stem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plant_stem)s of [vascular plant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vascular_plant)s.

Pitlochry fish ladder is a [fish ladder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fish_ladder) next to the Pitlochry Power Station, near [Pitlochry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pitlochry), [Perth and Kinross](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Perth_and_Kinross), Scotland, which allows [salmon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salmon) to travel upstream during the breeding season.

Proximity ligation-assisted chromatin immunoprecipitation sequencing (PLAC-seq) is a [chromatin conformation capture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chromosome_conformation_capture)(3C)-based technique to detect and quantify genomic [chromatin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chromatin) structure from a protein-centric approach.

placenta (: placentas or placentae) is a temporary [embryo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Embryo)nic and later [fetal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fetus) [organ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organ_(biology)) that begins [developing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Embryonic_development) from the [blastocyst](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blastocyst) shortly after [implantation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Implantation_(embryology)).

plagiaulacoid is a type of blade-like, most often serrated, [tooth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tooth) present in various [mammal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mammal) groups, usually a [premolar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Premolar).

plait is an anatomical feature which is present on the [shells](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gastropod_shell) of some [snail](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Snail)s, or [gastropod](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gastropod)s.

Planar cell polarity (PCP) is a type of [cell polarity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_polarity) in which the [cells](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_(biology)) are oriented in a coordinated way across the plane of an [epithelial tissue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Epithelium).

media.file: Cartoon representation of Planar polarity in fly and mouse epithelia.png

definition: Planet Simulator, also known as a Planetary Simulator, is a [climate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Climate)-controlled [simulation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simulation) chamber designed to aid in the study of the [origin of life](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abiogenesis).

planidium is a specialized form of [insect](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Insect) [larva](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Larva) seen in the first-[instar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Instar) of a few families of insects that have [parasitoid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parasitoid)al ways of life.

planktivore is an aquatic organism that feeds on [plankton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plankton)ic food, including [zooplankton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zooplankton) and [phytoplankton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phytoplankton).

Planktology is the [study](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Research) of [plankton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plankton), various small drifting plants, animals and [microorganism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microorganism)s that inhabit bodies of [water](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Water).
Plant anatomy or phytotomy is the general term for the study of the internal structure of [plant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plant)s.
Plant bioacoustics refers to the creation of sound waves by plants.

Plant breeders' rights (PBR), also known as plant variety rights (PVR), are rights granted in certain places to the [breeder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plant_breeding) of a new [variety](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plant_variety_(law)) of plant that give the breeder [exclusive control](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Exclusive_right) over the propagating material (including [seed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seed), cuttings, divisions, tissue culture) and harvested material ([cut flowers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cut_flowers), fruit, foliage) of a new variety for a number of years.
[Plant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plant) breeding is the science of changing the traits of [plants](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plants) in order to produce desired characteristics.

Plant cells are the [cells](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_(biology)) present in [green plants](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Viridiplantae), photosynthetic [eukaryote](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eukaryote)s of the kingdom [Plant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plant)ae.
plant cover, which is the relative area covered by different plant species in a small plot.

plant cuticle is a protecting film covering the outermost skin layer ([epidermis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Epidermis_(botany))) of [leaves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leaf), young shoots and other aerial plant organs (aerial here meaning all plant parts not embedded in soil or other substrate) that have no [[Bark (botany)#Periderm|periderm]].

Plant defense against herbivory or host-plant resistance is a range of [adaptation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adaptation)s [evolved](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evolution) by [plants](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plants) which improve their [survival and reproduction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fitness_(biology)) by reducing the impact of [herbivore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Herbivore)s.
Plant density is the number of individual plants present per unit of ground area.

definition: plant development are [buds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buds), [shoot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shoot_(botany))s, [root](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Root)s, [leaves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leaf), and [flower](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flower)s; [plant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plant)s produce these tissues and structures throughout their life from [meristem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meristem)s ==References== [[Category:Plant development| ]] [[Category:Botany|Development]] nsf4uk1hxrg6rp6cnjdv6axbfh2wkui

Plant DNA C-values Database (https://cvalues.science.kew.org/) is a comprehensive catalogue of [C-value](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C-value) ([nuclear](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_nucleus) [DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA) content, or in [diploid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diploid)s, [genome size](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genome_size)) data for [land plants](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Embryophyte) and [algae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Algae).

Plant ecology is a subdiscipline of [ecology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ecology) that studies the distribution and [abundance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abundance_(ecology)) of [plant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plant)s, the effects of [environmental factor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Environmental_factor)s upon the abundance of plants, q=plant+ecology | title=Plant Ecology | publisher=Blackwell Scientific Publications | orig-date=1986| year=1997 | access-date=April 24, 2012 | author=Crawley, Michael J.| isbn=978-0-632-03639-

definition: Plant Ecology is a [scientific journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_journal) on [plant ecology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plant_ecology), formerly known as Vegetatio, a journal whose editors resigned in protest of high pricing.

Plant Ecology and Evolution is a triannual [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer-reviewed) [open access](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Open_access) [scientific journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_journal) covering [ecology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ecology), [phylogenetics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phylogenetics), and [systematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Systematics) of plants (including [algae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Algae), [fungi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fungus), and [slime mold](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slime_mold)s), including related fields such as comparative and developmental morphology, [conservation biology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conservation_biology), [evolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evolution), [phytogeography](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phytogeography), [reproductive biology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reproductive_biology), [population genetics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Population_genetics), and vegetation studies.
Plant evolution is the subset of [evolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evolution)ary phenomena that concern [plants](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plants).
Plant Genetic Systems (PGS), since 2002 part of [Bayer CropScience](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bayer_CropScience), is a biotech company located in Ghent, Belgium.

media.file: Marc van Montagu and Jozef Schell.jpg

definition: Plant genetics is the study of [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene)s, [genetic variation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetic_variation), and [heredity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heredity) in [plant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plant)s.

plant genome assembly represents the complete [genomic sequence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genome) of a [plant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plant) species, which is assembled into [chromosome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chromosome)s and other [organelle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organelle)s by using [DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA) (deoxyribonucleic acid) fragments that are obtained from different types of [sequencing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA_sequencing) technology.

Plant growth analysis refers to a set of concepts and equations by which changes in size of [plant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plant)s over time can be summarised and dissected in component variables.

Plant Heritage, formerly known as the National Council for the Conservation of Plants and Gardens (NCCPG), is a [registered charity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charitable_organisation) and a botanical conservation organisation in the United Kingdom.

Plant litter (also leaf litter, tree litter, soil litter, litterfall, or duff) is dead [plant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plant) material (such as [leaves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leaf), [bark](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bark_(botany)), [needles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Needle_(botany)), [twig](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twig)s, and [cladode](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cladode)s) that has fallen to the ground.
Plant morphology or phytomorphology is the study of the physical form and external structure of plants.
Plant nucleus movement is the movement of the [cell nucleus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_nucleus) in plants by the [cytoskeleton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cytoskeleton).

Plant nutrition is the study of the [chemical element](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chemical_element)s and [compounds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chemical_compound) necessary for plant growth and reproduction, plant metabolism and their external supply.
categories: Biology and pharmacology of chemical elements

definition: Plant Pathology is a [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer_review) [scientific journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_journal) published by [Wiley-Blackwell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wiley-Blackwell) in association with the [British Society for Plant Pathology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Society_for_Plant_Pathology).

Plant perception is the ability of [plant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plant)s to sense and respond to the environment by adjusting their [morphology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plant_morphology) and [physiology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plant_physiology).

Plant physiology is a subdiscipline of [botany](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Botany) concerned with the functioning, or [physiology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Physiology), of [plant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plant)s.

Plant Physiology is a monthly [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer-reviewed) scientific journal covering research in [plant physiology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plant_physiology), [biochemistry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biochemistry), [cell biology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_biology), [molecular biology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Molecular_biology), [genetics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetics), [biophysics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biophysics), and [environmental biology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Environmental_biology) of plants.

plant press is a piece of equipment used by [botanist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Botanist)s to flatten and dry [specimens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biological_specimen) so that they can be preserved in [herbaria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Herbaria).

Plant Proteome Database is a [National Science Foundation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Science_Foundation)-funded project to determine the biological function of each [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) in [plant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plant)s.
Plant root exudates are fluids emitted through the roots of plants.
Plant [senescence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Senescence) is the process of aging in plants.
stem is one of two main structural axes of a [vascular plant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vascular_plant), the other being the [root](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Root).

media.file: Translocation from the source to the sink within the phloem.svg

definition: Plant stress measurement is the [quantification](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantification_(science)) of environmental effects on plant health.

media.file: Classes of stresses that plants are exposed to.jpg

definition: Plant Systematics and Evolution is a biannual [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer-reviewed) [scientific journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_journal) covering [systematic botany](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Systematic_botany) and [evolutionary biology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evolutionary_biology).
Tolerance is the ability of plants to mitigate the negative [fitness](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fitness_(biology)) effects caused by [herbivory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Herbivory).

Plant transformation vectors are [plasmid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plasmid)s that have been specifically designed to facilitate the generation of [transgenic plants](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transgenic_plants).

term: Plant use of endophytic fungi in defense
page: Plant use of endophytic fungi in defense

definition: Plant variety is a legal term, following the [International Union for the Protection of New Varieties of Plants](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Union_for_the_Protection_of_New_Varieties_of_Plants) (UPOV) Convention.

media.file: Trend in plant variety applications worldwide 2008-2022.png

related: International Union for the Protection of New Varieties of Plants

definition: Plant viruses are [virus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virus)es that have the potential to affect [plant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plant)s.

Plant-growth promoting fungi (PGPF) are a diverse and heterogeneous group of [non-pathogenic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nonpathogenic_organisms), filamentous, [soil-borne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soil_borne_pathogen) [fungi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fungus) that colonize plant roots, particularly in the [rhizosphere](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhizosphere), and have a positive or [mutualistic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mutualism_(biology)) effect on plant health and development.
Induced systemic resistance (ISR) is a resistance mechanism in [plant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plant)s that is activated by [infection](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Infection).

Planta is a monthly [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer-reviewed) [scientific journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_journal) covering all areas of [plant biology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plant_biology).

Plantationocene is a proposed theoretical framework describing the ways in which the [plantation system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plantation) established in the Americas during early [settler-colonialism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Settler_colonialism) continues to shape the world and the environment today.

planted motif search (PMS) also known as a (l, d)-motif search (LDMS) is a method for identifying conserved [motifs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sequence_motif) within a set of [nucleic acid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nucleic_acid_sequence) or [peptide sequence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peptide_sequence)s.

Plants is a [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer-reviewed) [open-access](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Open-access) [scientific journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_journal) that covers various areas of [plant biology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plant_biology), including [cellular biology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cellular_biology), [molecular biology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Molecular_biology), [genetics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetics), and [ecology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ecology).

Plants For A Future (PFAF) is an online [not for profit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_for_profit) resource for those interested in edible and useful plants, with a focus on [temperate region](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Temperate_region)s.

Plants, People, Planet is a bimonthly [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer-reviewed) [scientific journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_journal) which focuses on [plant science](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plant_science), and the links between plant science and [society](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Society) in particular.
plantsman is an enthusiastic and knowledgeable gardener (amateur or professional), [nurseryman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nursery_(horticulture)) or nurserywoman.
Plant-animal interactions are important pathways for the transfer of energy within ecosystems, where both advantageous and unfavorable interactions support ecosystem health.

Plant–fungus horizontal gene transfer is the movement of [genetic material](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetic_material) between individuals in the [plant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plant) and [fungus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fungus) [kingdoms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingdom_(biology)).

Plant–soil feedback is a process where plants alter the [biotic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biotic_component) and [abiotic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abiotic_component) qualities of [soil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soil) they grow in, which then alters the ability of plants to grow in that soil in the future.

planula is the free-swimming, flattened, [ciliated](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cilium), [[symmetry (biology)#Bilateral symmetry|bilaterally symmetric]] [larval form](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Larva) of various [cnidaria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cnidaria)n species and some species of [Ctenophores](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ctenophora), which are not closely related to cnidarians.
Plaque hybridization is a technique used in [Molecular biology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Molecular_biology) for the identification of [recombinant phages](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phages).

plasma membrane monoamine transporter (PMAT) is a low-affinity [monoamine transporter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monoamine_transporter) [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) which in humans is encoded by the SLC29A4 [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).
Plasmagene is a term used to describe genetic elements that exist outside of the nucleus, typically within the [cytoplasm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cytoplasm) of a cell.

plasmid is a small, [extrachromosomal DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Extrachromosomal_DNA) molecule within a cell that is physically separated from [chromosomal DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GDNA) and can replicate independently.

plasmid partition system is a mechanism that ensures the stable inheritance of [plasmid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plasmid)s during bacterial [cell division](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_division).
plasmid preparation is a method of [DNA extraction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA_extraction) and purification for [plasmid DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plasmid).

Plasmid-mediated resistance is the transfer of [antibiotic resistance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antibiotic_resistance) genes which are carried on [plasmid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plasmid)s.
plasmidome refers to the [plasmid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plasmid)s present in it.

plasmodium is a [unicellular organism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unicellular_organism), a living structure of [cytoplasm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cytoplasm) that contains many [nuclei](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_nucleus), rather than being divided into individual cells each with a single nucleus.
Plasmolysis is the process in which cells lose water in a [hypertonic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hypertonic) solution.

term: Plastic pollution in the Mediterranean sea
page: Plastic pollution in the Mediterranean sea

media.file: Global microplastic abundance at the ocean surface (ArcGIS).jpg

definition: plastid is a [membrane-bound organelle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Membrane-bound_organelle) found in the [cell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_(biology))s of [plants](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plants), [algae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Algae), and some other [eukaryotic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eukaryotic) organisms.

Plate readers, also known as microplate readers or microplate photometers, are instruments which are used to detect [biological](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biology), [chemical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chemistry) or [physical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Physics) events of samples in [microtiter plate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microtiter_plate)s.

plateau principle is a [mathematical model](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mathematical_model) or [scientific law](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_law) originally developed to explain the time course of drug action ([pharmacokinetics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pharmacokinetics)).

Platelets or thrombocytes () are a part of [blood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blood) whose function (along with the [[coagulation#Coagulation factors|coagulation factors]]) is to react to [bleeding](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bleeding) from [blood vessel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blood_vessel) injury by clumping to form a [blood clot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thrombus).

Platelet-mimicking particles are [bioengineered](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bioengineered) constructs that functionally replicate the size, shape, and mechanical properties of natural [platelets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Platelets), which assist various [hemostatic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hemostatic) mechanisms.

Platform screen doors (PSDs), also known as platform edge doors (PEDs), are used at some [train](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Train), [rapid transit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rapid_transit) and [people mover](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People_mover) stations to separate the [platform](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Railway_platform) from train tracks, as well as on some [bus rapid transit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bus_rapid_transit), [tram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tram) and [light rail](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Light_rail) systems.

Platyclades are flattened, [photosynthetic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Photosynthesis) shoots, [branch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Branch)es or [stem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plant_stem)s that resemble or perform the function of [leaves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leaves), as in [Homalocladium platycladum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Homalocladium_platycladum) and some [cactus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cactus) genera like [Opuntia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Opuntia) and [Schlumbergera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Schlumbergera).

Plazi is a Swiss-based international [nonprofit association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nonprofit_organization) supporting and promoting the development of persistent and openly accessible digital [bio-taxonomic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biological_classification) literature.

Plectenchyma (from [Greek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ancient_Greek) πλέκω pleko 'I weave' and ἔγχυμα enchyma 'infusion', i.e., 'a woven tissue') is the general term employed to designate all types of [fungal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fungus) tissues.
Pleiotropy () is a condition in which a single [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene) or genetic variant influences multiple [phenotypic trait](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phenotypic_trait)s.

Pleomorphism is a term used in [histology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Histology) and [cytopathology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cytopathology) to describe variability in the size, shape and [staining](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Staining) of [cell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_(biology))s and/or their [nuclei](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_nucleus).

Pleurodont is a form of tooth implantation common in [reptile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reptile)s of the order [Squamata](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Squamata), as well as in at least one [temnospondyl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Temnospondyl).

media.file: Tooth shape changes within the jaw (heterodont - homodont).jpg

definition: plica semilunaris is a small fold of [bulbar conjunctiva](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conjunctiva) on the medial canthus of the [eye](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eye).
PLINK is a free, open-source [whole-genome association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Whole_genome_association_study) analysis toolkit used to perform a wide-range of genetic data analysis.

plithotaxis () is the tendency for each individual [cell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_(biology)) within a [monolayer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monolayer) to [migrate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cellular_migration) along the local orientation of the maximal [principal stress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Principal_stress), or equivalently, minimal intercellular [shear stress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shear_stress).

media.file: Plithotaxis - Cells trekking rugged stress landscape.gif

definition: Plombières Agreement (; ) of 21 July 1858 was a secret verbal agreement that took place at [Plombières-les-Bains](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plombières-les-Bains) between the chief minister of [Piedmont-Sardinia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingdom_of_Sardinia), [Camillo Benso, Count of Cavour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Camillo_Benso,_Count_of_Cavour), paving the way for [Italian unification](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unification_of_Italy) to be fully realized twelve years later.

media.file: Camillo Benso di Cavour 1864 by Francesco Hayez 041.jpg

definition: PLOS Biology is a monthly [peer-reviewed scientific journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer-reviewed_scientific_journal) covering all aspects of [biology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biology).

PLOS Computational Biology is a monthly [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer-reviewed) [open access](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Open_access) [scientific journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_journal) covering [computational biology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computational_biology).

PLOS Genetics is a [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer-reviewed) [open access](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Open_access) [scientific](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific) journal established in 2005 and published by the [Public Library of Science](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Public_Library_of_Science).

Plum Island Animal Disease Center (PIADC) is a United States federal research facility dedicated to the study of [foreign animal disease](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foreign_animal_disease)s of [livestock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Livestock).

Plumage (), or feathering, is a layer of [feather](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Feather)s that covers a [bird](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bird) and the pattern, colour, and arrangement of those feathers.

PLUMED is an open-source library implementing enhanced-sampling algorithms, various [free-energy methods](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Free_energy_perturbation), and analysis tools for [molecular dynamics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Molecular_dynamics) simulations.

pluriblast is a [pluripotent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pluripotency) population of [cells](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_(biology)) in the [embryogenesis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Embryogenesis) of [marsupial](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marsupial)s, called the [inner cell mass](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inner_cell_mass) in [eutherian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eutherian)s.
pluripotency of biological compounds describes the ability of certain substances to produce several distinct biological responses.

categories: Biological research institutes in the United Kingdom

definition: pneumatodes are air-containing structures in plant roots.

pneumostome or breathing pore is a respiratory opening of the external body anatomy of a [pulmonate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pulmonate) land [slug](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slug) or [land snail](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Land_snail).

Peptide:N-glycosidase F, commonly referred to as PNGase F, is an [amidase](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amidase) of the [peptide-N4-(N-acetyl-beta-glucosaminyl)asparagine amidase](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peptide-N4-(N-acetyl-beta-glucosaminyl)asparagine_amidase) class.
pocket prairie is a small, artificially created, self-sustaining area of land where [forb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forb)s and plants predominate.

Podocytes are [cells](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_(biology)) in [Bowman's capsule](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bowman's_capsule) in the [kidney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kidney)s that wrap around [capillaries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Capillary) of the [glomerulus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glomerulus_(kidney)).

Podosomes are conical, [actin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Actin)-rich structures found as [appendage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Appendage)s on the outer surface of the [plasma membrane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plasma_membrane) of [animal cell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Animal_cell)s.

poecilogony was coined by [Alfred Mathieu Giard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alfred_Mathieu_Giard) to describe a [polymorphism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polymorphism_(biology)) in [larva](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Larva)l development in [marine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marine_habitats) [invertebrate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Invertebrate)s.

Poikilohydry is the lack of ability (structural or functional mechanism) to maintain and/or regulate water content to achieve [homeostasis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Homeostasis) of cells and tissue connected with quick equilibration of cell/tissue water content to that of the environment.
poikilotherm () is an [animal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Animal) (Greek poikilos – 'various', 'spotted', and therme – 'heat') whose internal temperature varies considerably.

point mutation is a [genetic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetics) [mutation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mutation) where a single nucleotide base is changed, inserted or deleted from a [DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA) or [RNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RNA) sequence of an organism's genome.

Poison exons (PEs); also called [premature termination codon (PTC)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stop_codon) exons or [nonsense-mediated decay (NMD)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nonsense-mediated_decay) exons] are a class of [[Alternative splicing#Modes|cassette exons]] that contain PTCs.

definition: Polar Biology is a monthly [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer-reviewed) [scientific journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_journal) covering the [biology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biology) of the [polar regions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polar_regions).

Polar body biopsy is the [sampling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sampling_(medicine)) of a [polar body](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polar_body) of an [oocyte](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oocyte).

Polar capsules are structures found in the valves of [myxosporea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Myxosporea)n parasites, which contain the [polar filament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polar_filament).
Polar ecology is the relationship between plants and animals in a polar environment.

polar organelle is a structure at a specialized region of the [bacteria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bacteria)l [polar membrane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polar_membrane) that is associated with the [flagellar apparatus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flagellum).

Polar overdominance is a unique form of inheritance originally described in livestock, with relevant examples in humans ==See also== *[Imprinting (genetics)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Imprinting_(genetics)) *[MEG3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MEG3) - a gene occasionally expressed through polar overdominance == References == ==Further reading== * [[Category:Genetics]] 3o1non5j1c0cwngtijf82iyu4ecf0uq

Polar Research is the [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer-reviewed), multi-disciplinary scholarly journal published by the [Norwegian Polar Institute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Norwegian_Polar_Institute).

polarized membrane is a [lipid membrane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lipid_bilayer) that has a positive [electrical charge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electrical_charge) on one side and a negative charge on another side, which produces the [resting potential](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Resting_potential) in living cells.

categories: Fellows of the American Institute for Medical and Biological Engineering

definition: Polistepipona is an [Afrotropical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Afrotropical) genus of [potter wasp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Potter_wasp)s.
Political ecology is the study of the relationships between political, economic and social factors with environmental issues and changes.

Politics and the Life Sciences (PLS) is a [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer_review) [academic journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academic_journal) that was first published in 1982 with Thomas Wiegele as the editor.
Pollen is a powdery substance produced by most types of flowers of [seed plant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seed_plant)s for the purpose of sexual reproduction.

Pollen Analysis Circular was a mimeographed publication that maintained communications among scientists working on either side of the Atlantic Ocean during [World War II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_II) and aided the early development of the field of [palynology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palynology).
pollen basket or corbicula (plural corbiculae) is part of the [[Arthropod leg#Hexapoda|tibia]] on the hind legs of the female of certain species of [bee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bee)s.

Pollen [DNA barcoding](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA_barcoding) is the process of identifying [pollen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pollen) donor [plant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plant) species through the [amplification](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polymerase_chain_reaction) and [sequencing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA_sequencing) of specific, conserved regions of plant [DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA).
pollen tube is a tubular structure produced by the male [gametophyte](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gametophyte) of [seed plants](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seed_plants) when it germinates.

pollination network is a bipartite [mutualistic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mutualism_(biology)) network in which plants and [pollinator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pollinator)s are the [nodes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Node_(graph_theory)), and the [pollination](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pollination) interactions form the links between these nodes.

Pollination syndromes are suites of [flower](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flower) traits that have evolved in response to [natural selection](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Natural_selection) imposed by different [pollen vectors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pollination), which can be abiotic (wind and water) or biotic, such as birds, bees, flies, and so forth through a process called [pollinator-mediated selection](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pollinator-mediated_selection), a form of selection pressure.

pollinator is an animal that moves [pollen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pollen) from the male [anther](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anther) of a [flower](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flower) to the female [stigma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carpel) of a flower.

Pollinator decline is the reduction in abundance of [insect](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Insect) and other animal [pollinator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pollinator)s in many [ecosystem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ecosystem)s worldwide that began being recorded at the end of the 20th century.

pollinium (: pollinia) is a coherent mass of [pollen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pollen) grains in a plant that are the product of only one [anther](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anther), but are transferred, during pollination, as a single unit.

Polony sequencing is an inexpensive but highly accurate [multiplex sequencing technique](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multiplex_sequencing_technique) that can be used to “read” millions of immobilized DNA sequences in parallel.

Poly(ADP-ribose) polymerase family member 14 is a [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) that, in [human](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human)s, is encoded by the PARP14 [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).

Polyanhydrides are a class of [biodegradable](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biodegradable) [polymer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polymer)s characterized by [anhydride](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anhydride) bonds that connect [repeat unit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Repeat_unit)s of the polymer [backbone chain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Backbone_chain).

Polycerates (meaning ==Mythology== [Cerastes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cerastes), a legendary Greek horned [serpent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Serpent_(symbolism)), is sometimes described with two horns or with four small ones.

definition: polyculture is the practice of growing more than one crop species together in the same place at the same time, in contrast to [monoculture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monoculture), which had become the dominant approach in developed countries by 1950.

Polydactyly in stem-tetrapods should here be understood as having more than five digits to the finger or foot, a condition that was the natural state of affairs in the earliest [stegocephalians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stegocephalia) during the [evolution of terrestriality](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vertebrate_land_invasion).
Polyembryony is the phenomenon of two or more [embryo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Embryo)s developing from a single fertilized egg.

polygene is a member of a group of non-[epistatic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Epistasis) [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene)s that interact additively to influence a [phenotypic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phenotype) trait, thus contributing to multiple-gene inheritance (polygenic inheritance, multigenic inheritance, quantitative inheritance Another interest of statistical geneticists using QTL mapping is to determine the complexity of the genetic architecture underlying a phenotypic trait.

Polygenic adaptation describes a process in which a [population](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Population_(biology)) adapts through small changes in [allele frequencies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Allele_frequency) at hundreds or thousands of [loci](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Locus_(genetics)).
polygenic score (PGS) is a number that summarizes the estimated effect of many genetic variants on an individual's [phenotype](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phenotype).

Polyhaline or Mixo-haline, is a salinity category term applied to [brackish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brackish) [estuaries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Estuaries) and other marine waters with a [salinity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salinity) between 18 and 30 [parts per thousand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parts_per_thousand).

polylecty or generalist is used in [pollination](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pollination) [ecology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ecology) to refer to [bees](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bees) that collect pollen from a range of unrelated plants.

definition: Polymerase cycling assembly (or PCA, also known as Assembly PCR) is a method for the assembly of large [DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA) [oligonucleotide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oligonucleotide)s from shorter fragments.

Polymerase stuttering is the process by which a [polymerase](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polymerase) [transcribe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transcription_(genetics))s a nucleotide several times without progressing further on the [mRNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MRNA) chain.

definition: polyp in [zoology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zoology) is one of two forms found in the [phylum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phylum) [Cnidaria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cnidaria), the other being the [medusa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medusa_(biology)).
polyphyodont is any animal whose [teeth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tooth_(animal)) are continually replaced.

Polysialic acid is an unusual [posttranslational modification](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Posttranslational_modification) that occurs on [neural cell adhesion molecule](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neural_cell_adhesion_molecule)s (NCAM).

Polysome profiling is a technique in [molecular biology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Molecular_biology) that is used to study the association of [mRNAs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MRNAs) with [ribosome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ribosome)s.

pomato (a [portmanteau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portmanteau) of [potato](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Potato) and [tomato](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tomato)), also known as a tomtato, is a [hybrid plant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybrid_plant) that is able to grow both tomatoes and potatoes.

Pontiac fever is an acute, nonfatal respiratory disease caused by various species of [Gram-negative bacteria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gram-negative_bacteria) in the genus [Legionella](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legionella).

pooling layer is a kind of [network layer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Layer_(deep_learning)) that [downsamples](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Downsampling_(signal_processing)) and aggregates information that is dispersed among many vectors into fewer vectors.
Pop-up satellite archival tags (PSATs) are used to track movements of (usually large, migratory) [marine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marine_(ocean)) animals.

Popliteal refers to anatomical structures located in the back of the [knee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Knee): *[Popliteal artery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Popliteal_artery) *[Popliteal vein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Popliteal_vein) *[Popliteal fossa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Popliteal_fossa) *[Popliteal lymph nodes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Popliteal_lymph_nodes) *[Popliteus muscle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Popliteus_muscle) *Popliteal [nerves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nerves) *[Popliteal pterygium syndrome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Popliteal_pterygium_syndrome) [[Category:Lower limb anatomy]] rgeqaibw3d45in29sqpqhu03wnyswlu
popularity is how much a person, idea, place, item or other concept is either liked or accorded status PopularityExplained.com, retrieved July 19, 2015.

population of [organisms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organism) is a group of individuals of the same [species](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Species), defined by a discontinuity or [[wikt:disjunction|disjunction]] from other groups of individuals in certain characteristics, such as living area, genetic attributes, demographic structure.

human population is the set of [people](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human) living in a particular [geographic area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Region), increasing or decreasing in [size](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Population_size) over time, == See also == * [Community (ecology)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Community_(ecology)) * [Human ecology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_ecology) == References == == External links == * [https://www.un.org/esa/population/unpop.htm United Nations Population Division] * [http://www.cicred.org/Eng/Publications/IndexPublications.htm CICRED homepage] a platform for interaction between research centres and international organizations, such as the United Nations Population Division, [UNFPA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UNFPA), [WHO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WHO) and [FAO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FAO).

Population Balance (formerly World Population Balance) is a [501(c)(3)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/501(c)(3)_organization) [non-profit organization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nonprofit_organization) in the [United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States) that raises awareness of the connections between [pronatalism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Natalism), [human overpopulation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_overpopulation), [human supremacy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthropocentrism), [social inequalities](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Social_inequality), and [ecological overshoot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ecological_overshoot), and advocates pathways that address their combined impacts on the planet, people, and animals.

population bottleneck or genetic bottleneck is a sharp reduction in the size of a [population](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Population_(biology)) due to environmental events such as [famines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Famines), [earthquakes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Earthquakes), [floods](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Floods), fires, [disease](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disease), and [drought](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drought)s; or human activities such as [genocide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genocide), [speciocide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Extinction), widespread violence or intentional [culling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Culling).

Population Control Bill, 2019 (or, Population Regulation Bill, 2019) is a proposed bill introduced in the [Rajya Sabha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rajya_Sabha) in July 2019 by [Rakesh Sinha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rakesh_Sinha).
Population density is a measurement of [population size](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Population_size) per unit [land area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Land_area).

population dynamics of fisheries is used by [fisheries scientist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fisheries_science)s to determine [sustainable yields](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sustainable_yield_in_fisheries).

Population genetics is a subfield of [genetics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetics) that deals with genetic differences within and among [population](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Population_(biology))s, and is a part of [evolutionary biology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evolutionary_biology).

definition: Population Genetics Group (or PopGroup, or PGG) is an annual meeting of [population geneticists](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Population_genetics) held in the UK since 1968.
categories: Population genetics in the United Kingdom

definition: Population genomics is the large-scale comparison of [DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA) sequences of populations.
Population Investigation Committee is a United Kingdom social research group founded in 1936 by the council of the [British Eugenics Society](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Eugenics_Society).

Population momentum or demographic inertia is the tendency of the [raw birth rate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Birth_rate) to rise as a result of past high [fertility rates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Total_fertility_rate), even after fertility rates have fallen, or vice-versa.

Population pressure, a term summarizing the stress brought about by an excessive [population density](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Population_density) and its consequences, is used both in conjunction with [human overpopulation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_overpopulation) and with other [animal population](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Animal_population)s that suffer from too many individuals per area (or volume in the case of [aquatic organism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aquatic_organism)s).

population size (usually denoted N) is a [countable quantity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Countable_quantity) representing the number of individual [organism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organism)s in a [population](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Population_(biology)).

Population structure (also called genetic structure and population stratification) is the presence of a systematic difference in [allele](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Allele) [frequencies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Allele_frequency) between [subpopulation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Population_(biology))s.

Population thinking is a concept in [evolutionary biology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evolutionary_biology) coined by [Ernst Mayr](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ernst_Mayr) as part of his contributions to the [modern evolutionary synthesis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_synthesis).

population vector is the sum of the preferred directions of a population of [neuron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neuron)s, [weighted](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Weighted_arithmetic_mean) by the respective spike counts.

Population viability analysis (PVA) is a [species](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Species)-specific method of [risk assessment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Risk_assessment) frequently used in [conservation biology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conservation_biology).

pores of Kohn (also known as interalveolar connections or alveolar pores) are discrete holes in [walls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alveolar_wall) of adjacent [alveoli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pulmonary_alveolus).

definition: Porocytes are tubular cells which make up the pores of a [sponge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sea_sponge) known as [ostia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ostium_(sponges)).

Porosomes are cup-shaped supramolecular structures in the [cell membranes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_membranes) of [eukaryotic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eukaryote) cells where [secretory vesicle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secretory_vesicle)s transiently dock in the process of [vesicle fusion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vesicle_fusion) and [secretion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secretion).

Port Botany is a [suburb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Suburb) in the Eastern Suburbs of Sydney, in the state of [New South Wales](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_South_Wales), [Australia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australia).

[human brain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_brain) has the same general structure as the [brain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brain)s of other [mammal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mammal)s, but is larger than any other in relation to body size.
tissue is a cellular organizational level between [cells](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_(biology)) and a complete [organ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organ_(anatomy)).

Henry Vandyke Carter (born 22 May 1831, [Hull](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingston_upon_Hull) – 4 May 1897, [Scarborough](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scarborough,_North_Yorkshire)) was an English anatomist, surgeon, and anatomical artist most notable for his illustrations of the book, [Gray's Anatomy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gray's_Anatomy).
