page: Portland Press Excellence in Science Award
definition: Portland Press Excellence in Science Award was an annual award instituted in 1964 to recognize notable research in any branch of [biochemistry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biochemistry) undertaken in the UK or Republic of [Ireland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ireland).

Porton Down is a science and defence technology campus in [Wiltshire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wiltshire), England, just north-east of the village of [Porton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Porton), near [Salisbury](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salisbury).
categories: Biological research institutes in the United Kingdom

definition: Position-effect variegation (PEV) is a [variegation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Variegation_(histology)) caused by the silencing of a [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene) in some cells through its abnormal juxtaposition with [heterochromatin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heterochromatin) via rearrangement or [transposition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transposable_element).

Positional sequencing is a method of [sequencing DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA_sequencing) that simultaneously generates information about both identity and location of [nucleotide sequences](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nucleic_acid_sequence).
positive neuroscience is the study of what the [brain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_brain) does well.

Post-fire hillslope stabilization treatments are treatments aimed at stabilizing fire-affected [slope](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slope)s by counteracting the negative impact of fire on vegetation and [soil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soil) properties.

Post-orbital constriction is the narrowing of the [cranium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cranium) (skull) just behind the [orbit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orbit_(anatomy))s (eye sockets) found in most non-human [primates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primates) and early [hominins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hominins).

Transcriptional modification or co-transcriptional modification is a set of biological processes common to most [eukaryotic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eukaryote) cells by which an [RNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RNA) [primary transcript](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primary_transcript) is chemically altered following [transcription](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transcription_(biology)) from a [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene) to produce a mature, functional RNA molecule that can then leave the [nucleus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_nucleus) and perform any of a variety of different functions in the cell.
Post-transcriptional regulation is the control of [gene expression](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene_expression) at the [RNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RNA) level.

Post-translational modifications (PTMs) are the [covalent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Covalent) processes of changing [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein)s following their [synthesis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein_biosynthesis), and release from [ribosome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ribosome)s.

Post-canine megadontia is a relative enlargement of the molars and premolars compared to the size of the [incisor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Incisor)s and [canines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_tooth).

Postcode Plants Database was a UK resource for identifying locally native plants and species based on [postcode](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UK_postcodes), hosted by the [Natural History Museum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Natural_History_Museum,_London) in London.
postdentary trough is a skeletal feature seen in [Mesozoic mammals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evolution_of_mammals).
posterior carpometacarpal ligament consists of a series of bands on the posterior surface of the [carpometacarpal joints](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carpometacarpal_joints).

posterior chamber is a narrow space behind the peripheral part of the [iris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iris_(anatomy)), and in front of the [suspensory ligament of the lens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Suspensory_ligament_of_the_lens) and the [ciliary processes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ciliary_processes).

posterior compartment of the thigh is one of the [fascial compartments](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fascial_compartments_of_thigh) that contains the [knee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Knee) [[anatomical terms of motion#flexion|flexors]] and [hip](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hip) [[anatomical terms of motion#extension|extensors]] known as the [hamstring muscles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hamstring_muscles), as well as vascular and nervous elements, particularly the [sciatic nerve](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sciatic_nerve).

Posterior cortical atrophy (PCA), also called Benson's syndrome, is a rare form of [dementia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dementia) which is considered a visual variant or an atypical variant of [Alzheimer's disease](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alzheimer's_disease) (AD).

posterior humeral circumflex vessels or posterior circumflex humeral vessels are the [posterior humeral circumflex artery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Posterior_humeral_circumflex_artery) and the [posterior humeral circumflex vein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Posterior_humeral_circumflex_vein) which run through the [quadrangular](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quadrangular_space) (or quadrilateral) space with the [axillary nerve](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Axillary_nerve).

posterior interventricular sulcus or posterior longitudinal sulcus is one of the two grooves separating the [ventricles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ventricle_(heart)) of the [heart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heart) (the other being the [anterior interventricular sulcus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anterior_interventricular_sulcus)).
posterolateral palatal pits are gaps at the sides of the back of the bony [palate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palate), near the last [molars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Molar_(tooth)).
Postglacial vegetation refers to plants that colonize the newly exposed substrate after a [glacial retreat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Holocene_glacial_retreat).

Postmenopausal confusion, also commonly referred to as postmenopausal brain fog, is a group of symptoms of [menopause](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Menopause) in which women report problems with [cognition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brain) at a higher frequency during postmenopause than before.

Postmortem studies are a type of [neurobiological](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neurobiological) research, which provides information to researchers and individuals who will have to make medical decisions in the future.
Postnaturalism is the theory of the postnatural, a term coined to describe organisms that have been intentionally and heritably altered by humans.

postorbital bar (or postorbital bone) is a bony arched structure that connects the [frontal bone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frontal_bone) of the [skull](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skull) to the [zygomatic arch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zygomatic_arch), which runs laterally around the [eye socket](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eye_socket).

Potamkin Prize for Research in Pick's, Alzheimer's, and Related Diseases was established in 1988 and is sponsored by the [American Academy of Neurology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Academy_of_Neurology).

potassium channel RNA editing signal is an [RNA element](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cis-regulatory_element) found in human [Kv1.1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kv1.1) and its homologues which directs the efficient modification of an [adenosine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adenosine) to [inosine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inosine) by an adenosine deaminase acting on RNA ([ADAR](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ADAR)).

Poxytrins or dihydroxy-E,Z,E-polyunsaturated fatty acids (dihydroxy-E,Z,E-PUFAs) are [PUFA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PUFA) [metabolite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metabolite)s that possess two [hydroxyl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hydroxyl) residues and three in-series [conjugated double bond](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conjugated_double_bond)s in an E,Z,E [cis–trans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cis–trans) configuration.

Poço das Antas Biological Reserve () is a [biological reserve](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biological_reserve_(Brazil)) located in [Rio de Janeiro State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rio_de_Janeiro_(state)), [Brazil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brazil).

Praia do Sul State Biological Reserve () is a [biological reserve](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biological_reserve_(Brazil)) on the island of [Ilha Grande](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ilha_Grande), in the [State of Rio de Janeiro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rio_de_Janeiro_(state)), in [Brazil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brazil).

prairie remnant commonly refers to grassland areas in the [Western](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_United_States) and [Midwestern United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Midwestern_United_States) and [Canada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canada) that remain to some extent [undisturbed by European settlement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Remnant_natural_area).

preBötzinger complex, often abbreviated as preBötC, is a functionally and anatomically specialized site in the ventral-lateral region of the lower [medulla oblongata](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medulla_oblongata) (i.e., lower [brainstem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brainstem)).

Pre-Columbian woodlands of North America, consisting of a mixed woodland-grassland ecosystem, were maintained by both natural lightning fires and by [Native Americans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Native_American_use_of_fire) before the [significant arrival of Europeans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pre-Columbian).

Protein engineering is the process of developing useful or valuable [proteins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) through the design and production of unnatural [polypeptides](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peptide), often by altering [amino acid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amino_acid) sequences found in nature.

protein mimetic is a molecule such as a [peptide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peptide), a modified peptide or any other [molecule](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Molecule) that biologically mimics the action or activity of some other [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein).

Protein misfolding cyclic amplification (PMCA) is an [amplification](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amplification_(molecular_biology)) technique (conceptually like [polymerase chain reaction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polymerase_chain_reaction) (PCR) but not involving [nucleotide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nucleotide)s) to multiply misfolded [prion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prion)s originally developed by Soto and colleagues.

Protein phosphorylation is a reversible [post-translational modification](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post-translational_modification) of [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein)s in which an [amino acid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amino_acid) residue is [phosphorylated](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phosphorylation) by a protein [kinase](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kinase) by the addition of a covalently bound phosphate group.

media.file: Phosporylation of a serine residue, before and after shot.png

definition: Protein quinary structure refers to the features of [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) surfaces that are shaped by [evolutionary adaptation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adaptation) to the [physiological](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Physiological) context of [living cells](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Living_cells).

Protein sequencing is the practical process of determining the [amino acid sequence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amino_acid_sequence) of all or part of a [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) or [peptide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peptide).

media.file: Man using a Beckman-Spinco Protein-Peptide Sequencer bg257f292.tiff

definition: Protein structural phylogenetics (or Structural phylogenetics) is the branch of [molecular evolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Molecular_evolution) that incorporates three dimensional information from [protein structure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein_structure) to understand [phylogenetic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phylogenetics) relationships, and translates those evolutionary insights into understanding protein structure and function.

protein structure database is a database that is [modeled](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Data_modeling) around the various [[protein structure#Protein_structure_determination|experimentally determined]] [protein structure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein_structure)s.

protein superfamily is the largest grouping ([clade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clade)) of [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein)s for which [common ancestry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Common_ancestry) can be inferred (see [homology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Homology_(biology))).
Protein tags are peptide sequences genetically grafted onto a [recombinant protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Recombinant_protein).
protein-fragment complementation assay, or PCA, is a method for the identification and quantification of [protein–protein interactions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein–protein_interactions).

Proteinoplasts (sometimes called proteoplasts, aleuroplasts, and aleuronaplasts) are specialized [organelle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organelle)s found only in [plant cell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plant_cell)s.

term: Proteins produced and secreted by the liver
page: Proteins produced and secreted by the liver

definition: Protein–lipid interaction is the influence of [membrane protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Membrane_protein)s on the [lipid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lipid) [physical state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Physical_state) or vice versa.

proteolipid is a [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) covalently linked to [lipid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lipid) molecules, which can be [fatty acid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fatty_acid)s, [isoprenoids](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Terpenoid) or [sterol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sterol)s.
Proteomimetics are molecules that mimic certain protein characteristics such as shape, binding properties or enzymatic activity.
Proteostasis is the [dynamic regulation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Homeostasis) of a balanced, functional [proteome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Proteome).

prothallus, or prothallium, (from [Latin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latin) pro = forwards and [Greek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greek_language) θαλλος (thallos) = twig) is usually the [gametophyte](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gametophyte) stage in the life of a [fern](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fern) or other [pteridophyte](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pteridophyte).

prothoracic glands are either of a pair of [endocrine gland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Endocrine_gland)s located in the [prothorax](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prothorax) of certain insects that regulate [molting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Molting).

prothorax is the foremost of the three segments in the [thorax](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thorax_(insect_anatomy)) of an [insect](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Insect), and bears the first pair of [legs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Insect_leg).
Protistology is a scientific discipline devoted to the study of [protists](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protists), a highly diverse group of [[Microorganism#Eukaryotes|eukaryotic]] organisms.

Proto-Human language, also known as Proto-Sapiens, Proto-World, or the Urlanguage is the hypothetical direct [genetic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetic_relationship_(linguistics)) predecessor of all human languages.

protocell (or protobiont) is a [self-organized](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Self-organization), [membrane-bound](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Membrane_lipid) or [membraneless](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biomolecular_condensate) compartment that concentrates biomolecules, proposed as a rudimentary precursor to cells during the [origin of life](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abiogenesis).

Protofection is a protein-mediated [transfection](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transfection) of foreign [mitochondrial DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mitochondrial_DNA) (mtDNA) into the [mitochondria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mitochondrion) of cells in a tissue to supplement or replace the native mitochondrial DNA already present.

Protomap is a primordial molecular map of the functional areas of the mammalian [cerebral cortex](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cerebral_cortex) during early [embryonic development](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Embryonic_development), at a stage when [neural stem cells](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neural_stem_cells) are still the dominant cell type.
protomer is the structural unit of an [oligomeric protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein_quaternary_structure).

Proton-coupled amino acid transporters belong to the [SLC26A5](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SLC26A5) family; they are protein receptors whose main function is the [transmembrane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transmembrane_protein) movement of amino acids and their derivatives.

Protoplasma is a bimonthly [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer-reviewed) [scientific journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_journal) covering various aspects of [protoplasm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protoplasm) research.

Protoplast (), is a [biological](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biology) term coined by [Hanstein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johannes_von_Hanstein) in 1880 to refer to the entire cell, excluding the cell wall.
proventriculus is part of the [digestive system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digestive_system) of [birds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Birds).
proximal centriole-like (PCL) is an atypical type of [centriole](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Centriole) found in the [sperm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sperm) cells of insects.

proximal tubule is the segment of the [nephron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nephron) in [kidney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kidney)s which begins from the renal (tubular) pole of the [Bowman's capsule](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bowman's_capsule) to the beginning of [loop of Henle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loop_of_Henle).

proximity labeling (PL), also known as proximity-based labeling, is a [laboratory technique](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laboratory_technique) that labels [biomolecule](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biomolecule)s, usually [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein)s or [RNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RNA), proximal to a protein of interest.
proximodorsal [process](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Process_(anatomy)) is a feature of the skeleton of [archosaur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Archosaur)s.

Prp24 (precursor RNA processing, gene 24) is a protein part of the [pre-messenger RNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HnRNA) [splicing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RNA_splicing) process and aids the binding of [U6 snRNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U6_snRNA) to [U4 snRNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U4_snRNA) during the formation of [spliceosome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spliceosome)s.
PrrB/RsmZ RNA family are a group of related [non-coding RNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-coding_RNA) molecules found in bacteria.
Psammophory is a method by which certain plants armor themselves with sand on their body parts, lowering the chance of them being eaten by animals.
psammophyte is a plant that grows in sandy and often unstable soils.
pSC101 is a [plasmid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plasmid) that is used as a [cloning vector](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cloning_vector) in molecular biology.

Pseudo-panspermia (sometimes called soft panspermia, molecular panspermia or quasi-panspermia) is a well-supported hypothesis for a stage in the [origin of life](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Origin_of_life).
Pseudo-response regulator (PRR) refers to a group of genes that regulate the [circadian oscillator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Circadian_oscillator) in plants.
Pseudoallelism refers to a genetic phenomenon in which two or more functionally related loci are so closely linked on a chromosome that they were historically interpreted as alleles of a single gene.

pseudoautosomal regions or PARs are [homologous](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Homology_(biology)) sequences of [nucleotide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nucleotide)s found within the [sex chromosome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sex_chromosome)s of species with an [XY](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/XY_sex-determination_system) and [Madelung's deformity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madelung's_deformity).

media.file: A region in the pseudoautosomal region of the short arms of the X- and Y-chromosome.jpg

definition: Pseudochilus is a small [Afrotropical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Afrotropical) genus of [potter wasp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Potter_wasp)s consisting of 5 currently known species.

Pseudociliate refers to a type of cells which are covered by small coordinated flagella ([cilia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cilia)), but are not related to the [Harosan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SAR_supergroup) group called the [Ciliophora](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ciliate).
pseudoculus (plural pseudoculi, ) is the name applied to various [eye](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eye)-like structures which are nevertheless not eyes.

Pseudocyphellae (singular pseudocyphella) are structures in [lichen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lichen)s that appear as tiny pores on the outer surface (the [cortex](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cortex_(botany))) of the lichen.
pseudodeficiency allele or pseudodeficiency mutation is a mutation that alters the protein product or changes the [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene)'s expression, but without causing disease.

Pseudodynerus is a small [Neotropical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neotropical) genus of [potter wasp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Potter_wasp)s ([Hymenoptera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hymenoptera): [Vespidae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vespidae): [Eumeninae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eumeninae)) currently containing 16 species.

Pseudoextinction (or phyletic extinction) of a [species](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Species) occurs when all members of the species are [extinct](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Extinct), but members of a [daughter species](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chronospecies) remain alive.

pseudolinkage is a characteristic of a [heterozygote](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heterozygote) for a [reciprocal translocation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reciprocal_translocation), in which genes located near the [translocation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chromosomal_translocation) breakpoint behave as if they are [linked](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetic_linkage) even though they originated on [http://www.mondofacto.com/facts/dictionary?nonhomologous+chromosomes nonhomologous chromosomes].

Pseudoplanktonic [organism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organism)s are those that attach themselves to [planktonic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Planktonic) organisms or other floating objects, such as drifting wood, [buoyant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buoyant) shells of organisms such as [Spirula](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spirula), or man-made [flotsam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flotsam).

pseudopod or pseudopodium (: pseudopods or pseudopodia) is a temporary arm-like projection of an [eukaryotic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eukaryotic) [cell membrane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_membrane) that is emerged in the direction of movement.

Pseudoproteases are catalytically-deficient [pseudoenzyme](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pseudoenzyme) variants of [protease](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protease)s that are represented across the kingdoms of life. ![Superfamily](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein_superfamily) !Families containing pseudoenzymes !Examples |- |[CA clan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CA_clan) |C1, C2, C19 |[Calpamodulin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calpamodulin) |- |CD clan |C14 |[CFLAR](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CFLAR) |- |SC clan |S9, S33 |[Neuroligin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neuroligin) |- |SK clan |S14 |[ClpR](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clp_protease_family) |- |SR cl
pseudopupil appears as a dark spot which moves across the eye as the animal is rotated.
Psiliglossa is a circum-Mediterranean and Central-Asian genus of [potter wasp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Potter_wasp)s with seven known species.

Psychiatric genetics is a subfield of [behavioral neurogenetics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Behavioral_neurogenetics) and [behavioral genetics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Behavioural_genetics) which studies the role of genetics in the development of [mental disorder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mental_disorder)s (such as [alcoholism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alcoholism), [schizophrenia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Schizophrenia), [bipolar disorder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bipolar_disorder), and [autism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Autism)).
related: International Behavioural and Neural Genetics Society

definition: Psychiatric Genomics Consortium (PGC) is an international [consortium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Consortium) of scientists dedicated to conducting [meta- and mega-analyses of genomic-wide genetic data](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genome-wide_association_study), with a focus on [psychiatric disorder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Psychiatric_disorder)s.
stress is a [feeling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Feeling) of emotional strain and pressure.
Psychology, philosophy and physiology (PPP) was a [degree](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academic_degree) program at the [University of Oxford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Oxford).

Psychoneuroendocrinology is a monthly [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer-reviewed) [scientific journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_journal) covering research in [psychoneuroendocrinology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Psychoneuroendocrinology) published by [Elsevier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elsevier).

Psychoneuroimmunology (PNI), also referred to as psychoendoneuroimmunology (PENI) or psychoneuroendocrinoimmunology (PNEI), is the study of the interaction between psychological processes and the nervous and immune systems of the human body.

Psychophysiological interaction (PPI) is a brain connectivity analysis method for [functional brain imaging](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FMRI) data, mainly [functional magnetic resonance imaging](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Functional_magnetic_resonance_imaging) (fMRI).

Psychophysiology is a monthly [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer-reviewed) [scientific journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_journal) published by [Wiley-Blackwell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wiley-Blackwell) on behalf of the [Society for Psychophysiological Research](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Society_for_Psychophysiological_Research).

Psychosocial distress refers to the unpleasant [emotion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emotion)s or [psychological symptoms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Psychology) an individual has when they are overwhelmed, which negatively impacts their [quality of life](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quality_of_life).

Psychosynthesis is a framework and approach to [psychology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Psychology) developed by Italian psychiatrist [Roberto Assagioli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roberto_Assagioli).

pterostigma (plural: pterostigmata) is a group of specialized cells in the outer [wing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Insect_wing)s of [insect](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Insect)s, which are often thickened or coloured, and thus stand out from other cells.

media.file: Raphidia ophiopsis M NL-Doorwerth-19540617 right wing - collection Naturalis.jpg

definition: pterygium (: pterygia or pterygiums) is any wing-like triangular membrane occurring in the neck, eyes, knees, elbows, ankles or digits.

ptilinum is an eversible pouch on the head, above the base of the [antenna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antenna_(biology)) in [schizophoran](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Schizophora) [flies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diptera) (a [section](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Section_(biology)) of [muscomorphan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muscomorpha) and [cyclorrhaphan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cyclorrhapha) flies).
ptotic chin is a [chin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chin) that droops over the [jawline](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jawline).

PubMed is an openly accessible, free [database](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_academic_databases_and_search_engines) which primarily includes the [MEDLINE](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MEDLINE) [database](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bibliographic_database) of references and [abstracts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abstract_(summary)) on [life sciences](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Life_sciences) and [biomedical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biomedicine) topics.
PubMed Central Canada (PMC Canada) was a Canadian national digital repository of peer-reviewed health and life sciences literature.
pUC19 is one of a series of plasmid [cloning vector](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cloning_vector)s designed by [Joachim Messing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joachim_Messing) and co-workers.

Puddling is a behaviour in which an organism seeks out [nutrients](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nutrients) in certain moist substances such as rotting plant matter, [mud](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mud), and [carrion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carrion), and sucks up the fluid.

Puhtu Biological Station is a research station located in [Pärnu county](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pärnu_county) [Lääneranna Parish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lääneranna_Parish), Estonia, at the coast of [Baltic Sea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baltic_Sea).
Pulmocutaneous circulation is part of the [amphibian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amphibian) [circulatory system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Circulatory_system).

pulmonary alveolus (; ), also called an air sac or air space, is one of millions of hollow, distensible cup-shaped cavities in the [lung](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lung)s where pulmonary gas exchange takes place.

pulmonary artery is an [artery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artery) in the [pulmonary circulation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pulmonary_circulation) that carries deoxygenated [blood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blood) from the right side of the [heart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heart) to the [lung](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lung)s.
Pulmonary artery stenosis (PAS) is a narrowing of the [pulmonary artery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pulmonary_artery).
Pulmonary bay is a medical term which describes a finding on the [chest radiograph](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chest_radiograph).
pulmonary circulation is a division of the [circulatory system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Circulatory_system) in all vertebrates.

term: Pulmonary diffusing capacity for nitric oxide
page: Pulmonary diffusing capacity for nitric oxide

definition: pulmonary shunt is the passage of deoxygenated blood from the [[Heart#Right heart|right side of the heart]] to the [[Heart#Left heart|left]] without participation in gas exchange in the pulmonary capillaries.
Pulmonary stretch receptors are [mechanoreceptors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mechanoreceptors) found in the [lungs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_lung).

Pulmonary surfactant is a surface-active complex of [phospholipid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phospholipid)s and [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein)s formed by [type II alveolar cells](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Type_II_cells).

media.file: An alveolus, is an anatomical structure that has the form of a hollow cavity. Mainly found in the lung, the pulmonary alveoli are spherical outcroppings of the respiratory bronchioles and are the.png

definition: pulmonary valve (sometimes referred to as the pulmonic valve) is a [valve of the heart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heart_valve) that lies between the [right ventricle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Right_ventricle) and the [pulmonary artery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pulmonary_artery), and has three cusps.

pulmonary veins are the [vein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vein)s that transfer [[Blood#bloodtransport|oxygenated blood]] from the [lung](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lung)s to the [heart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heart).

pulp is the [connective tissue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Connective_tissue), [nerves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nerves), [blood vessels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blood_vessels), and [odontoblast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Odontoblast)s that comprise the innermost layer of a [tooth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tooth).
Pulpitis is [inflammation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inflammation) of [dental pulp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dental_pulp) tissue.

Pulsatile secretion is a [biochemical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biochemistry) phenomenon observed in a wide variety of [cell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_(biology)) and [tissue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tissue_(biology)) types, in which [chemical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chemical_substance) products are secreted in a regular temporal pattern.
pulse is the rhythmic expansion and contraction of an [artery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artery) in response to the [cardiac cycle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardiac_cycle) (heartbeat).

Pulse computation is a hybrid of [digital](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digital_computer) and [analog](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Analog_computer) [computation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computation) that uses [aperiodic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aperiodic) electrical spikes, as opposed to the [periodic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Periodic_function) voltages in a digital computer or the continuously varying voltages in an analog computer.

Pulse pressure is the difference between [systolic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Systole) and [diastolic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diastole) [blood pressure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blood_pressure).

Pulsed-field gel electrophoresis (PFGE) is a technique used for the separation of large [DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA) [molecule](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Molecule)s by applying an [electric field](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electric_field) that periodically changes direction to a [gel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gel) matrix.
Pump-handle is a movement of the [rib](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rib)s that results in a change in the anteroposterior diameter of the [thorax](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thorax).

media.file: Boundary awards between 1899 and 1904 in the Puna de Atacama region.png

definition: Punctuated gradualism is a [microevolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microevolution)ary [hypothesis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hypothesis) that refers to a species that has Lohmann, G.

pupa (; : pupae) is the [life stage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biological_life_cycle) of [insect](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Insect)s from the [Holometabola](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Holometabola) [clade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clade) undergoing [metamorphosis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metamorphosis) between immature and mature stages.

Puppet-rearing is a method of breeding [birds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Birds) in [captivity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Captivity_(animal)) for [reintroduction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reintroduction) into the wild.

purD RNA motif is a conserved [RNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RNA) structure found in [Campylobacterota](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Campylobacterota), such as the genera [Helicobacter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Helicobacter) and [Campylobacter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Campylobacter).

Purinergic Signalling is a quarterly [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer_review) [scientific journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_journal) covering research on [purinergic signalling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Purinergic_signaling).
purma is a type of early successional forest, or [secondary forest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secondary_forest), in the [Amazon Basin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amazon_Basin).

Pursuit predation is a form of [predation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Predation) in which [predator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Predator)s actively give chase to their [prey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prey), either solitarily or [as a group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pack_hunter).
Pusztai affair is a controversy that began in 1998.
putative gene is an alignment segment of [DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA) that is believed to be a [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).

primary value learned value (PVLV) [model](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computer_simulation) is a possible explanation for the reward-predictive firing properties of [dopamine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dopamine) (DA) neurons.

definition: Recent human evolution refers to evolutionary [adaptation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adaptation), [sexual](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sexual_selection) and [natural selection](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Natural_selection), and [genetic drift](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetic_drift) within [Homo sapiens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human) populations, since their separation and dispersal in the [Middle Paleolithic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Middle_Paleolithic) about 50,000 years ago.

reciprocal causation arises when developing organisms are both products of [evolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evolution) as well as causes of evolution.
reciprocal cross is a breeding experiment designed to test the role of parental sex on a given inheritance pattern.

Reciprocal silencing, a [genetic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetics) phenomenon that primarily occurs in plants, refers to the pattern of redundant [genes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genes) being [silenced](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene_silencing) following a [polyploid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polyploidy) event.

[Reciprocity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reciprocity_(social_psychology)) in [evolutionary biology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evolutionary_biology) refers to mechanisms whereby the evolution of cooperative or altruistic behaviour may be favoured by the probability of future mutual interactions.

recognition sequence is a [DNA sequence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA_sequence) to which a [structural motif](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Structural_motif) of a [DNA-binding domain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA-binding_domain) exhibits [binding specificity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chemical_specificity).

Recombinant DNA (rDNA) molecules are [DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA) molecules formed by laboratory methods of [genetic recombination](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetic_recombination) (such as [molecular cloning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Molecular_cloning)) that bring together genetic material from multiple sources, creating [sequences](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA_sequence) that would not otherwise be found in the [genome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genome).

recombinant inbred strain or recombinant inbred line (RIL) is an organism with chromosomes that incorporate an essentially permanent set of recombination events between chromosomes inherited from two or more [inbred strain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inbred_strain)s.
Recombinases are [genetic recombination](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetic_recombination) [enzymes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enzymes).

RMCE (recombinase-mediated cassette exchange) is a procedure in [reverse genetics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reverse_genetics) allowing the systematic, repeated modification of higher eukaryotic genomes by targeted integration, based on the features of [site-specific recombination](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Site-specific_recombination) processes (SSRs).

Recombination hotspots are regions in a [genome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genome) that exhibit elevated rates of [recombination](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Homologous_recombination) relative to a neutral expectation.

rECOrd is a Local Biological Records Centre (LRC) serving [Cheshire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cheshire), [Halton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Halton_(borough)), [Warrington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warrington) and Wirral (including the [vice-county](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vice-counties) 'pan-handle' boundary around [Stockport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stockport)) - 'The Cheshire region'.

rectosigmoid junction, formerly the rectosigmoid sphincter or sphincter of O'Beirne, is the junction of the [sigmoid colon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sigmoid_colon) and the [rectum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rectum).

red clump is a clustering of [red giant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_giant)s in the [Hertzsprung–Russell diagram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hertzsprung–Russell_diagram) at around 5,000 K and [absolute magnitude](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Absolute_magnitude) (M == References == ==External links== *[http://www.astronomy.ohio-state.edu/~kstanek/CfA/RedClump/ Stanek's page on red clumps used for distance measurement] [[Category:Red giants]] [[Category:Stellar evolution]] [[Category:Standard candles]] [[Category:Concepts

red pulp of the [spleen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spleen) is composed of [connective tissue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Connective_tissue) known also as the [cords of Billroth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cords_of_Billroth) and many splenic [sinusoids](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sinusoid_(blood_vessel)) that are engorged with blood, giving it a red color.

Red Queen hypothesis is a [hypothesis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hypothesis) in [evolutionary biology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evolutionary_biology) proposed in 1973, that species must constantly [adapt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adaptation), [evolve](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evolution), and proliferate in order to survive while pitted against ever-evolving opposing species.
red-suffusion rose-faced lovebird (Agapornis roseicollis), also known as the red-pied lovebird, is not a true colour mutation of lovebird species.

Redfield ratio or Redfield stoichiometry is the consistent atomic ratio of [carbon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carbon), [nitrogen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nitrogen) and [phosphorus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phosphorus) found in marine [phytoplankton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phytoplankton) and throughout the deep oceans.

Redi Award is an international science award given to scientists who have made significant contributions in [toxinology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toxinology), the scientific study of [venoms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Venoms), [poisons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poisons) and [toxins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toxins).

reductive dechlorination describes any [chemical reaction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chemical_reaction) which [cleaves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bond_cleavage) the [covalent bond](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Covalent_bond) between [carbon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carbon) and [chlorine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chlorine) via [reductant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reductant)s, to release [chloride](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chloride) ions.
Reductive evolution is a process involving the progressive loss of genes, also known as reductive genomic evolution.

reedbed or reed bed is a natural [habitat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Habitat) found in [floodplain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Floodplain)s, waterlogged depressions and [estuaries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Estuary).

definition: reference ecosystem, also known as an ecological reference, is a Reference ecosystems usually include [remnant natural area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Remnant_natural_area)s that have not been degraded by human activities such as [agriculture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Agriculture), [logging](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Logging), [development](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Land_development), [[Fire_ecology#Examples of fire in different ecosystems|fire]] suppression, or [non-native species invasion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Invasive_species).

reference genome is a [genome assembly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genome_assembly) that represents the [complete genetic sequence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genome) of an organism as a continuous string of [nucleotide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nucleotide)s (A, T, C, and G).

Reflectins are a family of [intrinsically disordered proteins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intrinsically_disordered_proteins) evolved by a certain number of [cephalopods](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cephalopods) including [Euprymna scolopes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euprymna_scolopes) and [Doryteuthis opalescens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doryteuthis_opalescens) to produce [iridescent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iridescence) camouflage and signaling.

[Reflex](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reflex) bradycardia is a [bradycardia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bradycardia) (decrease in [heart rate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heart_rate)) in response to the [baroreceptor reflex](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baroreceptor_reflex), one of the body's homeostatic mechanisms for preventing abnormal increases in [blood pressure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blood_pressure).

Reflexogenous (reflexogenic) zone (or the receptive field of a reflex) is the area of the body stimulation of which causes a definite [unconditioned reflex](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unconditioned_response).

Refractoriness is the fundamental property of any object of [autowave](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Autowave) nature (especially [excitable medium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Excitable_medium)) not responding to stimuli, if the object stays in the specific refractory state.

refuge is a concept in [ecology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ecology), in which an organism obtains protection from [predation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Predation) by hiding in an area where it is inaccessible or cannot easily be found.

refugium (plural: refugia) is a location which supports an isolated or [relict](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Relict_(biology)) [population](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Population_(biology)) of a once more widespread species.

Refuse-derived fuel (RDF) is a [fuel produced from various types of waste](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waste-to-energy) such as [municipal solid waste](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Municipal_solid_waste) (MSW), [industrial waste](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Industrial_waste) or commercial waste.

Regeneration in [biology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biology) is the process of renewal, restoration, and tissue growth that makes [genome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genome)s, [cell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_(biology))s, [organisms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organisms), and [ecosystems](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ecosystems) [resilient](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Resilience_(ecology)) to natural fluctuations or events that cause disturbance or damage.

regeneration is the ability of an [ecosystem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ecosystem)specifically, the [environment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Environment_(biophysical)) and its living [population](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Population_(biology))to renew and recover from damage.

definition: Regeneration in humans refers to the restoration and sometimes limited regrowth of tissue following injury or as part of natural body processes.

Regenerative biology is a branch of [biology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biology) that studies the cellular and molecular mechanisms by which organisms replace or reconstitute cells, tissues, or body parts lost due to injury or cell death.

Regenerative design is about designing [systems](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Systems) and solutions that work with or mimic the ways that natural ecosystems return energy from less usable forms to more usable forms.

Regensburg Botanical Society (Regensburgische Botanische Gesellschaft), founded 1790 in the city of [Regensburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Regensburg), Bavaria, Germany, is the oldest extant scientific society focused on botany.

Regime shifts are large, abrupt, persistent changes in the structure and function of [ecosystem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ecosystem)s, the [climate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Climate), [financial system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Financial_system)s or other [complex systems](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Complex_systems).

regional differentiation, or regional specification is the process by which different areas are identified in the development of the early [embryo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Embryo).

Registry of Standard Biological Parts is a collection of genetic parts that are used in the assembly of systems and devices in [synthetic biology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Synthetic_biology).

definition: Reid's Paradox of Rapid Plant Migration or Reid's Paradox, describes the observation from the [paleoecological](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paleoecology) record that plant ranges shifted northward, after the [last glacial maximum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Last_Glacial_Maximum), at a faster rate than the [seed dispersal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seed_dispersal) rates commonly occur.

Reinforcement is a process of [speciation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Speciation) where [natural selection](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Natural_selection) increases the [reproductive isolation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reproductive_isolation) (further divided to [pre-zygotic isolation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pre-zygotic_isolation) and [post-zygotic isolation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post-zygotic_isolation)) between two populations of species.

Reinke crystals are rod-like [cytoplasmic inclusions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cytoplasmic_inclusions) which can be found in [Leydig cell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leydig_cell)s of the [testes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Testes).
Reinke's space is a potential space between the vocal ligament and the overlying mucosa.

Reinnervation is the restoration—either by spontaneous [cellular regeneration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Regeneration_(biology)) or by surgical reconstruction—of nerve supply to a body part from which it has been lost or damaged.

definition: relapse or recidivism is a recurrence of a past (typically medical) condition.

relationship between telomeres and longevity and changing the length of [telomere](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Telomere)s is one of the new fields of research on increasing human [lifespan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Longevity) and even human [immortality](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Immortality).

Relative apparent synapomorphy analysis, or RASA, is a method that aims to determine whether a given character is shared between [taxa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taxon) due to [shared ancestry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shared_ancestry) or due to [convergence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Convergence_(biology)).
Relative growth rate (RGR) is growth rate relative to size - that is, a rate of growth per unit time, as a proportion of its size at that moment in time.

Relative nonlinearity is a [coexistence mechanism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coexistence_theory) that maintains species diversity via differences in the response to and effect on variation in [resource](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Resource_(biology)) density or some other factor mediating competition.

relative rate test is a genetic comparative test between two ingroups (somewhat closely related species) and an [outgroup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Outgroup_(cladistics)) or “reference species” to compare mutation and evolutionary rates between the species.

Relative species abundance is a component of [biodiversity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biodiversity) and is a measure of how common or rare a species is relative to other species in a defined location or community.

relaxase is a single-strand DNA [transesterase](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transesterification) [enzyme](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enzyme) produced by some [prokaryote](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prokaryote)s and [virus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virus)es.

relaxation is the [emotional state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emotional_state) of low tension, in which there is an absence of [arousal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arousal), particularly from negative sources such as [anger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anger), [anxiety](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anxiety), or [fear](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fear).

relaxosome is the [complex of proteins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multiprotein_complex) that facilitates [plasmid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plasmid) transfer during [bacterial conjugation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bacterial_conjugation).

REM rebound is the lengthening and increasing frequency and depth of [rapid eye movement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rapid_eye_movement_sleep) (REM) sleep which occurs after periods of [sleep deprivation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sleep_deprivation).

remnant natural area, also known as remnant habitat, is an ecological [community](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Community_(ecology)) containing [native](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Native_species) flora and fauna that has not been significantly [disturbed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disturbance_(ecology)) by destructive activities such as [agriculture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Agriculture), [logging](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Logging), [pollution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pollution), [development](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Land_development), [[Fire_ecology#Examples of fire in different ecosystems|fire]] suppression, or [non-native species invasion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Invasive_species).

definition: renal [calyces](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calyx_(anatomy)) ( calyx) are conduits in the [kidney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kidney) through which urine passes.

renal capsule is a tough fibrous layer surrounding the [kidney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kidney) and covered in a layer of perirenal fat known as the [adipose capsule of kidney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adipose_capsule_of_kidney).

renal chloride reabsorption refers to the process by which the [kidneys](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kidneys), having filtered out [waste products](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metabolic_waste) from the [blood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blood) to be [excreted](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Excreted) as [urine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urine), re-absorb [chloride](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chloride) ions () from the waste.

renal cortex is the outer portion of the [kidney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kidney) between the [renal capsule](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Renal_capsule) and the [renal medulla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Renal_medulla).

renal fascia is a dense, [elastic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elastic_connective_tissue) [connective tissue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Connective_tissue) envelope enclosing the [kidney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kidney) and [adrenal gland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adrenal_gland), together with the layer of [perirenal fat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Perirenal_fat) surrounding these two.

Renal glucose reabsorption is the part of [kidney (renal) physiology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Renal_physiology) that deals with the retrieval of filtered [glucose](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glucose), preventing it from disappearing from the body through the urine.

renal hilum is the recessed central fissure of the [kidney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kidney) where its vessels, [nerve](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nerve)s and [ureter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ureter) (renal pedicle) pass.
renal medulla (Latin: medulla renis 'marrow of the kidney') is the innermost part of the [kidney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kidney).

Renal oligopeptide reabsorption is the part of [renal physiology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Renal_physiology) that deals with the retrieval of filtered [oligopeptide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oligopeptide)s, preventing them from disappearing from the body through the urine.
renal pelvis or pelvis of the kidney is the funnel-like dilated part of the [ureter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ureter) in the [kidney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kidney).

Renal protein reabsorption is the part of [renal physiology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Renal_physiology) that deals with the retrieval of filtered [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein)s, preventing them from disappearing from the body through the urine.

renal sinus is a cavity within the [kidney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kidney) which is occupied by the [renal pelvis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Renal_pelvis), [renal calyces](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Renal_calyx), blood vessels, nerves and fat.

renal sodium reabsorption refers to the process by which the [kidneys](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kidneys), having filtered out [waste products](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metabolic_waste) from the [blood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blood) to be [excreted](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Excreted) as [urine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urine), re-absorb [sodium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sodium) ions () from the waste.

Renal urea handling is the part of [renal physiology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Renal_physiology) that deals with the [reabsorption](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reabsorption) and [secretion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secretion) of [urea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urea).

definition: reniculate kidney is a multilobed [kidney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mammalian_kidney) found in [marine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marine_mammal) and [aquatic mammal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aquatic_mammal)s such as [pinniped](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pinniped)s ([seal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pinniped)s, [sea lion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sea_lion)s and [walrus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walrus)es) and [cetacean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cetacean)s ([dolphin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dolphin)s and [whale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Whale)s) but absent in terrestrial mammals except [bear](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bear)s.

Renin ([[#Discovery and naming|etymology and pronunciation]]), also known as an angiotensinogenase, is an [aspartic protease](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aspartic_protease) [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) and [enzyme](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enzyme) secreted by the [kidneys](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kidneys) that participates in the body's [renin–angiotensin–aldosterone system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Renin–angiotensin_system) (RAAS), which increases the volume of [extracellular fluid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Extracellular_fluid) ([blood plasma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blood_plasma), [lymph](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lymph), and [interstitial fluid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interstitial_fluid)) and causes arterial [vasoconstriction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vasoconstriction).
René Bernards (born 4 January 1953) is a Dutch cancer researcher.

definition: Reperfusion injury, sometimes called ischemia-reperfusion injury (IRI) or reoxygenation injury, is the [tissue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tissue_(biology)) damage caused when [blood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blood) supply returns to tissue ([[wikt:re-#Prefix|re-]] + [perfusion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Perfusion)) after a period of [ischemia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ischemia) or lack of oxygen (anoxia or [hypoxia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hypoxia_(medical))).

Replica plating is a [microbiological](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microbiology) technique in which one or more secondary [Petri plate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Petri_plate)s containing different solid ([agar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Agar)-based) [selective growth media](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Selective_medium) (lacking nutrients or containing chemical growth inhibitors such as [antibiotic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antibiotic)s) are inoculated with the same colonies of [microorganism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microorganism)s from a primary plate (or master dish), reproducing the original spatial pattern of colonies.
replicates are an experimental units that are treated identically.

replicator equation is a type of [dynamical system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dynamical_system) used in [evolutionary game theory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evolutionary_game_theory) to model how the frequency of strategies in a population changes over time.

replisome is a complex [molecular machine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Molecular_machine) that carries out [replication](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA_replication) of [DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA).

RAC otherwise known as Repository of Antibiotic resistance Cassettes is a [database](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biological_database) that uses the automatic Attacca annotation system in order to comprehensively annotate [gene-cassettes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene_cassette) and [transposable element](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transposable_element)s in a stream-lined manner and to discover novel gene cassettes.
Repoxygen was the tradename for a type of [gene therapy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene_therapy) to produce [erythropoietin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Erythropoietin) (EPO).

representational drift is a phenomenon describing the gradual change in how the [brain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brain) represents information over time, even when the information (and associated perception or behavior) itself remains constant.

repressilator is a [genetic regulatory network](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetic_regulatory_network) consisting of at least one [feedback loop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Feedback) with at least three genes, each expressing a protein that represses the next gene in the loop.

Reproductive interference is the interaction between individuals of different [species](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Species) during mate acquisition that leads to a reduction of [fitness](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fitness_(biology)) in one or more of the individuals involved.

reproductive isolation are a collection of [evolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evolution)ary mechanisms, [behaviors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethology) and [physiological processes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Physiology) critical for [speciation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Speciation).

Reproductive rights are [legal right](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legal_right)s and freedoms relating to [reproduction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_reproduction) and [reproductive health](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reproductive_health) that vary amongst countries around the world.
Reproductive success is an individual's production of offspring per breeding event or lifetime.
rescue effect is a phenomenon which was first described by Brown and Kodric-Brown, [[Category:Population ecology]] 14tcfvjarcii7ffhzm7p7o0hlsxkjsw

Research Institute of Molecular Pathology (IMP) is a biomedical research center, which conducts curiosity-driven [basic research](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basic_research) in the [molecular](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Molecular_biology) [life sciences](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Life_sciences).

residence time of a [fluid parcel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fluid_parcel) is the total time that the parcel has spent inside a [control volume](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Control_volume) (e.g.: a [chemical reactor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chemical_reactor), a [lake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake_retention_time), a [human body](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_body)).

Resin canals or resin ducts are [fusiform](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fusiform) intercellular spaces surrounded by [epithelial cells](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Epithelium) which secrete [resin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Resin).

definition: resistance is the property of [communities](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Community_(ecology)) or populations to remain ==References== [[Category:Ecology terminology]] [[Category:Ecological restoration]] [[Category:Conservation biology]] 65talewaegqh1tld8fvo05crovt7m2j
resistance gene is any [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene) producing resistance against an agent.

resonating device is a structure used by an [animal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Animal) that improves the quality of its [vocalizations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Animal_communication) through amplifying the sound produced via [acoustic resonance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Acoustic_resonance).
Resources are all the materials available in the environment which are technologically accessible, economically feasible and culturally sustainable and help to satisfy needs and wants.

resource is a substance or object in the environment required by an organism for normal [growth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Developmental_biology), maintenance, and [reproduction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reproduction).
The resource fragmentation hypothesis was first proposed by Janzen Janzen, D.
resource holding potential (RHP) is the ability of an animal to win an all-out fight if one were to take place.

Resource selection functions (RSFs) are a class of functions that are used in [spatial ecology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spatial_ecology) to assess which [habitat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Habitat) characteristics are important to a specific population or species of animal, by assessing a probability of that animal using a certain resource proportional to the availability of that resource in the environment.
resource-use hypothesis is a [macroevolutionary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Macroevolutionary) theory proposed by [paleontologist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paleontologist) [[Elisabeth S.

Respiratory adaptation is the specific change that the [respiratory system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Respiratory_system) undergoes in response to the demands of [physical exertion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Physical_exercise).

respiratory center is located in the [medulla oblongata](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medulla_oblongata) and [pons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pons), in the [brainstem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brainstem).

respiratory quotient (RQ or respiratory coefficient) is a [dimensionless number](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dimensionless_quantity) used in calculations of [basal metabolic rate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basal_metabolic_rate) (BMR) when estimated from carbon dioxide production.

respiratory rate is the rate at which [breathing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Breathing) occurs; it is set and controlled by the [respiratory center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Respiratory_center) of the brain.

respiratory system is the system with which it introduces respiratory [gas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gas)es to its interior and performs [gas exchange](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gas_exchange).
respiratory system of the horse is the biological system by which a [horse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horse) circulates air for the purpose of gaseous exchange.

respiratory tract is the subdivision of the [respiratory system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Respiratory_system) involved with the process of conducting air to the [alveoli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pulmonary_alveolus) for the purposes of [gas exchange](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gas_exchange) in [mammal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mammal)s.

Respirocytes are hypothetical, microscopic, [artificial](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artificial_cell) [red blood cell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_blood_cell)s that are intended to emulate the function of their organic counterparts, so as to supplement or replace the function of much of the human body's normal [respiratory system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Respiratory_system).

response to sneezing is a [customary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Customary) verbal acknowledgement, [blessing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blessing), or [polite phrase](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Etiquette) uttered by a witness to another person's [sneeze](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sneeze).
resting spore is a resistant cell, adapted to survive adverse environmental conditions.
Reston virus (RESTV) is one of six known viruses within the [genus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genus) [Ebolavirus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ebolavirus).

Restorative Neurology and Neuroscience is a bimonthly [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer-reviewed) [medical journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medical_journal) published by [IOS Press](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IOS_Press) that was established in 1989.
restriction digest is a procedure used to prepare [DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA) for analysis or other processing.

restriction enzyme, restriction endonuclease, REase, ENase or restrictase is an [enzyme](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enzyme) that cleaves [DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA) into fragments at or near specific recognition sites within molecules known as [restriction site](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Restriction_site)s.

definition: restriction fragment is a [DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA) fragment resulting from the cutting of a DNA strand by a [restriction enzyme](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Restriction_enzyme) (restriction endonucleases).

restriction fragment length polymorphism (RFLP) is a technique that exploits variations in [homologous](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Homology_(biology)) [DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA) sequences, known as [polymorphisms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene_polymorphism), in order to distinguish individuals, populations, or species in order to pinpoint the locations of [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene)s within a sequence.

Restriction landmark genomic scanning (RLGS) is a [genome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genome) analysis method for rapid simultaneous visualization of thousands of landmarks, or [restriction sites](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Restriction_enzyme).
restriction map is a map of known [restriction sites](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Restriction_sites) within a sequence of [DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA).

restriction modification system (RM system) is found in [bacteria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bacteria) and [archaea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Archaea), and provides a defense against foreign [DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA), such as that borne by [bacteriophage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bacteriophage)s.

restriction sites, or restriction recognition sites, are regions of a [DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA) molecule containing specific (4-8 [base pair](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Base_pair)s in length [https://www.nullomers.org/ Nullomers Database] contains a comprehensive catalogue of minimal absent motifs many of which might potentially be not-yet-known restriction motifs.

resurrection plant is a plant that can survive extreme dehydration of its vegetative tissues and resume normal metabolic activity upon rehydration.

rete mirabile ([Latin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latin) for 'wonderful net'; : retia mirabilia) is a complex of [arteries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artery) and [vein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vein)s lying very close to each other, found in some [vertebrate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vertebrate)s, mainly [warm-blooded](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warm-blooded) ones.

Reticulate evolution, or network evolution is the origination of a [lineage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lineage_(evolution)) through the partial merging of two ancestor lineages, leading to relationships better described by a [phylogenetic network](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phylogenetic_network) than a bifurcating [tree](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phylogenetic_tree).
reticuloendothelial system (abbreviated RES) is a network of immune cells distributed throughout the body that defends against foreign invaders, clears cellular debris, and recycles iron.
reticulum is the second chamber in the four-chamber [alimentary canal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alimentary_canal) of a [ruminant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ruminant) mammal.

Horizontal cells are the laterally interconnecting neurons having cell bodies in the [inner nuclear layer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inner_nuclear_layer) of the [retina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Retina) of [vertebrate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vertebrate) eyes.
retinal nerve fiber layer (RNFL) or nerve fiber layer, stratum opticum, is part of the [anatomy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anatomy) of the [eye](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eye).
Retinal precursor cells are biological cells that differentiate into the various cell types of the [retina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Retina) during development.

Retinal waves are spontaneous bursts of [action potentials](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Action_potentials) that propagate in a wave-like fashion across the developing [retina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Retina).

retinalophototroph is one of two different types of [phototroph](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phototroph)s, and are named for [retinal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Retinal)-binding proteins ([microbial rhodopsin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microbial_rhodopsin)s) they utilize for cell signaling and converting light into energy.

retinohypothalamic tract (RHT) is a photic neural [input pathway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neural_pathway) involved in the [circadian rhythms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Circadian_rhythms) of [mammal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mammal)s.

Retinylidene proteins, or rhodopsins [in a broad sense](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sensu_lato), are proteins that use [retinal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Retinal) as a [chromophore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chromophore) for [light](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Light) reception.

Retromer is a complex of [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein)s that has been shown to be important in recycling [transmembrane receptors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transmembrane_receptors) from [endosome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Endosome)s to the [trans-Golgi network](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golgi_apparatus) (TGN) and directly back to the plasma membrane.

definition: Reunification of Brittany or Breton Reunification is a political movement to reunite the [Loire-Atlantique](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loire-Atlantique) department with the [administrative region of Brittany](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brittany_(administrative_region)), to form the entire cultural and historical region of [Brittany](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brittany).
Reverse complement polymerase chain reaction (RC-PCR) is a modification of the [polymerase chain reaction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polymerase_chain_reaction) (PCR).
Reverse ecology refers to the use of [genomics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genomics) to study or predict an organism's [ecology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ecology).

Reverse genetics is a method in [molecular genetics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Molecular_genetics) that is used to help understand the function(s) of a [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene) by analysing the [phenotypic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phenotype) effects caused by [genetically engineering](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetic_engineering) specific [nucleic acid sequence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nucleic_acid_sequence)s within the gene.
reverse migration is the phenomenon in which some neutrophils migrate away from the inflammation site, against the chemokine gradient, during inflammation resolution.
reverse northern blot is a method by which gene expression patterns may be analyzed by comparing isolated RNA molecules from a tester sample to samples in a control cDNA library.

Reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) is a laboratory technique combining [reverse transcription](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reverse_transcription) of [RNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RNA) into [DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA) (in this context called [complementary DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Complementary_DNA) or cDNA) and amplification of specific DNA targets using [polymerase chain reaction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polymerase_chain_reaction) (PCR).
Reverse transfection is a technique for the transfer of [genetic material](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene) into [cells](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_(biology)).

Reversible Michaelis–Menten kinetics, using the reversible form of the [Michaelis–Menten equation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michaelis–Menten_kinetics), is therefore important when developing computer models of [cellular processes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biochemical_systems_equation) involving enzymes.

Revue suisse de Zoologie (English: Swiss Journal of Zoology) is a biannual [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer-reviewed) [scientific journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_journal) for [zoological systematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taxonomy_(biology)).

Reward dependence (RD) is characterized as a tendency to respond markedly to signals of [reward](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reward_system), particularly to verbal signals of social approval, social support, and sentiment.

Reward devaluation refers to a psychological and neurobiological phenomenon where the subjective value or motivational significance of a reward diminishes over time, often due to repeated exposure, satiation, or changes in contextual relevance.

Rewilding is a form of [ecological restoration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ecological_restoration) aimed at increasing [biodiversity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biodiversity) and restoring natural processes.
