definition: Rfam is a [database](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Database) containing information about [non-coding RNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-coding_RNA) (ncRNA) families and other structured RNA elements.

Rhabdites (from Greek, rhabdos, rod) are rodlike structures in the cells of the [epidermis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Epidermis_(skin)) or underlying parenchyma in certain [turbellarians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turbellarians), and in the epidermis of [nemertea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nemertea)ns.
rheophile is an animal that prefers to live in fast-moving water.

(Positive) Rheotaxis is a form of [taxis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taxis), or movement in response to [stimuli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stimulus_(physiology)), seen in many aquatic organisms like [fish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fish).

rhinophore is one of a pair of [chemosensory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chemoreceptor) club-shaped, rod-shaped or ear-like structures which are the most prominent part of the external head anatomy in [sea slugs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sea_slugs), [marine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marine_(ocean)) [gastropod](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gastropod) [opisthobranch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Opisthobranch) [mollusk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mollusk)s such as the [nudibranchs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nudibranchs), sea hares ([Aplysiomorpha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aplysiomorpha)), and sap-sucking sea slugs ([Sacoglossa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sacoglossa)).
rhizines are [multicellular](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multicellular_organism) [root](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Root)-like structures arising mainly from the lower surface.
Rhizobacteria are root-associated [bacteria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bacteria) that can have a detrimental (parasitic varieties), neutral or beneficial effect on plant growth.

Rhizobia are [diazotrophic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diazotrophic) [bacteria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bacteria) that [fix nitrogen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nitrogen_fixation) after becoming established inside the [root nodule](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Root_nodule)s of [legume](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legume)s ([Fabaceae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fabaceae)).

Rhizoids are [[wiktionary:protuberance|protuberances]] that extend from the lower [epidermal cells](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Epidermis_(botany)) of [bryophyte](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryophyte)s and [algae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Algae).

rhizoplast (also known as internal flagellar root, fibrous root or cross-banded root) is an [organelle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organelle) present in a variety of [flagellate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flagellate)s, including [ochrophyte](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ochrophyte) and [chlorophyte](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chlorophyte) algae and some [fungi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fungi).

definition: Rhizostomins are [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein)s that are part of a [pigment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pigment) family only found in [jellyfish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jellyfish) in the order [Rhizostomeae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhizostomeae).

Rho utilisation site, also known by the acronym rut, is a sequence of RNA in [bacteria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bacteria) upstream of the terminator region which serves as a binding site for the protein known as [rho factor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rho_factor).

rhombic lip is a posterior section of the developing [metencephalon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metencephalon) which can be recognized transiently within the vertebrate embryo.

rhombus of Michaelis, also known as the Michaelis-Raute or the quadrilateral of Michaelis, is a [rhombus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhombus)-shaped contour (also referred to as kite-shaped or diamond-shaped) that is sometimes visible on the lower human back.

definition: ribs () are the long curved [bone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bone)s which form the [rib cage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rib_cage), part of the [axial skeleton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Axial_skeleton).

rib cage or thoracic cage is an [endoskeletal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Endoskeletal) enclosure in the [thorax](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thorax) of most [vertebrate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vertebrate)s that comprises the [rib](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rib)s, [vertebral column](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vertebral_column) and [sternum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sternum), which protect the [vital organ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vital_organ)s of the [thoracic cavity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thoracic_cavity), such as the [heart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heart), [lung](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lung)s and [great vessels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_vessels) and support the [shoulder girdle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shoulder_girdle) to form the [core](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Core_(anatomy)) part of the [axial skeleton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Axial_skeleton).

definition: Ribonucleoprotein]] Networks Analyzed by Mutational Profiling (RNP-MaP) is a strategy for probing [RNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RNA)-[protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) networks and protein binding sites at a [nucleotide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nucleotide) resolution.

[Ribosomal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ribosome) frameshifting, also known as translational frameshifting or translational recoding, is a biological phenomenon that occurs during [translation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Translation_(biology)) that results in the production of multiple, unique [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein)s from a single [mRNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Messenger_RNA).

Ribosomal RNA (rRNA) intergenic spacer analysis (RISA) is a method of [microbial community](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microbial_community) analysis that provides a means of comparing differing environments or treatment impacts without the bias imposed by culture-dependent approaches.

definition: Ribosomally synthesized and post-translationally modified peptides (RiPPs), also known as ribosomal natural products, are a diverse class of [natural products](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Natural_product) of [ribosomal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ribosomal) origin.

Ribosome profiling, or Ribo-Seq (also named ribosome footprinting), is an adaptation of a technique developed by [Joan Steitz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joan_Steitz) and [Marilyn Kozak](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marilyn_Kozak) almost 50 years ago that [Nicholas Ingolia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nicholas_Ingolia) and [Jonathan Weissman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jonathan_Weissman) adapted to work with [next generation sequencing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Next_generation_sequencing) that uses specialized messenger RNA ([mRNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MRNA)) sequencing to determine which mRNAs are being actively [translated](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Translation_(biology)).

ribosome binding site, or ribosomal binding site (RBS), is a sequence of [nucleotides](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nucleotides) upstream of the [start codon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Start_codon) of an [mRNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MRNA) transcript that is responsible for the recruitment of a [ribosome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ribosome) during the initiation of [translation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Translation_(biology)).
Ribotyping is a molecular technique for bacterial identification and characterization that uses information from [rRNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ribosomal_RNA)-based phylogenetic analyses.

Self-agency, also known as the phenomenal will, is the sense that actions are self-generated.

Self-incompatibility (SI) is a general name for any genetic mechanism that prevents [self-fertilization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Self-fertilization) in fertile [hermaphroditic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hermaphrodite) organisms, and thus encourages [outcross](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Outcross)ing and [allogamy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Allogamy).

self-transforming brain refers to the ability of the self to consciously use mental activity to change/modify the brain's neural network in order to experience life with more happiness and fulfillment.

Sellar region is a small area in the [central nervous system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_nervous_system) (CNS) that includes the [sella turcica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sella_turcica), [cavernous sinus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cavernous_sinus), suprasellar cistern, and [pituitary gland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pituitary_gland).

Semi-deciduous or semi-evergreen is a botanical term which refers to [plant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plant)s that lose their [foliage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foliage) for a very short period, when old [leaves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leaves) fall off and new foliage growth is starting.

semi-field study or semifield study is a type of [scientific investigation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_study) which is intermediate between [laboratory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laboratory) study and open [field research](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Field_research).

Semi-slugs, also spelled semislugs, are land [gastropod](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gastropod)s whose [shells](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gastropod_shell) are too small for them to retract into, but not quite [vestigial](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vestigiality).

semiaquatic refers to various [macro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Macroscopic)-[organism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organism)s that live regularly in both [aquatic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aquatic_environment) and [terrestrial environment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Terrestrial_ecosystem)s.
Bovine seminal RNase (BS-RNase) is a member of the ribonuclease superfamily produced by the bovine seminal vesicles.

Semper's organ is an [anatomical structure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anatomy), a [gland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gland) located in the [head](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Head) of some [land snail](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Land_snail)s, [pulmonate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pulmonata) [gastropod](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gastropod) [mollusk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mollusc)s.

SENSE Lab is [[wikt:sensory|Sensory]] Encoding and Neuro- Sensory Engineering Lab in [Halifax, Nova Scotia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Halifax,_Nova_Scotia), Canada.

sense of agency (SoA), or sense of control, is the [subjective](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Subjectivity) [awareness](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Awareness) of initiating, executing, and controlling one's own [volition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volition_(psychology))al actions in the world.

definition: sensory drive hypothesis is a hypothesis in [population ecology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Population_ecology) that posits that when local environmental conditions differ between [conspecific populations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conspecific), [communication systems](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Animal_communication) will adapt to these conditions.
Sensory ecology is a relatively new field focusing on the [information](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Information) organisms obtain about their environment.

Sensory history is an area of [academic study](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academic_study) which examines the role conceptions of our [senses](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Five_senses) have played in the past.

definition: Sensory maps and brain development is a concept in [neuroethology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neuroethology) that links the development of the brain over an animal’s lifetime with the fact that there is spatial organization and pattern to an animal’s sensory processing.

Sensory neuroscience is a subfield of [neuroscience](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neuroscience) which explores the anatomy and physiology of [neuron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neuron)s that are part of [sensory system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sensory_system)s such as vision, hearing, and olfaction.
Sensory substitution is a change of the characteristics of one [sensory modality](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sensory_modality) into stimuli of another sensory modality.

sensory trap hypothesis describes an [evolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evolution)ary idea that revolves around [mating](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mating) behavior and female [mate choice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mate_choice).

Septate junctions are intercellular junctions found in [invertebrate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Invertebrate) epithelial cells, appearing as ladder-like structures under [electron microscopy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electron_microscope).

Septins are a group of [GTP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guanosine_triphosphate)-[binding protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Molecular_binding)s [expressed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene_expression) in all [eukaryotic cells](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eukaryote) except [plant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plant)s.

septum ([Latin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latin_language) for something that encloses; septa) is a wall, dividing a [cavity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Body_cavity) or structure into smaller ones.
septum (plural septa) is one of the radiating vertical plates lying within the [corallite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corallite) wall.

septum glandis, also septum of the glans, refers to the [fibrous](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fiber) partition of the ventral aspect of the [glans penis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glans_penis) that separates the two glans wings in the ventral midline.

septum transversum is a thick mass of cranial [mesenchyme](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mesenchyme), formed in the [embryo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Embryo), that gives rise to parts of the [thoracic diaphragm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thoracic_diaphragm) and the [ventral mesentery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ventral_mesentery) of the foregut in the developed human being and other mammals.

sequence alignment is a way of arranging the sequences of [DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA), [RNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RNA), or protein to identify regions of similarity that may be a consequence of functional, [structural](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Structural_biology), or [evolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evolution)ary relationships between the sequences.
Sequence graph, also called an alignment graph, breakpoint graph, or adjacency graph, are bidirected graphs used in [comparative genomics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comparative_genomics).

Sequence homology is the [biological homology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Homology_(biology)) between [DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA_sequence), [RNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RNA_sequence), or [protein sequences](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein_primary_structure), defined in terms of shared ancestry in the [evolutionary history of life](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evolutionary_history_of_life).

sequence learning is inherent to human ability because it is an integrated part of conscious and nonconscious learning as well as activities.
Sequence Ontology (SO) is an [ontology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ontology_(information_science)) suitable for describing [biological sequences](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sequence_(biology)).

Sequence saturation mutagenesis (SeSaM) is a chemo-enzymatic [random mutagenesis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mutagenesis_(molecular_biology_technique)) method applied for the [directed evolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Directed_evolution) of [proteins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Proteins) and [enzymes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enzymes).

sequence space is a way of representing all possible sequences (for a [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein), [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene) or [genome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genome)).

Sergei Popov is a Russian biologist and [bioweaponeer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biological_warfare) formerly in the [Soviet biological weapons program](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soviet_biological_weapons_program).

Serial homology is a special type of [homology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Homology_(biology)), defined by Owen as demonstrating that shared developmental pathways structure the covariation of serially homologous limbs.
Serial passage is the process of growing [bacteria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bacteria) or a [virus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virus) in iterations.

serotonin transporter (SERT or 5-HTT), also known as the sodium-dependent serotonin transporter and [solute carrier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Solute_carrier_family) family 6 member 4, is a [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) that in humans is encoded by the SLC6A4 [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).

serotype or serovar is a distinct variation within a [species](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Species) of [bacteria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bacteria) or [virus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virus) or among [immune cells](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Immune_cells) of different individuals.

serous fluid or serosal fluid (originating from the [Medieval Latin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medieval_Latin) word serosus, from [Latin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latin) serum) is any of various [body fluid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Body_fluid)s resembling [serum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Serum_(blood)), that are typically pale yellow or transparent and of a [benign](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benign) nature.
Serra Negra Biological Reserve () is a [Biological reserve](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biological_reserve_(Brazil)) in the state of Pernambuco, Brazil.

Serratus is a large scale [viroinformatics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Viroinformatics) platform for uncovering the total genetic diversity of Earth's [virome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virome).

Serum Metabolome database is a free web database about small molecule [metabolites](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metabolites) found in human [serum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Serum_(blood)) and their concentration values.
Sessility, a property of certain [animals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Animal), is a lack of self-locomotion.
Seston (from ) refers to the particles suspended in bodies of water, such as oceans, lakes, and rivers.
setae (; seta ; ) are any of a number of different bristle- or [hair](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hair)-like structures on living [organism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organism)s.

definition: Sex linkage describes the sex-specific patterns of [inheritance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heredity) and [presentation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phenotype) when a [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene) [mutation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mutation) ([allele](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Allele)) is present on a [sex chromosome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sex_chromosome) (allosome) rather than a non-sex chromosome ([autosome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Autosome)).

Sex pheromones are [pheromone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pheromone)s released by an organism to attract an individual of the same species, encourage it to mate with it, or perform some other function closely related with [sexual reproduction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sexual_reproduction).
Dosage compensation is the process by which organisms equalize the expression of genes between members of different biological sexes.

Sex-limited genes are [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene)s that are present in both sexes of [sexually reproducing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sexual_reproduction) [species](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Species) but are expressed in only one sex and have no [penetrance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penetrance), or are simply 'turned off' in the other.
Sex-linked barring is a plumage pattern on individual feathers in chickens, which is characterized by alternating pigmented and apigmented bars.

Sexual antagonistic co-evolution is the relationship between males and females where sexual morphology changes over time to counteract the opposite's [sex traits](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sex_traits) to achieve the maximum [reproductive success](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reproductive_success).
Sexual bimaturism describes a difference in developmental timing between males and females of the same species.

Sexual characteristics are physical traits of an [organism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organism) (typically of a [sexually dimorphic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sexually_dimorphic) organism) which are indicative of or resultant from biological [sex](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sex)ual factors.
Sexual differentiation in humans is the process of development of [sex differences in humans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sex_differences_in_humans).

Sexual dimorphism is the condition where different [sex](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sex)es of the same [species](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Species) exhibit different [morphological](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morphology_(biology)) characteristics, including characteristics not directly involved in [reproduction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reproduction).

definition: Sexual dimorphism in human bonding refers to the sex-based differences in how humans form, maintain, and experience social and emotional bonds, including romantic partnerships, parent-child relationships, [friendships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Friendship) and broader social connections.

Sexual reproduction is a type of [reproduction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reproduction) that involves a complex [life cycle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biological_life_cycle) in which a [gamete](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gamete) ([haploid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haploid) reproductive cells, such as a [sperm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sperm) or [egg cell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Egg_cell)) with a single set of [chromosome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chromosome)s combines with another gamete to produce a [zygote](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zygote) that develops into an organism composed of [cells](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_(biology)) with two sets of chromosomes ([diploid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diploid)).

sexual segregation is the differential use of [space](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spatial_ecology), [habitat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Habitat)s, and resources by males and females, or the separation of males and females into different [social groups](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sociality) outside the breeding season.

Sexual selection is a mechanism of [evolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evolution) in which members of one [sex](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sex) [choose mates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mate_choice) of the other sex (intersexual selection) to [mate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mating) with, and compete with members of the same sex for access to members of the opposite sex (intrasexual selection).

sexual system is a distribution of [male](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Male) and [female](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Female) functions across [organism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organism)s in a [species](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Species).

shade tolerance is a [plant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plant)'s ability to tolerate low [light](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Light) levels.

shade tree is a large tree whose primary role is to provide shade in the surrounding environment due to its spreading [canopy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canopy_(forest)) and [crown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crown_(botany)), where it may give shelter from [sunlight](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sunlight) in the heat of the summer for people who seek recreational needs in [urban parks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urban_parks) and house [yard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Front_yard)s, and thus, also protecting them from the sun's harmful UV rays.

shadow biosphere is a hypothetical [microbial](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microbe) [biosphere](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biosphere) of Earth that would use radically different [biochemical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biochemistry) and [molecular](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Molecular_biology) processes from those of known life.

Shallow-water blackout is loss of consciousness at a shallow depth due to [hypoxia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hypoxia_(medical)) during a [dive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Underwater_diving), which could be the result of any one of significantly differing causative circumstances.

Specific leaf area (SLA) is the quotient of [leaf](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leaf) area to leaf [dry mass](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dry_mass); it has [SI units](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SI_units) of square centimeters per kilogram (cm²/kg).

Specific Physical Preparedness (abbreviated SPP), also referred to by Sports-specific Physical Preparedness is the status of being prepared for the movements in a specific activity (usually a [sport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sport)).

specific ventilation is defined as the ratio of the volume of gas entering a region of the lung (ΔV) following an inspiration, divided by the end-expiratory volume (V [Xe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xenon)) or proton MRI (oxygen enhanced imaging).
specific-locus test (SLT) is a genetic test to assess the impact of mutagens such as radiation or chemicals on mutation rates in a selected set of easily measured genes.
Specified complexity is a creationist [intelligent design](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intelligent_design) argument introduced by [William Dembski](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Dembski).

Sperm chemotaxis is a form of [sperm guidance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sperm_guidance), in which [sperm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sperm) cells ([spermatozoa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spermatozoa)) follow a [concentration gradient](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Concentration_gradient) of a [chemoattractant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chemoattractant) secreted from the [oocyte](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oocyte) and thereby reach the oocyte.

Sperm competition is the competitive process between [spermatozoa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spermatozoon) of two or more different males to [fertilize](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fertility) the same [egg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Egg_cell) Pound, N.

Sperm guidance is the process by which [sperm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sperm) cells ([spermatozoa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spermatozoa)) are directed to the [oocyte](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oocyte) (egg) for the aim of [fertilization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fertilization).
Sperm precedence is the tendency of a female who has bred with multiple males to give birth to the offspring of those males in unequal proportions.

Sperm thermotaxis is a form of sperm guidance, in which [sperm cell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sperm_cell)s (spermatozoa) actively change their swimming direction according to a temperature gradient, swimming up the gradient.

definition: Spermarche, also known as semenarche, is the time at which a male experiences his first ejaculation.

spermatophylax is a [gelatinous](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gelatine) [bolus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bolus_(digestion)) which some male [insect](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Insect)s eject during [copulation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copulation_(zoology)) with females through their [aedeagi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aedeagus) together with [spermatophore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spermatophore)s, and which functions as a [nutritive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nutrition) supplement for the female.
spermosphere is the zone surrounding a seed where soil, microorganisms, and seed [germinating](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germination) interact.

sphaeroblast is a woody extrusion from the [trunk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trunk_(botany)) or [branch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Branch) of a [tree](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tree), usually taking the form of a rounded spherical shape, as if the tree had a boil or mole.
Sphaerotilus natans is an aquatic [periphyton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Periphyton) bacterial organism associated with polluted water.
Cicada killer wasps ([genus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genus) Sphecius) are large, solitary, ground-dwelling, predatory [wasp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wasp)s.

sphincter of Boyden (also known as the choledochal sphincter) is a [sphincter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sphincter) located in the [common bile duct](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Common_bile_duct) before it joins with the [pancreatic duct](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pancreatic_duct) to form the [ampulla of vater](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ampulla_of_vater).

Sphingolipids are a class of [lipid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lipid)s containing a backbone of sphingoid bases, which are a set of [aliphatic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aliphatic) [amino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amino) [alcohol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alcohol_(chemistry))s that includes [sphingosine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sphingosine).

Sphingomyelin (SM, ) is a type of [sphingolipid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sphingolipid) found in animal [cell membranes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_membranes), especially in the membranous [myelin sheath](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Myelin_sheath) that surrounds some [nerve cell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nerve_cell) [axons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Axons).
spicules, also known as copulatory spicules, are needle-like mating structures found only in males.

Spiculectomy is a minor soft-tissue [surgical procedure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Surgical_procedure) to remove a spicule or splinter, often a fragment of [toenail](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nail_(anatomy)), penetrating the nail bed.

Spiegelman's Monster is an [RNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RNA) chain of only 218 [nucleotides](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nucleotides) that is able to be reproduced by the RNA replication enzyme [RNA-dependent RNA polymerase](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RNA-dependent_RNA_polymerase), also called RNA replicase.

Spike directivity is a [vector](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gradient_vector) that quantifies changes in transient charge density during [action potential](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Action_potential) propagation.

Spike-in controls or spike-ins are known quantities of molecules—such as [oligonucleotide sequences](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oligonucleotide_sequence) (RNA, DNA), [proteins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein), or [metabolites](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metabolite)—added to a biological sample for more accurate quantitative estimation of the molecule of interest across samples and batches.

Spike-triggered covariance (STC) analysis is a tool for characterizing a neuron's response properties using the [covariance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Covariance) of stimuli that elicit spikes from a neuron.
Spiking neural networks (SNNs) are [artificial neural network](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artificial_neural_network)s (ANN) that mimic natural neural networks.

definition: Spin column-based nucleic acid purification is a [solid phase extraction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Solid_phase_extraction) method to quickly purify [nucleic acid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nucleic_acid)s.

spinal column, also known as the vertebral column, spine or backbone, is the core part of the [axial skeleton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Axial_skeleton) in [vertebrate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vertebrate)s.

spindle apparatus is the [cytoskeletal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cytoskeletal) structure of [eukaryotic cell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eukaryotic_cell)s that forms during [cell division](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_division) to separate [sister chromatid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sister_chromatid)s between daughter [cells](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_(biology)).

spinneret is a [silk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spider_silk)-spinning [organ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organ_(anatomy)) of a [spider](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spider) or the [larva](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Larva) of an [insect](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Insect).

Spirometry (meaning the measuring of breath) is the most common of the [pulmonary function test](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pulmonary_function_test)s (PFTs).

Spitzenkörper ([German](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German_language) for 'pointed body', SPK) is a structure found in fungal [hyphae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hyphae) that is the organizing center for hyphal growth and [morphogenesis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morphogenesis).

splanchnocranium (or visceral skeleton) is the portion of the [cranium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cranium) that is derived from [pharyngeal arch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pharyngeal_arch)es.

Spleen pain is a pain felt from the left upper [quadrant of the abdomen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abdominal_pain) or [epigastrium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Epigastrium) where the human [spleen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spleen) is located or neighboring.
Spleen transplantation is the transfer of [spleen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spleen) or its fragments from one individual to another.
splenectomy is the [surgical procedure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Surgery) that partially or completely removes the [spleen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spleen).
splenic injury, which includes a ruptured spleen, is any injury to the [spleen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spleen).

splenorenal recess (perisplenic space, pouch of Koller, or Koller's pouch) is the [intraperitoneal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peritoneal_cavity) compartment that separates the [spleen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spleen) and the left [kidney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kidney).
Splenosis is the result of [spleen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spleen) tissue breaking off the main organ and implanting at another site inside the body.

Society for the Promotion of LCA Development (SPOLD) was the association of multiple companies that wanted to create a file format that would help mold [Life-cycle assessment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Life-cycle_assessment) (LCA) software into a better management tool.
Sponge microbiomes are diverse communities of microorganisms in symbiotic association with marine [sponge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sponge)s as their hosts.

sporocarp (also known as fruiting body, fruit body or fruitbody) of [fungi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fungi) is a [multicellular structure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multicellular_organism) on which [spore-producing structures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sporangium), such as [basidia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basidium) or [asci](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ascus), are borne.

stable ocean hypothesis (SOH) is one of several hypotheses within larval fish [ecology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ecology) that attempt to explain recruitment variability (Figure 1; Excellent research focusing on early life history and larval recruitment mechanisms was done from 1960–1990, and this body of research, including Lasker's, laid the basis for larval ecology studies today.

Stable-isotope probing (SIP) is a technique in [microbial ecology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microbial_ecology) for tracing uptake of [nutrient](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nutrient)s in [biogeochemical cycling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biogeochemical_cycling) by microorganisms.

staggered extension process (also referred to as StEP) is a common technique used in [biotechnology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biotechnology) and [molecular biology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Molecular_biology) to create new, mutated genes with qualities of one or more initial genes.
Staining is a technique used to enhance contrast in samples, generally at the [microscopic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microscope) level.
stamen (: stamina or stamens) is a part consisting of the male [reproductive organ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reproductive_organ)s of a flower.
Stamford Raffles Award is an award of the [Zoological Society of London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zoological_Society_of_London).
staminode is an often rudimentary, sterile or abortive [stamen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stamen), which means that it does not produce [pollen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pollen).

standard solar model (SSM) is a mathematical [model](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Model) of the [Sun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sun) as a [spherical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spherical) ball of gas (in varying states of [ionisation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ionisation), with the hydrogen in the deep interior being a completely ionised [plasma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plasma_(physics))).

Standards for Reporting Enzymology Data (STRENDA) is an initiative as part of the [Minimum Information Standard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minimum_Information_Standard)s which specifically focuses on the development of guidelines for reporting (describing metadata) enzymology experiments.

Starling principle holds that fluid movement across a semi-permeable blood vessel such as a capillary or small venule is determined by the [hydrostatic pressures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pressure) and [colloid osmotic pressures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colloid_osmotic_pressure) ([oncotic pressure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oncotic_pressure)) on either side of a semipermeable barrier that sieves the filtrate, retarding larger molecules such as proteins from leaving the blood stream.

start codon is the first [codon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Codon) of a [messenger RNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Messenger_RNA) (mRNA) transcript translated by a [ribosome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ribosome).

Starvation response in animals (including humans) is a set of adaptive [biochemical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biochemical) and [physiological](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Physiological) changes, triggered by lack of food or extreme weight loss, in which the body seeks to conserve energy by reducing [metabolic rate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metabolic_rate) and/or non-resting energy expenditure to prolong survival and preserve [body fat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Body_fat) and [lean mass](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lean_mass).

stay apparatus is an arrangement of muscles, tendons, and ligaments that work together so that an animal can remain standing with virtually no muscular effort.

Stazione Zoologica Anton Dohrn is a [research institute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Research_institute) in [Naples](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naples), [Italy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italy), devoted to basic research in biology.

steady state topography (SST) is a methodology for observing and measuring [human brain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_brain) activity that was first described by Richard Silberstein and co-workers in 1990.
steady-state visually evoked potential (SSVEP) is an electrophysiological response that is phase-locked to a periodic visual stimulus.

Steatopygia is the state of having substantial levels of tissue on the [buttocks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buttocks) and thighs leading to a protruding 90-degree angled appearance and accompanied by [lordosis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lordosis).

stele (also called vascular stele or vascular cylinder) is the central part of the [root](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Root) or [stem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plant_stem) containing the tissues derived from the procambium.

stellar birthline is a predicted line on the [Hertzsprung–Russell diagram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hertzsprung–Russell_diagram) that relates the [effective temperature](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Effective_temperature) and [luminosity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luminosity) of [pre-main-sequence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pre-main-sequence) stars at the start of their contraction.

Stellar chemistry is the study of the [chemical composition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chemical_composition) of [star](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Star)s and the physical and chemical processes that govern how elements are formed, transported, and observed in stellar environments.

media.file: Echelle Spectra of the Carbon Star UU Aurigae.jpg

definition: Stellar evolution is the process by which a [star](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Star) changes over the course of time.

media.file: Artist’s impression of a vampire star and its victim.jpg

Stellepipona is a small (7 species currently recognized) [Afrotropical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Afrotropical) genus of [potter wasp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Potter_wasp)s.

Stellification is a theoretical process by which a [brown dwarf](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brown_dwarf) [star](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Star) or [Jovian-class planet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jovian_planet) is turned into a star, or by which the [luminosity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luminosity) of dim stars is greatly magnified.

stem cells are [undifferentiated](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cellular_differentiation) or partially differentiated [cells](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_(biology)) that can change into various [types of cells](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Types_of_cells) and [proliferate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_proliferation) indefinitely to produce more of the same stem cell.

Stem cell chip is a device that detects given biochemical changes in [stem cells](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stem_cells), for example changes in [RNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RNA) expression.

Stem Cell Research is a [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer-reviewed) [open-access](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Open-access) [scientific journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_journal) covering research on [stem cell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stem_cell)s.

stem cell theory of aging postulates that the [aging process](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ageing) is the result of the inability of various types of [stem cell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stem_cell)s to continue to replenish the [tissues](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tissue_(biology)) of an [organism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organism) with functional [differentiated cell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Differentiated_cell)s capable of maintaining that tissue's (or [organ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organ_(anatomy))'s) original function.

stemflow is the flow of [intercepted](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interception_(water)) [water](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Water) down the [trunk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trunk_(botany)) or stem of a [plant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plant).

Stenohaline describes an organism, usually [fish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fish), that cannot tolerate a wide fluctuation in the [salinity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salinity) of [water](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Water).

Stenotic nares means the [nares](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nares) (nostrils) are pinched or narrow, making it more difficult for an animal to breathe, and resulting in a lot of open-mouth breathing and panting.

Stentrode (Stent-electrode recording array) is a small [stent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stent)-mounted [electrode array](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electrode_array) permanently [implanted](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brain_implant) into a blood vessel in the brain, without the need for open brain surgery.

stepwise mutation model (SMM) is a [mathematical theory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mathematical_and_theoretical_biology), developed by [Motoo Kimura](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Motoo_Kimura) and [Tomoko Ohta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tomoko_Ohta), that allows for investigation of the equilibrium distribution of [allelic frequencies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Allele_frequency) in a finite population where neutral alleles are produced in step-wise fashion.

Stereom is a [calcium carbonate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcium_carbonate) material that makes up the internal skeletons found in all [echinoderm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Echinoderm)s, both living and fossilized forms.

Stereopsis recovery, also recovery from stereoblindness, is the phenomenon of a [stereoblind](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stereoblind) person gaining partial or full ability of stereo vision ([stereopsis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stereopsis)).

Sterility is the [physiological](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Physiological) inability to effect [sexual reproduction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sexual_reproduction) in a living thing, members of whose kind have been produced sexually.
Sternal foramen (or perforated sternum) is an oval foramen present at lower one-third of the sternum.

rectus sternalis muscle is an [anatomical variation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anatomical_variation) that lies in front of the sternal end of the [pectoralis major](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pectoralis_major_muscle) parallel to the margin of the [sternum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sternum).

sternoclavicular joint or sternoclavicular articulation is a [synovial](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Synovial_joint) [saddle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saddle_joint) [joint](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joint) between the [[sternum#Manubrium|manubrium of the sternum]], and the [clavicle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clavicle_bone), and the first [costal cartilage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Costal_cartilage).

sternocostal joints, also known as sternochondral joints or costosternal articulations, are [synovial](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Synovial_joint) [plane joint](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plane_joint)s of the [costal cartilage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Costal_cartilage)s of the [true ribs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rib) with the [sternum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sternum).

definition: Stichocytes are glandular unicellular cells arranged in a row along the posterior portion of the [oesophagus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oesophagus), each of which communicates by a single pore with the lumen of the oesophagus.

stichosome (from Greek stichos (στίχος) = row; soma (σῶμα) = body) is a multicellular organ that is very prominent in some species of [nematode](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nematode)s and consists of a longitudinal series of glandular unicellular cells ([stichocyte](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stichocyte)s) arranged in a row along the [oesophagus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oesophagus) that forms the posterior esophageal glands.
Sticky mouse is a [murine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/House_mouse) possessing a gene mutation in the enzyme [alanyl-tRNA synthetase](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alanyl-tRNA_synthetase) (AARS).

stifle joint (often simply stifle) is a complex [joint](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joint) in the [hind limb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hind_limb)s of [quadruped](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quadruped) [mammal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mammal)s such as the [sheep](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sheep), [horse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horse) or [dog](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dog).

stinger (or sting) is a sharp [organ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organ_(anatomy)) found in various [animal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Animal)s (typically [insect](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Insect)s and other [arthropod](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthropod)s) capable of injecting [venom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Venom), usually by piercing the [epidermis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Epidermis) of another animal.
stipe () is the stem or stalk-like feature supporting the [cap](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pileus_(mycology)) of a [mushroom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mushroom).

Stizina is a subtribe of small to large-sized sand wasps in the tribe [Bembicini](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bembicini).

stomatogastric ganglion (STG) is a much-studied [ganglion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ganglion) (collection of [neuron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neuron)s) found in [arthropods](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthropods) and studied extensively in [decapod](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Decapoda) [crustacean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crustacean)s.

Stomatogastric Nervous System (STNS) is a commonly studied [neural network](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neural_network) composed of several [ganglia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ganglion) in [arthropod](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthropod)s that controls the motion of the gut and foregut.

stone of madness, also called stone of folly, was a hypothetical stone in a patient's head, thought to be the cause of madness, [idiocy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Idiocy) or [dementia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dementia).

definition: stop codon (or termination codon) is a [codon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetic_code) ([nucleotide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nucleotide) triplet within [messenger RNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Messenger_RNA)) that signals the termination of the [translation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Translation_(biology)) process of the current [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein).

storage effect is a coexistence mechanism proposed in the [ecological theory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ecological_theory) of [species](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Species) coexistence, which tries to explain how such a wide variety of similar species are able to coexist within the same [ecological community](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ecological_community) or [guild](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guild_(ecology)).
storage organ is a part of a plant specifically modified for storage of energy (generally in the form of [carbohydrate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carbohydrate)s) or water.

definition: Strategic Advisory Group of Experts (SAGE) is the principal advisory group to [World Health Organization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Health_Organization) (WHO) for [vaccines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vaccines) and [immunization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Immunization).

Strategic pluralism (also known as the dual-mating strategy) is a theory in [evolutionary psychology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evolutionary_psychology) regarding [human mating strategies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_mating_strategies) that suggests women have evolved to evaluate men in two categories: whether they are reliable long term providers, and whether they contain high quality genes.
stratification refers to the vertical layering of a [habitat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Habitat); the arrangement of [vegetation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vegetation) in layers.

definition: stratum basale (basal layer, sometimes referred to as stratum germinativum) is the deepest layer of the five layers of the [epidermis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Epidermis), the external covering of [skin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skin) in [mammal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mammal)s.

stratum granulosum (or granular layer) is a thin layer of cells in the [epidermis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Epidermis_(skin)) lying above the [stratum spinosum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stratum_spinosum) and below the [stratum corneum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stratum_corneum) ([stratum lucidum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stratum_lucidum) on the soles and palms).

definition: streambed or stream bed is the bottom of a [stream](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stream) or [river](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/River) and is confined within a [channel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stream_channel) or the [banks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bank_(geography)) of the waterway.

Stream ecology is the scientific study of the aquatic species, their interactions with one another, and their connection with the biological, chemical, and physical processes from multiple dimensions within streams.

Stream restoration or river restoration, also sometimes referred to as river reclamation, is work conducted to improve the environmental health of a [river](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/River) or [stream](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stream), in support of [biodiversity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biodiversity), recreation, [flood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flood) management and/or landscape development.

Genomic streamlining is a theory in [evolutionary biology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evolutionary_biology) and [microbial ecology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microbial_ecology) that suggests that there is a reproductive benefit to [prokaryote](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prokaryote)s having a smaller genome size with less [non-coding DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Noncoding_DNA) and fewer non-essential genes.

Strep-tag II is a synthetic [peptide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peptide) consisting of eight [amino acids](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amino_acids) ([Trp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tryptophan)-[Ser](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Serine)-[His](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Histidine)-[Pro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Proline)-[Gln](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gln)-[Phe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phenylalanine)-[Glu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glutamic_acid)-[Lys](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lysine)).

Streptoneury or chiastoneury is a [plesiomorphic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Symplesiomorphy) condition present in all [gastropods](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gastropoda) which is a result of an evolutionary event called [torsion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Torsion_(gastropod)) in which the intestines, heart, [nephridia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nephridium), gills, and nerve cords ==References== [[Category:Gastropod anatomy]] t03323cjkz0ld4lotlgtuhy4jxrtm15

Stress, whether [physiological](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Physiological), [biological](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biological) or [psychological](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Psychological), is an organism's response to a [stressor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stressor), such as an environmental condition or change in life circumstances.

definition: stress ball or hand exercise ball is a malleable toy, usually not more than in diameter.

definition: stress gradient hypothesis (SGH) is an evolutionary theory in [microbial ecology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microbial_ecology) and [community ecology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Community_ecology) that provides a framework to predict when positive or negative interactions should be observed in an habitat.

stress granules are [biomolecular condensate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biomolecular_condensate)s in the [cytosol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cytosol) composed of [proteins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Proteins) and [RNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RNA) that assemble into 0.1–2 μm [membraneless organelles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Membraneless_organelles) when the [cell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_(biology)) is under [stress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stress_(biology)).

related: Epigenetics of anxiety and stress–related disorders

definition: stressor is a chemical or [biological agent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biological_agent), [environmental](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Environment_(biophysical)) condition, [external stimulus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stimulus_(physiology)) or an event seen as causing [stress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stress_(biology)) to an [organism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biological_organism).

stretch-shortening cycle (SSC) is a natural muscle function in which there is a rapid transitioning from an [eccentric contraction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eccentric_contraction) (lengthening under load) to a [concentric contraction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Concentric_contraction) (shortening) of the same muscle, storing elastic energy during the stretch and releasing it during the shortening.

Strib porpoise research station was a [bioacoustic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bioacoustics) research facility located in [Strib](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Strib), a small town on the coast of [Little Belt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Little_Belt), [Denmark](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denmark).

string bog or string mire is a [bog](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bog) consisting of slightly elevated ridges and islands, with woody plants, alternating with flat, wet [sedge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sedge) mat areas.
stroke volume (SV) is the volume of [blood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blood) pumped from the [ventricle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ventricle_(heart)) per beat.
Stroma () is the part of a [tissue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tissue_(biology)) or [organ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organ_(anatomy)) with a structural or connective role.

Stroma, in [botany](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Botany), refers to the colorless fluid surrounding the [thylakoids](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thylakoid) (membrane-bound, sub-organelle compartments) within the [chloroplast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chloroplast).

media.file: Detail of the stromboid notch in Strombidae seashell (Strombus sp.).jpg

definition: stromule is a [microscopic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microscopy) tubular process extending from [plastid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plastid)s in [plant cell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plant_cell)s.

Strong reciprocity is an area of research in [behavioral economics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Behavioral_economics), [evolutionary psychology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evolutionary_psychology), and [evolutionary anthropology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evolutionary_anthropology) on the predisposition to cooperate even when there is no apparent benefit in doing so.
Strophosomia is a severe form of congenital ventral fissure, all abdominal and thoracic viscera being free in the uterus.

definition: Structural information theory (SIT) is a theory about [human perception](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Perception) and in particular about visual perceptual organization, which is a neuro-cognitive process.

definition: [Structural variation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Structural_variation) in the [human genome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_genome) is operationally defined as genomic alterations, varying between individuals, that involve [DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA) segments larger than 1 kilo base (kb), and could be either [microscopic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microscopic) or submicroscopic.

definition: Macromolecular structure validation is the process of evaluating reliability for 3-dimensional atomic models of large biological molecules such as [proteins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Proteins) and [nucleic acids](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nucleic_acids).

Structure-based combinatorial protein engineering (SCOPE) is a [synthetic biology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Synthetic_biology) technique for creating [gene libraries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene_library) ([lineages](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lineage_(evolution))) of defined composition designed from structural and probabilistic constraints of the encoded proteins.
Structured Digital Abstract (SDA) is a method of describing relationships between biological entities in a structured, but human-readable, format.
Strudiella devonica is a species of extinct arthropod from the [Devonian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devonian).

definition: Studies in History of Biology was an annual publication edited by [William Coleman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Coleman_(historian)) and [Camille Limoges](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Camille_Limoges) and published by Johns Hopkins University Press, Baltimore MD, in seven volumes from 1977 to 1984.

Stultification (from Latin stultus stupid) refers to the state of being or a situation or an action causing one to become * [stupid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stupidity) or * [foolish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foolishness) or * [unsound](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unsound_mind) The silent implication of stultification in neurobiological terms is that certain external influences can have a lasting neural effect (reduction of the number of synapses, reduced number of interconnections between brain areas, less efficient signal transmission, etc).
sturt is a measure of distance.
stylet is a hard, sharp, anatomical structure found in some [invertebrate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Invertebrate)s.

stylophthalmine trait is an adaptation present in the [larvae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fish_larva) of several different species of [actinopterygian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Actinopterygian) fish.

Su-In Lee (; born 1979) is a South Korean and American computer scientist known for her research on [explainable artificial intelligence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Explainable_artificial_intelligence) and its applications in [biomedical research](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biomedical_research).

definition: subarctic climate (also called subpolar climate, or boreal climate) is a [continental climate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Continental_climate) with long, cold (often very cold) winters, and short, warm to cool summers.

definition: Subareolar lymphatic plexus, also known as Sappey's plexus is the lymphatic drainage of the areola of the breast.
subclade is a subgroup of a [haplogroup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haplogroup).
subcloning is a technique used to move a particular DNA sequence from a parent [vector](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vector_(molecular_biology)) to a destination vector.
subcoracoid bursa or subcoracoid bursa of Collas is a [synovial bursa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Synovial_bursa) located in the [shoulder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shoulder).

SynbiCITE is the UK's national Innovation and Knowledge Centre (IKC) for the adoption and use of [synthetic biology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Synthetic_biology) by industry.
Synchronous coefficient of drag alteration (SCODA) is a [biotechnology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biotechnology) method for purifying, separating and/or concentrating bio-molecules.

synchronous or synchronized culture is a [microbiological culture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microbiological_culture) or a [cell culture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_culture) that contains [cell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_(biology))s that are all in the same [growth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_growth) stage.
Synergy is the concept that a combined effect of two or more entities is greater than the sum of their individual effects.

Syngameon refers to groups of [taxa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taxa) that frequently engage in natural [hybridization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybrid_(biology)) and lack strong [reproductive barrier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reproductive_barrier)s that prevent interbreeding.

SYNGAP1-related intellectual disability is a [monogenetic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Single-gene_disorder) developmental and epileptic [encephalopathy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Encephalopathy) that affects the [central nervous system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_nervous_system).

Syngenetic permafrost growth is a mode of the growth of [permafrost](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Permafrost) whereby additional material is deposited to a permafrost site during freezing conditions, causing the permafrost layer to build upwards.
Synaptogyrin-1 is a [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) that in humans is encoded by the SYNGR1 [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).
synonym is one of two or more [scientific names](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_names) that apply to the same [taxon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taxon).

Synopeas myles is a [platygastrid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Platygastridae) parasitoid of [Contarinia nasturtii](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Contarinia_nasturtii), that, like its host, is native to Europe.
synovial sheath is one of the two membranes of a [tendon sheath](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tendon_sheath) which covers a tendon.

Syntelic attachment occurs when both sister [chromosome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chromosome)s are attached to a single [spindle pole](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spindle_pole).

Syntelog: a special case of [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene) [homology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Homology_(biology)) where sets of genes are derived from the same [ancestral](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Common_descent) genomic region.
Synthesis-dependent strand [[Annealing (biology)#Annealing|annealing]] (SDSA) is a major mechanism of homology-directed repair of DNA [[DNA repair#Double-strand breaks|double-strand breaks]] (DSBs).

Synthetic biology (SynBio) is a multidisciplinary [scientific field](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_field) that applies the principles of [engineering](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Engineering) to develop new biological parts, devices, and systems or to redesign existing systems found in nature.

definition: Synthetic ecosystems are [on-chip integrated devices](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/System-on-a-chip) where cellular cultures (individuals) and [ecosystem services](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ecosystem_services) - such as the renewal of growth, delivery of regulatory signals as well as removal of waste - are patterned into an integrated [fluidic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fluidic) device using principles of [landscape ecology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Landscape_ecology), [physiology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Physiology) and [cell signaling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_signaling).

Synthetic genetic array analysis (SGA) is a [high-throughput](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/High-throughput_screening) technique for exploring [synthetic lethal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Synthetic_lethality) and synthetic sick [genetic interactions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetic_interactions) ([SSL](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Synthetic_lethality)).

Synthetic genomics is a nascent field of [synthetic biology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Synthetic_biology) that uses aspects of [genetic modification](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetic_modification) on pre-existing life forms, or [artificial gene synthesis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artificial_gene_synthesis) to create new DNA or entire lifeforms.
Synthetic immunology is the rational design and construction of synthetic systems that perform complex immunological functions.

Synthetic intelligence (SI) is an alternative/opposite term for [artificial intelligence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artificial_intelligence) emphasizing that the [intelligence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intelligence) of machines need not be an imitation or in any way artificial; it can be a genuine form of intelligence.

Synthetic ion channels are de novo chemical compounds that insert into [lipid bilayer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lipid_bilayer)s, form pores, and allow [ion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ion)s to flow from one side to the other.
Synthetic lethality is defined as a type of genetic interaction where the combination of two genetic events results in cell death or death of an organism.

Synthetic morphology is a sub-discipline of the broader field of [synthetic biology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Synthetic_biology).

Synthetic organelles, also known as artificial organelles, are artificial compartments designed to mimic the functions of these natural [organelles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organelle), enabling controlled [biochemical reactions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biochemical_reaction) within living cells.
Synthetic ribosomes are artificial small-molecules that can synthesize peptides in a sequence-specific matter.

synthetic vaccine is a [vaccine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vaccine) consisting mainly of synthetic [peptides](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peptides), [carbohydrate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carbohydrate)s, or [antigen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigen)s.
Synthetic virology is a branch of [virology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virology) engaged in the study and engineering of synthetic man-made [virus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virus)es.

Synusia (plural Synusiae) is a term in plant [ecology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ecology) that refers to a layer of vegetation consisting of species with shared [life forms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raunkiær_plant_life-form).

Systematic Botany is a [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer_review) [scientific journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_journal) covering the study of [systematic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Systematics) [botany](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Botany).

Systems Biology Ontology (SBO) is a set of controlled, relational vocabularies of terms commonly used in [systems biology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Systems_biology), and in particular in computational modeling.

Systems immunology is a research field under [systems biology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Systems_biology) that uses [mathematical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mathematical) approaches and [computational](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computational) methods to examine the interactions within cellular and [molecular networks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biological_network) of the [immune system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Immune_system).

Systems neuroscience is a subdiscipline of [neuroscience](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neuroscience) and [systems biology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Systems_biology) that studies the structure and function of various neural circuits and systems that make up the central nervous system of an organism.

Toponomics is a discipline in [systems biology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Systems_biology), [molecular cell biology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_biology), and [histology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Histology) concerning the study of the [toponome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toponome) of organisms.

definition: Trans-Spliced Exon Coupled RNA End Determination (TEC-RED) is a [transcriptomic technique](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transcriptomics_technologies) that, like [SAGE](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Serial_analysis_of_gene_expression), allows for the digital detection of messenger RNA sequences.

transactivation is the increased rate of [gene expression](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene_expression) triggered either by biological processes or by artificial means, through the expression of an intermediate transactivator protein.

transcendence is the aspect of existence that is completely independent of the material [universe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universe), beyond all known [physical law](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Physical_law)s.

Transcendental anatomy, also known as philosophical anatomy, was a form of [comparative anatomy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comparative_anatomy) that sought to find ideal patterns and structures common to all organisms in nature.

Transcription is the process of duplicating a segment of [DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA) into [RNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RNA) for the purpose of [gene expression](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene_expression).
Transcription activator-like effector nucleases (TALEN) are [restriction enzyme](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Restriction_enzyme)s that can be engineered to cut specific sequences of DNA.

transcription bubble is a molecular structure formed during the initialization of DNA [transcription](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transcription_(genetics)), when a limited portion of the [DNA double helix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA_double_helix) is unwound, providing enough space for [RNA polymerase](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RNA_polymerase) (RNAP) to bind to the template strand and begin [RNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RNA) synthesis.

transcription factor (TF) (or sequence-specific DNA-binding factor) is a [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) that controls the rate of [transcription](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transcription_(biology)) of [genetic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetics) information from [DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA) to [messenger RNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Messenger_RNA), by binding to [DNA sequences](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA_sequence).

Transcription factor II B (TFIIB) is a [general transcription factor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/General_transcription_factor) that is involved in the formation of the [RNA polymerase II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RNA_polymerase_II) [preinitiation complex](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transcription_preinitiation_complex) (PIC) This is thought to affect transcription in these diseases as it reduces the availability of TFIIB to other promoters in the [brain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brain) as the TFIIB is instead interacting with the expanded polyglutamine tracts.

Transcription-translation feedback loop (TTFL) is a [cellular model](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cellular_model) for explaining [circadian rhythm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Circadian_rhythm)s in behavior and [physiology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Physiology).

transcriptional amplification is the process in which the total amount of [messenger RNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Messenger_RNA) (mRNA) molecules from expressed genes is increased during disease, [development](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Developmental_biology), or in response to stimuli.

Transcriptome-wide association study (TWAS) is a genetic methodology that can be used to compare the genetic components of [gene expression](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene_expression) and the genetic components of a trait to determine if an association is present between the two components.

Transcriptomics technologies are the techniques used to study an organism's [transcriptome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transcriptome), the sum of all of its [RNA transcripts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RNA).

transcriptor is a [transistor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transistor)-like device composed of [DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA) and [RNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RNA) rather than a [semiconducting material](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Semiconducting_material) such as [silicon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Silicon).

Transdetermination is a concept in [developmental biology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Developmental_biology) to describe the process by which [pluripotent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_potency) stem cells change their [fate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cellular_differentiation) from becoming one kind of specialized cell lineage to a different lineage.
transduction is the translation of arriving stimulus into an action potential by a sensory receptor.

Transduction is the process by which foreign [DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA) is introduced into a cell by a [virus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virus) or [viral vector](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Viral_vector).

Transepidermal water loss (TEWL or TWL) is the loss of [water](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Water) that passes from inside a body ([animal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Animal) or [plant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plant)) through the epidermis (that is, either the [epidermal layer of animal skin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Epidermis) or the [epidermal layer of plants](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Epidermis_(botany))) to the surrounding [atmosphere](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atmosphere) via [diffusion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diffusion) and [evaporation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evaporation) processes.

Transepithelial potential difference (TEPD) is the [voltage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Voltage) across an [epithelium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Epithelium), and is the sum of the [membrane potential](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Membrane_potential)s for the outer and inner [cell membrane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_membrane)s.

Transfection is the process of deliberately introducing naked or purified [nucleic acids](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nucleic_acids) into [eukaryotic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eukaryote) [cells](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_(biology)).
transfer DNA (T-DNA) binary system is a pair of [plasmids](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plasmids) consisting of a T-DNA binary vector and a vir helper plasmid.

Transfersome is a proprietary [drug delivery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drug_delivery) technology, an artificial [vesicle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vesicle_(biology_and_chemistry)) designed to exhibit the characteristics of a [cell vesicle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vesicle_(biology)) suitable for controlled and potentially [targeted drug delivery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Targeted_drug_delivery).

Transflammation describes the process by which [innate immune response](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Innate_immune_response) mechanisms affect the [epigenetic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Epigenetics) plasticity of a cell during nuclear reprogramming.

Transformation efficiency refers to the ability of a cell to take up and incorporate exogenous DNA, such as [plasmid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plasmid)s, during a process called [transformation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformation_(genetics)).

Transformed cladistics, also known as pattern cladistics is an epistemological approach to the [cladistic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cladistic) method of phylogenetic inference and classification that makes no a priori assumptions about [common ancestry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Common_ancestry).

Transgenic Research, international in scope, is a bimonthly, [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer_review), [scientific journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_journal), published by [Springer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Springer_Science+Business_Media).

transgressive segregation is the formation of extreme [phenotypes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phenotype), or transgressive phenotypes, observed in segregated [hybrid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybrid_(biology)) populations compared to phenotypes observed in the parental lines.
transheterozygote is used in modern genetics periodicals in two different ways.

Transient receptor potential channels (TRP channels) are a group of [ion channel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ion_channel)s located mostly on the [plasma membrane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plasma_membrane) of numerous animal cell types.
