definition: transitional fossil is any [fossil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fossil)ized remains of a life form that exhibits traits common to both an ancestral group and its derived descendant group.

Translation is the process in [biological cells](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_(biology)) in which [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein)s are produced using [RNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RNA) molecules as templates.

definition: translational efficiency or translation efficiency is the rate of [mRNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MRNA) [translation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Translation_(biology)) into [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein)s within [cell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_(biology))s.

Translational neuroscience is the field of study which applies [neuroscience](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neuroscience) research to translate or develop into clinical applications and novel therapies for [nervous system disorders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nervous_system_disease).
Transmembrane channels, also called [membrane channels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Membrane_channels), are pores within a [lipid bilayer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lipid_bilayer).

transmission disequilibrium test (TDT) was proposed by Spielman, McGinnis and [Ewens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warren_Ewens) (1993) is the number of PQ children from parents with the PQ and QQ types.

Transmission electron microscopy DNA sequencing is a single-molecule [sequencing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA_sequencing) technology that uses [transmission electron microscopy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transmission_electron_microscopy) techniques.

Transmutation of species and transformism are 18th and early 19th-century ideas about the change of one [species](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Species) into another that preceded [Charles Darwin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_Darwin)'s theory of evolution through [natural selection](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Natural_selection).

Transpiration is the process of [water](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Water) movement through a [plant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plant) and its [evaporation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evaporation) from aerial parts, such as [leaves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leaf), [stems](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plant_stem) and [flower](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flower)s.

definition: Transpirational cooling is the cooling provided as plants [transpire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transpiration) water.

transplant experiment, or common garden experiment, is an [experiment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Experiment) to test the effect of [environment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Environment_(biophysical)) by moving two species from their native environments into a common environment.

transposable element (TE), also known as transposons, jumping gene, or [mobile genetic element](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mobile_genetic_element), are DNA sequences that can change their position, or translocate, within a genome.

definition: transposase is any of a class of [enzyme](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enzyme)s capable of binding to the end of a [transposon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transposon) and catalysing its movement to another part of a [genome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genome), typically by a cut-and-paste mechanism or a replicative mechanism, in a process known as transposition.

Transposon mutagenesis, or transposition mutagenesis, is a [biological](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biological) process that allows genes to be transferred to a host organism's [chromosome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chromosome), interrupting or modifying the function of an [[wikt:extant|extant]] [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene) on the chromosome and causing [mutation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mutation).
transposon tagging is a process where [transposon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transposon)s (transposable elements) are amplified inside a biological cell by a tagging technique.

Transpulmonary pressure is the difference between the [alveolar pressure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alveolar_pressure) and the [intrapleural pressure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intrapleural_pressure) in the [pleural cavity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pleural_cavity).

transrepression is a process whereby one [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) represses (i.e., inhibits) the activity of a second protein through a [protein-protein interaction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein-protein_interaction).

Transterm is a database of [mRNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MRNA) sequences, [codon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Codon) usage, and associated [cis-regulatory element](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cis-regulatory_element)s that regulate [gene expression](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene_expression).

Transudate is [extravascular](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Extravascular) fluid with low [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) content and a low [specific gravity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Specific_gravity) ( or a [Rivalta test](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rivalta_test) can be used to distinguish transudate from [exudate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Exudate).

transumbilical plane or umbilical plane, one of the [transverse plane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transverse_plane)s in human anatomy, is a horizontal line that passes through the abdomen at the level of the [navel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navel) (or umbilicus).
transverse plane is a plane that is rotated 90° from two other planes.
trap crop is a plant that attracts agricultural pests, usually insects, away from nearby harvested crops.

Traube's (semilunar) space is an [anatomic space](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spatium) of some clinical importance.
Traçadal Biological Reserve () is a [biological reserve](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biological_reserve_(Brazil)) in the state of [Rondônia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rondônia), Brazil.

Tre recombinase is an experimental [enzyme](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enzyme) that in lab tests has removed [DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA) inserted by [HIV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HIV) from infected cells.

treadmilling is a phenomenon observed within [protein filament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein_filament)s of the [cytoskeleton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cytoskeleton)s of many [cell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_(biology))s, especially in [actin filament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Actin_filament)s and [microtubules](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microtubules).

Treaty of Bucharest (; ; ; ) was concluded on 10 August 1913, by the delegates of [Bulgaria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingdom_of_Bulgaria), [Romania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingdom_of_Romania), [Serbia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingdom_of_Serbia), [Montenegro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingdom_of_Montenegro) and [Greece](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingdom_of_Greece).

Treaty of Craiova (; ) was signed on 7 September 1940 and ratified on 13 September 1940 by the [Kingdom of Bulgaria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingdom_of_Bulgaria) and the [Kingdom of Romania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingdom_of_Romania).
Tree breeding is the application of genetic, reproductive biology and economics principles to the genetic improvement and management of forest trees.

definition: tree line is the edge of a [habitat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Habitat) at which [tree](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tree)s can grow and beyond which they cannot.

tree of life or universal tree of life is a [metaphor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metaphor), [conceptual model](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conceptual_model), and research tool used to explore the [evolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evolution) of life and describe the relationships between [organism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organism)s, both living and extinct, as described in a famous passage in [Charles Darwin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_Darwin)'s [On the Origin of Species](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/On_the_Origin_of_Species) (1859).

Tree of Life Web Project (ToL) is an [Internet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Internet) project providing information about the [diversity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biodiversity) and [phylogeny](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phylogeny) of [life](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Life) on [Earth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Earth).

tree stump is the remaining portion of a [tree](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tree) [trunk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trunk_(botany)) and its [root](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Root)s that remain after a tree has been [felled](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tree_felling) or has naturally fallen.
Uprooting is a form of treefall in which the root plate of a tree is torn from the soil, disrupting and mixing it and leaving a [pit-mound](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pit-and-mound_topography).

treefall gap is a distinguishable hole in the [canopy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canopy_(biology)) of a [forest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forest) with vertical sides extending through all levels down to an average height of above ground.

The trematode mitochondrial code (translation table 21) is a [genetic code](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetic_code) found in the [mitochondria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mitochondria) of [Trematoda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trematoda).

triradiate pelvic girdle is a [shared feature](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apomorphy) common to [archosaur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Archosaur)s.

Trophic mutualism is a key type of ecological [mutualism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mutualism_(biology)).

Trophic species are a scientific grouping of organisms according to their shared [trophic (feeding) positions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trophic_level) in a [food web](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Food_web) or [food chain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Food_chain).

Trophobiosis is a [symbiotic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Symbiosis) association between [organism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organism)s where food is obtained or provided.
trophoblast (from [Greek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greek_language) : to feed; and : germinator) is the outer layer of cells of the [blastocyst](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blastocyst).

upper [limb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Limb_(anatomy))s or upper extremities are the [forelimb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forelimb)s of an [upright-postured](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Upright_posture) [tetrapod](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tetrapod) [vertebrate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vertebrate), extending from the [scapula](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scapula)e and [clavicle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clavicle)s down to and including the [digit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digit_(anatomy))s, including all the [musculature](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Musculature)s and [ligament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ligament)s involved with the [shoulder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shoulder), [elbow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elbow), [wrist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wrist) and [knuckle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Knuckle) joints.

definition: upstream activating sequence or upstream activation sequence (UAS) is a [cis-acting regulatory sequence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cis-regulatory_element) found in [yeast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yeast) like [Saccharomyces cerevisiae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saccharomyces_cerevisiae).

upstream [signaling pathway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Signaling_pathway) is triggered by the binding of a signaling molecule, a [ligand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ligand), to a receiving molecule, a [receptor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Receptor_(biochemistry)).

upstream open reading frame (uORF) is an [open reading frame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Open_reading_frame) (ORF) within the [5' untranslated region](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/5'_untranslated_region) (5'UTR) of an [mRNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MRNA).
Urban ecology is the scientific study of the relation of living organisms with each other and their surroundings in an [urban environment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urban_environment).
urban ecosystems are considered an ecosystem functional group within the [intensive land-use biome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthropogenic_biome).
Urban evolution refers to the heritable genetic changes of populations in response to urban development and anthropogenic activities in [urban area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urban_area)s.

Urban metabolism (UM) is a [model](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_modelling) to facilitate the description and analysis of the [flows of the materials](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Material_flow) and [energy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Energy_transfer) within [cities](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cities), such as undertaken in a [material flow analysis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Material_flow_analysis) of a city.

urban wild is a remnant of a natural [ecosystem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ecosystem) found in the midst of an otherwise highly developed [urban area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urban_area).
urea transporter is a [membrane transport protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Membrane_transport_protein), transporting [urea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urea).

definition: Van der Hoeven's organ is the infrabuccal lamellar organ in the adult male of genus [Nautilus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nautilus).

Van der Vecht's gland or Van der Vecht's organ is a [gland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gland) which is located in an area of modified [cuticle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cuticle_(insect_anatomy)) on the rearmost gastral [sternite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sternite) of female wasps.
Van Veen grab sampler is an instrument to sample [sediment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sediment) in water environments.

Vanessa Miranville (born 26 July 1983) is a French politician who has held office as the mayor of [La Possession](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Possession) in [Réunion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Réunion) since 2014.
variability hypothesis, also known as the greater male variability hypothesis, is the hypothesis that human males generally display greater variability in traits than human females do.

Variant Call Format or VCF is a standard text file format used in [bioinformatics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bioinformatics) for storing [gene sequence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene_sequence) or [DNA sequence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA_sequence) variations.
variation potential (VP) (also called slow wave potential) is a hydraulically propagating electrical signal occurring exclusively in [plant cell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plant_cell)s.
variational properties of an organism are those properties relating to the production of variation among its offspring.

Variegation is the appearance of differently coloured zones in the [foliage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leaf), [flowers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flower), and sometimes the [stems](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plant_stem) and [fruit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fruit) of [plants](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plant), granting a speckled, striped, or patchy appearance.

variome is the whole set of [genetic variation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetic_variation)s found in populations of [species](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Species) that have gone through a relatively short [evolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evolution) change.

varix (: varices) is an anatomical feature of the [shell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gastropod_shell) of certain [sea snail](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sea_snail)s, [marine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marine_(ocean)) [gastropod](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gastropod) [mollusc](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mollusc)s.

Varroa sensitive hygiene (VSH) is a behavioral trait of [honey bee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honey_bee)s (Apis mellifera) in which bees detect and remove bee [pupa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pupa)e that are infested by the [parasitic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parasite) [mite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mite) [Varroa destructor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Varroa_destructor).

definition: vasa recta of the kidney, (vasa recta renis) are capillaries of the [kidney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kidney), – a series of [blood vessel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blood_vessel)s in the [blood supply of the kidney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Renal_circulation) that enter the [medulla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Renal_medulla) as the straight arterioles, and leave the medulla to ascend to the cortex as the straight venules.

vascular cambium is the main growth [tissue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tissue_(biology)) in the [stem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plant_stem)s and [root](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Root)s of many plants exhibiting [secondary growth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secondary_growth), specifically in [dicot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dicot)s such as [buttercups](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buttercups) and [oak trees](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oak_trees), [gymnosperm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gymnosperm)s such as [pine trees](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pine_trees), as well as in certain other [vascular plant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vascular_plant)s.
Vascular recruitment is the increase in the number of perfused [capillaries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Capillaries) in response to a stimulus.

Vascular resistance is the resistance that must be overcome for [blood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blood) to flow through the [circulatory system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Circulatory_system).

Vascular tissue is a complex transporting [tissue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tissue_(biology)), formed of more than one cell type, found in [vascular plant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vascular_plant)s.

Vascularity, in [bodybuilding](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bodybuilding), is the condition of having many highly visible, prominent, and often extensively-ramified [superficial vein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Superficial_vein)s.

vasculum or a botanical box is a stiff container used by [botanist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Botanist)s to keep field [sample](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sample_(material))s viable for transportation.

Vasodilation, also known as vasorelaxation, is the widening of [blood vessel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blood_vessel)s.

Vasopressin receptor 1A (V1AR), or arginine vasopressin receptor 1A (officially called AVPR1A) is one of the three major [receptor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Receptor_(biochemistry)) types for [vasopressin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vasopressin) ([AVPR1B](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arginine_vasopressin_receptor_1B) and [AVPR2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arginine_vasopressin_receptor_2) being the others), and is present throughout the [brain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brain), as well as in the periphery in the [liver](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liver), [kidney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kidney), and [vasculature](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Circulatory_system).

veil or velum, in mycology, is one of several structures in [fungi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fungi), especially the thin [membrane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Membrane_(selective_barrier)) that covers the cap and stalk of an immature [mushroom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mushroom).

veliger is the [plankton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plankton)ic [larva](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Larva) of many kinds of [sea snails](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sea_snails) and [freshwater snails](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Freshwater_snails), as well as most [bivalve](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bivalve) [mollusc](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mollusc)s (clams) and [tusk shell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tusk_shell)s.

venous heart is a type of [heart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heart) in which only blood with [carbon dioxide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carbon_dioxide) circulates.
Venous return is the rate of blood flow back to the heart.

ventilation/perfusion ratio (V/Q ratio) is a [ratio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ratio) used to assess the efficiency and adequacy of the [ventilation-perfusion coupling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ventilation-perfusion_coupling) and thus the matching of two variables: * V – [ventilation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ventilation_(physiology)) – the [air](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air) that reaches the [alveoli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pulmonary_alveolus) * Q – [perfusion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Perfusion) – the [blood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blood) that reaches the alveoli via the capillaries The V/Q ratio can therefore be defined as the ratio of the amount of air reaching the alveoli per minute to the amount of blood reaching the alveoli per minute—a ratio of [volumetric flow rate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volumetric_flow_rate)s.

Ventilation–perfusion coupling is the relationship between [ventilation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Breathing) and [perfusion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Perfusion) in the [respiratory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Respiratory_system) and [cardiovascular systems](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardiovascular_system).
